result.family: FAMILY 5 — MEASUREMENT-PROTOCOL CORRESPONDENCE (does the simulator reproduce the experimental PROTOCOL, or only compute a superficially similar number?)

instruments.name: Virtual AFM = whole-cell parallel-plate compression
instruments.what_its_name_implies: AFM indentation of a cell, comparable to Zbiral 2023 MCF7 E=249 Pa measured with a 10 um-DIAMETER colloidal bead on adherent cells.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The reaction of a FREE, UNADHERED sphere squeezed symmetrically between TWO plates that each advance to R0*(1-strain). Both poles are constrained; there is no substrate, no adhesion, no finite cell height, no one-sided indenter, and no bottom-effect (Dimitriadis/Garcia) correction. Only the TOP plate's penetration is summed into reaction[0]; the bottom plate contributes force to nodes but nothing to the reading.
instruments.evidence: plate_kernel docstring calls itself "the virtual-AFM / Fischer-Friedrich parallel-plate compression" — Fischer-Friedrich is a SUSPENDED-cell wedged-cantilever protocol, Zbiral is a BEAD-on-ADHERENT-cell protocol; the code compares to Zbiral. FF_AFM_FULLCOMPARTMENT_2026-07-07.md reports V/V0 falling to 0.901 and dP reaching 84,750 Pa at 25% strain — a whole-cell undrained volumetric squeeze of an area-inextensible shell (reshape fixes segment length, the cortex has no area-elastic term), which is not the local, volume-preserving deformation a bead indent produces. ff_bulge_probe.py exists precisely because the cortex under-bulges (+4.9% vs +17.0% constant-volume, FF_RESULTS_LOG.md:93).
instruments.canonical_replacement: One-sided rigid spherical indenter of the EXPERIMENT'S radius pressed into an ADHERENT cell resting on the substrate plane (ff_cell_on_substrate.py already builds that cell), with the cell's finite height recorded and a bottom-effect correction applied to the inverted E exactly as the source paper's analysis does — or, if the two-plate geometry is kept, re-anchor the target to a suspended-cell parallel-plate datum instead of Zbiral.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Run the same indentation twice, once with the bottom plate replaced by a free surface (one-sided). If the geometry were protocol-faithful the inverted E would be unchanged; here it must change by O(1) because the symmetric constraint is what generates the volumetric pressure that dominates the force.

instruments.name: Hertz-inversion harness E_fit (the AFM modulus number)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The apparent Young's modulus an AFM operator would extract, with press-speed dependence swept (mode=ratesweep).
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A STEP-strain response read at a fixed, non-converged 1600 iterations. The rate sweep never passes v_press_um_s, so the mechanical loading history is INSTANTANEOUS at step 0 while load_time_s (=2*R0*strain/v) is fed only to the drainage and crosslink-turnover clocks. So "E vs loading rate" is a step-strain solve with rescaled chemical clocks, not a ramp.
instruments.evidence: run() at :75-78 passes strain, n_steps, Lp, K_drained, load_time_s, xl_koff — and NOT v_press_um_s; network_warp.py:882 states "v_press_um_s=None -> instant strain applied at step 0 (legacy quasi-static)". FF_RESULTS_LOG.md:229-238 shows n_steps 1600->3200->6400->12800 gives E = 4127 -> 262 -> 20 -> 19 Pa, i.e. the file's own default (1600) is the retracted under-relaxed setting: running `python -m ffn_sim.scripts.ff_hertz_validation` today still reproduces the withdrawn 16.5x. Two different load-time conventions coexist: the harness uses 2*R0*s/v (:73) while the kernel ramp uses R0*strain/v (network_warp.py:892) — a factor-2 in the single most influential protocol parameter.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Drive the mechanics with v_press_um_s at the source paper's approach speed, to the source paper's maximum indentation, and read F at the same point of the curve the operator reads (ramp end, or after the paper's dwell) — then attach a relaxation certificate E(2N)/E(N) to every reported E.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Double n_steps and require |E(2N)/E(N) - 1| < 0.05. The harness's existing validity gate is E_pt "flatness" across strain (:89), which PASSED on the retracted 4127 Pa result (FF_RESULTS_LOG.md:163 marks it "flat E_pt (Hertzian) OK") — a gate structurally blind to its own dominant failure mode, because a uniformly under-relaxed run is uniformly wrong and therefore flat.

instruments.name: Indentation depth delta1 = R0_mean * strain
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The contact indentation depth the AFM operator uses after cantilever-deflection correction and contact-point detection.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The NOMINAL plate travel measured from the cortex's MEAN radius, on a rough shell whose outermost nodes contact first, against a COMPLIANT penalty plate that the nodes penetrate. None of the three real corrections (contact-point determination, cantilever compliance, indenter-vs-sample deflection split) is performed.
instruments.evidence: delta1 = R0*s with s in {0.02,0.025,0.03} gives delta1 = 0.15-0.23 um. k_plate is a penalty spring (network_warp.py:852-853), so real penetration is nonzero and the true contact depth differs from the nominal. Because E ~ delta^-1.5, a 0.1 um contact-point error at delta1=0.15 um is a 3-5x error in E — the largest single silent-error channel in this instrument, and there is no contact-point estimator anywhere.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Define delta from the FIRST-CONTACT node radius (or from a fitted F-delta contact point, as AFM software does), and use the rigid_plate path so penetration is exactly zero; report the contact-point sensitivity dE/E = -1.5 * ddelta/delta alongside E.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Re-invert the same F-vs-plate-position data with the contact reference set to R0_mean, R0_max and R0_percentile95. E_fit must agree within the quoted uncertainty; if it moves several-fold, the number is a contact-point artifact, not a modulus.

instruments.name: Press-speed / viscous-elastic split and the eta_eff "calibration"
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The per-node drag validated against the analytic Newtonian ground truth eta = 65.9 Pa*s, licensing the headline that the model "passes THROUGH the MCF7 band at ~0.5-1 um/s".
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A whole-cell TRANSLATIONAL Stokes drag (6*pi*eta*R) smeared over all cortex nodes, then divided by an invented squeeze-flow geometry factor (Hertz contact area x nominal strain rate v/2R0). The resulting eta_eff = 124-141 Pa*s is declared "validated to ~2x of the 65.9 target" — the factor 2 is the arbitrary geometry factor, not a measurement.
instruments.evidence: FF_RESULTS_LOG.md:281-296. The whole chain was run at NF = 1500 filaments (ff_drag_calibration.py:12,17) and 2000 (ff_hertz_validation.py:57, ff_press_speed_probe.py:14), against a mandatory native population of 70,686 / 494,802 nodes — and the elastic branch is precisely the density-bound gamma-floor, so the elastic/viscous partition that decides "in band" is exactly the quantity that cannot be read at 1500 filaments. Separately: the experiment fixes v = 5 um/s (model 9.3x); the model reaches 0.9x only at 0.5 um/s, i.e. the protocol parameter the experiment PINS is being used as the free knob that lands the band.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Invert the drag law's OWN analytic prediction for the imposed plate kinematics (no invented area/strain-rate factor) so the positive control returns eta_eff/eta_input = 1.000 exactly; then report E only at the experiment's stated approach speed, at native population.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Feed eta_bulk_Pa_s = 2*65.9 and require the recovered eta_eff to double exactly (ratio 2.000). Any surviving O(1) offset is in the geometry factor, and the "validated to 2x" claim collapses into what it is: an unmeasured shape constant.

instruments.name: gamma_apparent = 0.5 * dP_turgor * R_eq reported as AFM cortical tension
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The apparent cortical tension an AFM/parallel-plate cortical-tension protocol extracts ("per standard AFM cortical-tension protocol", FF_AFM_FULLCOMPARTMENT_2026-07-07.md).
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The model's own INTERNAL state variable dP_turgor multiplied by half the equatorial radius, using the SPHERE Laplace law (R1 = R2 = R) on a shape that is being deliberately flattened. The experimentalist has no access to dP; the whole point of the protocol is to infer tension from the MEASURABLE force and the imaged shape. Reading an internal pressure back out is not the inversion.
instruments.evidence: The same function computes the protocol-faithful channel dP_from_force = F_plate/(pi*contact_radius^2) (network_warp.py:1417) — the actual Fischer-Friedrich estimator — and a grep shows it is written into metrics at :1439 and :1797 and NEVER read anywhere else in the tree. The reported apparent gamma reaches 319 mN/m at 25% strain (FF_AFM_FULLCOMPARTMENT table), ~1000x any measured cortical tension, because it is tracking a volumetric penalty. Additionally contact_radius is the MAX radial distance of nodes within |(|z|-half_gap)| < 0.15*seg + 0.05 (:1413-1414) — an outlier-driven maximum with a mesh-dependent tolerance, not a fitted contact radius.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Report tension only through the measurable route (F_plate, contact radius, equatorial radius, meridional curvature) using the TWO principal curvature radii, and publish the residual between that and 0.5*dP_turgor*R as the non-equilibrium error rather than suppressing one of the two.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Gate |dP_from_force / dP_turgor - 1| at convergence. Both numbers already exist in the same metrics dict; nobody has ever compared them. If they disagree, at least one of the tension routes is wrong and the disagreement is dimensionless.

instruments.name: method_of_planes_gamma as the "observable comparable to an AFM/Laplace band"
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A surface tension directly comparable to AFM/micropipette cortical-tension bands (Chugh 2017 350-650 pN/um; Hosseini MCF7 180-400 pN/um).
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: mean over orientations of the ABSOLUTE per-plane cut force divided by the great-circle circumference 2*pi*R, over whatever element families the caller passes. Three protocol defects: (1) mean(|gamma_n|) is positively biased — a network with zero mean tension and random element tensions returns gamma > 0, and gamma can never be negative, destroying sign-sense; (2) a diametral plane through the WHOLE cell counts every crossing interior element (nucleus, IF, MT, stress fibers) and divides a 3-D bulk cut force by a 1-D surface circumference; (3) it returns one ISOTROPIC scalar, so it cannot supply the two principal tensions a Laplace inversion on a flattened or adherent cell requires.
instruments.evidence: gamma_estimator.py:103 `return float(np.mean(np.abs(np.asarray(gammas))))`. cortical_tension.py:171 rolls up `tuple(families.keys())` — every family — into gamma_total and labels it AFM-comparable. gamma_estimator.py:41 records the only MCF7 band as "MCF7 interphase SUSPENDED, Hosseini 2020 ... adherent = absent", while PI priority 3 is an ADHERENT cell: the acceptance band for the intended baseline does not exist. gamma_estimator.py:33-42 also builds the comparison target as ACTIVE_FRACTION(0.70) x total band while the same comment states the turgor Laplace partner is "NOT additive - double-book" — the band construction contradicts its own note.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Restrict the cut to cortical elements within the shell thickness and report the two principal cut tensions separately (hoop, meridional) with SIGNED per-orientation values; for the adherent baseline, drop the suspended-cell gamma band as an acceptance gate and use the surface-excess (Kirkwood-Buff) integral of (sigma_tangential - sigma_normal) across the shell.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Randomize the SIGNS of the element tensions (or feed a thermal-noise-only network). A tension estimator must return ~0; mean(|.|) will return a finite positive floor, and that floor is the instrument's bias — which is directly relevant to a project whose headline deficit is a gamma FLOOR.

instruments.name: Traction force microscopy (bead/gel displacement -> traction inversion)
instruments.where: absent; nearest analogues /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/scripts/h7_manifold_traction.py:1-30 (per-patch sum of explicit integrin bond forces) and /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/scripts/ff_clutch_traction.py:50 (sum of clutch stretches)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A traction field comparable to published TFM maps and peak tractions.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The GROUND-TRUTH sum of explicit bond forces, binned onto surface patches. There is no substrate displacement field, no Green's-function/FTTC inversion, no regularization parameter, no bead-density-limited spatial resolution, and no restriction to the in-plane components that 2D TFM actually resolves. Published TFM values are the OUTPUT of a regularized inverse problem that provably smooths and under-estimates peaks; comparing an un-smoothed per-bond sum to them is a systematic, one-directional bias.
instruments.evidence: h7_manifold_traction.py asserts only the contact-conservation identity (sum per-patch force == sum per-bond force) — an internal bookkeeping check, not a protocol. It also imports ffn_sim.archive.hoomd_legacy.bridge.manifold_traction (:7,:46,:49,:53), i.e. the traction-FIELD instrument only exists on the forbidden HOOMD runtime. GlobalCellLedger carries force/work/mass/balance but no moment and no centroid channel (ac/engine/ledger.py:14-20,:167-179), so the two most robust and most-often-published TFM observables — the contractile moment tensor M_ij = sum r_i (x) f_j and the strain energy U = 0.5 * integral u.T dA — cannot be computed at all. This is the same hole as the missing crawl force dipole.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Forward-project the exact per-bond traction onto a linear-elastic half-space at the target paper's gel modulus, sample it at the paper's bead spacing with the paper's noise, invert with the paper's regularizer, and report both the recovered field and the recovered/true ratio. Add moment + centroid channels to the ledger and report the contractile moment and strain energy as the primary TFM-comparable scalars.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: The inversion round-trip ratio itself: recovered_peak/true_peak and recovered_moment/true_moment. Both are pure dimensionless ratios requiring no sourced constant, and they quantify exactly how much of the published-vs-model gap is instrument loss rather than physics.

instruments.name: FA Dirichlet reaction at PINNED anchors read as traction (GATE B)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The traction a stress fiber delivers to its focal adhesion — comparable to TFM per-FA forces.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The residual force left on a node held by a Dirichlet pin, i.e. the reaction of an INFINITELY RIGID substrate. Its sign (inward = contractile) and its radial projection are sound and magnitude-free; its magnitude is a stall value at zero adhesion displacement, and it is stiffness-INDEPENDENT by construction.
instruments.evidence: The repo states the defect itself, in ff_stiffness_sensing.py:4-6: "A rigid dish (substrate_plane_kernel + FIXED FA anchors) makes stiffness structurally impossible - every anchor is infinitely rigid, so traction can only rise with contraction, never read E." Published TFM is performed on 1-30 kPa gels and its single most robust, most reproduced result is that traction RISES with substrate rigidity (biphasic in the motor-clutch picture). A pinned-anchor instrument returns a flat line against that axis, so it cannot be compared to any TFM dataset, and the current script's own honest banner (:634) already forbids quoting the magnitudes.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Replace the pins with the Winkler-compliant anchors already implemented (k_sub = 2*E*a/(1-nu^2), ff/substrate.py via ff_stiffness_sensing.py PATH-b) or with the two-sided cell<->ECM clutch (PATH-a), so the adhesion has a displacement and the traction acquires an E dependence.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Sweep the substrate modulus over the PA-gel ladder and require the traction to MOVE. A flat response is proof the instrument is measuring a boundary condition rather than a traction — and it is a check that costs no sourced parameter, only a relative sweep.

instruments.name: Substrate-stiffness sensing (Winkler anchors, biphasic optimum)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The cell reads substrate rigidity; traction traces the Bangasser-Odde biphasic optimum.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that, through one derived knob (k_sub = 2*E*a/(1-nu^2), flat-punch on an elastic half-space), with E as the input and the optimum MEASURED. The script itself declares that the ABSOLUTE traction carries the unsourced adhesion-patch radius a and that only the RELATIVE optimum (which E maximises traction) is a-invariant and therefore claimed.
instruments.evidence: ff_stiffness_sensing.py:40-44: "No parameter is tuned to an outcome: E is the input, k_sub is the DERIVED Winkler relation, and the biphasic optimum is MEASURED" and "only the RELATIVE optimum ... is a-invariant and claimed here." This is the one instrument in the family that separates its magnitude-dependent claim from its magnitude-free claim before reporting, and it is exactly the discipline PI priority 2 asks for. Caveat: its own banner (:45-46) says findings must be reconfirmed at native, and it quotes the retired --nf 38000 rather than 70,686.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None needed; promote this file's claim-splitting pattern to the template for every other instrument in this family, and update its native banner from 38000 to 70,686.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Already present in spirit: rerun with rigid (pinned) anchors and confirm the biphasic optimum DISAPPEARS. That contrast is the positive control for the whole stiffness axis and should be committed as a test.

instruments.name: Micropipette aspiration (Evans-Yeung)
instruments.where: ABSENT from all executable code. Text-only: /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ff/network_warp.py:1672 (the word "aspiration" in a docstring), /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/validation/oracles/spheroid/surface_tension_bridge.py:32-34,:92-94 (Roffay pipette-validated ratio)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Nothing in the code claims to be aspiration — but aspiration-derived numbers are registered as validation targets.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing. There is no pipette radius R_p, no suction pressure ramp, no tongue length L_p(t), no critical-pressure criterion dP_crit = 2*T*(1/R_p - 1/R_c), and no cortex-only vs whole-cell distinction (aspiration at small R_p probes the cortex; at large R_p it probes the whole cell — a factor that alone accounts for order-of-magnitude spread in the published literature).
instruments.evidence: grep for aspirat|micropipette|pipette across all *.py returns only archive/hoomd_legacy, one network_warp docstring word, and the spheroid oracle. Meanwhile MDA_MB_231_BASELINE_CONTRACT_2026-07-13.md:50 registers "206 Pa (aspiration)" alongside "224 Pa (AFM)" as validation data, and TURGOR_PRESSURE_MCF7_2026-07-24.md relies on aspiration literature. So aspiration numbers are comparison targets with no reproducing protocol, and the AFM-vs-aspiration difference (adherent-local vs suspended-global, small vs large strain) is being silently treated as agreement.
instruments.canonical_replacement: A suction-BC harness on the resting suspended cell: fixed R_p, ramped suction, measure L_p(R_p) and the flow-in threshold, invert with the SAME Evans-Yeung relation the source paper used, and report cortex-only vs whole-cell separately.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: The dimensionless L_p/R_p vs dP*R_p/T collapse: aspiration data from different pipette radii must fall on ONE curve. If the model's curves do not collapse, the tension it reports is R_p-dependent, i.e. not a material tension. Requires no absolute constant.

instruments.name: Laser ablation recoil
instruments.where: ABSENT. The token "ablation" in this tree means two different, unrelated things: sensitivity-ablation studies (/Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/emergence/__init__.py:27, ffn_sim/scripts/h1_ablation_nodenode_rep.py) and ERM-tether de-adhesion for blebbing (/Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/cell/bleb_perturbation.py:4,:49)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A cut-and-recoil tension measurement, as in stress-fiber or junction ablation.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing of the sort. bleb_perturbation.py irreversibly de-adheres ERM tethers inside an angular cap — that is the Charras bleb-nucleation protocol, and it is a legitimate protocol, but it measures bleb growth, not recoil. No element is ever SEVERED to release tension, and no recoil velocity is measured anywhere (grep recoil|retraction_velocity|sever across ac/, ff/, scripts/ returns only the population-bookkeeping sever in ac/engine/population.py:148).
instruments.evidence: The name collision is itself a measurement hazard of exactly the kind this audit exists for: a reader who greps "ablation" finds ten hits and could conclude the protocol exists. Note also the physics point that must be written into the instrument when it is built: initial recoil velocity measures tension/EFFECTIVE FRICTION, not tension — so a recoil comparison without an independent friction/drag determination is an underdetermined two-parameter inference, and the timescale window matters (the first ~1 s is elastic recoil, later relaxation is viscoelastic).
instruments.canonical_replacement: A sever-and-release harness: remove a set of elements along a line inside one accepted transaction, then record the retraction of the two cut ends at high time resolution; report v_recoil AND the fitted relaxation time, and state explicitly that only the ratio tension/friction is determined by v_recoil alone.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Sever in a network held at ZERO prestress (myosin off, turgor at rest): v_recoil must be 0 within noise. Then sweep the imposed prestress and require v_recoil to scale linearly with it at fixed drag — a magnitude-free exponent check that also proves the instrument reads tension rather than the cut geometry.

instruments.name: Spreading assay A(t)/A0 and its time base
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A cell-spreading time course comparable to Cuvelier 2007 / Dubin-Thaler / Betorz 2023, validated against A/A0 ~ 2-4.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: (a) AREA: "basal contact footprint = convex-hull area of the lamellipodial actin near the basal plane" — simultaneously basal-contact, footprint AND convex-hull, i.e. three members of the set the PI registered as automatic RETRACT on 2026-06-12, versus the ratified top-down xy silhouette. (b) A0: the footprint at the first sample AFTER warmup and soft-start equilibration, when a construction-geometry lamellipodium already exists — so A0 is already a spread area and A/A0 is systematically compressed. (c) TIME: t_phys_min = (r_front - r_front0) / v_front_lit_um_min, i.e. the physical time axis is obtained by DIVIDING the model's own front advance by a literature spreading velocity, and S_accel_effective is then back-computed from it.
instruments.evidence: Lines :28-30 and :89-96 for the forbidden area family; :298 `A0 = r0["A_um2"]` taken from the post-warmup sample; :398-404 for the time-axis construction. The time base is therefore not measured but calibrated against the literature quantity the run is being compared to — any A(t) rate agreement is guaranteed and only the SHAPE of the curve is a prediction. Separately the harness imports archive/hoomd_legacy (:53,:181,:232), so the only spreading instrument with a time base runs on the forbidden runtime, and there is no ac/ spreading harness at all.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Use the ratified top-down xy silhouette; define A0 as the SUSPENDED cell's projected area (pi*R^2) or the area at first substrate contact, and define t=0 at first contact with the seeding transient reported rather than absorbed; drive time by the physical clock and report the kinetic acceleration factor S as an explicit, separately-reported approximation.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: S-collapse: run at two acceleration factors S and 2S and require the A(t/S) curves — and in particular the fitted early power-law exponent — to superimpose. If the exponent moves with S, the fast-forward has changed the physics, not just the clock. This is a pure dimensionless collapse test.

instruments.name: A/A0 top-down silhouette (the ratified definition) as implemented
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Top-down silhouette area — the PI-ratified 2026-06-12 spreading observable, explicitly "NEVER basal contact area".
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The 2-D CONVEX HULL of all live nodes projected to xy. For a convex compacted aggregate this equals the silhouette; for a lobed, stellate or multi-lobed spread morphology the hull strictly OVER-estimates the silhouette, and the over-estimate grows precisely as the morphology becomes interesting. The docstring says "silhouette"; the code says ConvexHull.
instruments.evidence: dcm_warp_decohesion.py:248-250: "Top-down silhouette area [um2] = 2D convex hull of all live nodes (PI rule: NEVER basal contact area)" then `ConvexHull(pos_xy_um).volume`. The A0 convention is also worth stating openly: A0 is the post-settle RESTED area (:1604-1606), so settle frames read >1 falling to 1.0 and spread frames climb above 1.0 — a defensible choice, but it means A/A0 mixes a compaction phase and a spreading phase on one axis.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Rasterize the projected occupancy (or use an alpha-shape at the node spacing) and report hull_area/silhouette_area alongside; keep the hull only if that ratio is shown to stay within a stated tolerance.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: hull_area / rasterized_silhouette_area must stay near 1. Construct a deliberately non-convex configuration (two lobes) and confirm the hull inflates while the raster does not — a pure ratio, no parameter.

instruments.name: Optical / magnetic tweezers
instruments.where: ABSENT as a protocol. Nearest analogue: /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ff/network_warp.py:1089-1102 (local_load patch force), :1358-1364 and :1457-1462 (patch_deflection_um). Tweezer literature appears only as the SOURCE of a blocked parameter: /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/engine/intermediate_filament_rig.py:835-844
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A calibrated local force applied to a bead, with the bead displacement read against a trap stiffness.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: local_load applies a uniform f_node_pN along an axis to every cortex node inside a cos-threshold cap, and reports the mean axial displacement of that cap relative to the centroid. There is no bead, no trap stiffness, no bead-cortex coupling, and the applied load scales with the NUMBER of nodes in the cap (n_patch_nodes is reported, so the total force is n_patch*f_node and therefore mesh-resolution-dependent), rather than being a fixed total force on a fixed-size probe.
instruments.evidence: network_warp.py:1096 `_ll_f = f_node_pN` applied per node with the cap mask at :1098; metrics at :1460-1462 report patch_deflection_um, n_patch_nodes and f_node_pN separately — i.e. the instrument itself exposes that its total load is n_patch-dependent. The centroid-referencing at :1099-1102 to remove rigid COM drift is a genuinely good correction and should be kept. intermediate_filament_rig.py:838-844 refuses to invent a keratin stiffness because the optical-tweezer source is paywalled — correct discipline, and it shows tweezer data is a live comparison target with no protocol behind it.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Specify a TOTAL force on a probe of specified radius (grid-intensive: f_node = F_total/n_patch so the load is mesh-invariant), add an explicit trap-stiffness spring between the probe and its target so the measured quantity is the bead displacement the experiment records, and report the local compliance F/delta rather than a raw deflection.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Grid invariance of the local compliance: refine the cortex mesh at fixed F_total and fixed cap solid angle; F_total/delta must be unchanged. With the present per-node convention it will scale with n_patch, which is exactly the silent 10x.

instruments.name: Osmotic shock — the prediction oracle (Boyle-van't Hoff)
instruments.where: /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/validation/oracles/osmotic_response.py:1-56 (incl. an explicit Sanity Gate with a "Measurement-protocol" clause), :90-107 (pbvh_v_eq)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The acceptance envelope for the osmotic axis: Ponder-Boyle-van't Hoff v_eq = b + (1-b)/r, two-timescale time course, permeant-solute reflection decay, shape split via alpha, stiffness sensitivity via m.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly what it says, dimensionlessly, as a swept literature-range BAND rather than a single curve — and it states its own protocol convention in writing: "v is V/V0 of the SAME cell relative to its in-medium reference; there is deliberately no 'osmotic pressure = 0' control". It also separates volume change from shape change (alpha) so "shrunk" cannot be confused with "flattened", and it labels E/E0 = v^-m a SENSITIVITY, not a law.
instruments.evidence: osmotic_response.py:44-56 lists dimensional, boundary, conservation (lx*ly*lz = v exactly), sign-sense, permeant and measurement-protocol checks. This is the best-specified measurement contract in the repository and is the model the other seven techniques should be rewritten against. Its only limitation is structural and correctly declared: it is runtime-import-forbidden, so it can only ever be an acceptance target.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None. Use its Sanity-Gate block as the required header template for every instrument in this family.

In ff/ the coupling does exist and has the correct BvH shape, Pi_in(V) = N kT/(V - Vmin) with Vmin = 0.30*V0, deriving K_vol instead of positing it. instruments.name: AFM / micropipette on the NUCLEUS
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Nuclear mechanics anchored to a measured nuclear Young's modulus (399 Pa MCF7, Fischer/Hayn/Mierke 2020).
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Two separate protocol substitutions. (1) The 399 Pa datum is an IN-SITU OVER-NUCLEUS apparent modulus: an indenter pressing through membrane + cortex + cytoplasm above the nucleus. It is assigned as the nucleus shell's OWN material modulus in a model that ALSO explicitly represents cortex and cytoplasm — so the cortical and cytoplasmic contributions to that apparent number are counted twice. (2) The nucleus is never indented: ff_s3 measures the nucleus contribution by DIFFERENCE between whole-cell plate compression with and without the nucleus, and the E -> k bridge (n_beads*k_chrom = 4*pi*E*R) is a dimensionally-consistent heuristic, not the inverse of any contact model. There is no isolated-nucleus harness, no pipette, no indenter geometry.
instruments.evidence: compartments.py:189-196 documents the choice of the in-situ 399 Pa over the isolated-nucleus 1-5 kPa on physiological-baseline grounds — correct instinct, wrong inference: "the nucleus in situ is softer" and "the over-nucleus apparent modulus IS the nuclear modulus" are different claims. ff_s3_nucleus_compression.py:9-13 states the by-difference method and reports the nucleus at E=399 Pa is SOFTER than the bare cortex (~3624 Pa) with only ~+11% contribution at eps=0.45 — a result whose sign depends entirely on the double-counted calibration. Note also the internal contradiction: ff_s3:43 sets NU_NUC=0.499 "volume-conserving flattening" while :18-19 retires an equatorial-bulge gate as "structurally impossible for this volume-non-conserving shell nucleus".
instruments.canonical_replacement: Calibrate the nucleus law INVERSELY: choose k_chrom/k_lamin so that the MODEL'S OWN virtual over-nucleus indentation — same indenter radius, depth, speed, and contact model as Fischer 2020 — returns 399 Pa with the full membrane+cortex+cytoplasm stack present. Separately build an isolated-nucleus harness for the 1-5 kPa isolated datum, and check that the same material law reproduces both.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Composite-vs-component: run the virtual over-nucleus indentation with the nucleus REMOVED. Whatever apparent modulus the cortex+cytoplasm alone return is the amount currently being double-counted; if it is not small compared to 399 Pa, the direct assignment is invalid. Cost: one extra run, no new parameter.

instruments.name: Per-node virial von-Mises stress (ff_virial_stress)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The REAL internal Cauchy stress field of the cortex in Pa, nonzero at equilibrium, comparable to a measured stress.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A partial virial: crosslinks + myosin links + turgor only. The ACTIN BACKBONE inextensibility constraint tension — which in this cortex is the dominant load carrier, and which the project already extracts separately (ac/cell/assembled_cortical_stress.py:8, "the key extraction - ACTIN AXIAL TENSION from the inextensibility constraint") — is omitted, as is bending. And the absolute magnitude is set entirely by the caller-supplied node_vol; in ac/cell/assemble.py:931-932 that is cell_vol/n_actin, a whole-cell volume per actin node, not a cortical shell volume.
instruments.evidence: ff_virial_stress.py:8-11 lists the deviatoric carriers as crosslinks and myosin and explicitly excludes bending, with no mention of the constraint multipliers; assemble.py:931-932 sets node_vol = cell_vol/n_actin. Since sigma = (1/V_node) * sum(...), any comparison of the reported Pa to a measured stress is really a statement about the chosen node volume — and choosing a cortical-shell volume instead of a whole-cell volume changes it by the ratio of cell volume to shell volume, i.e. more than an order of magnitude.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Include the actin axial constraint tension (it already exists as an extraction) in the virial, state the excluded terms in the field's label, and derive node_vol from the cortex thickness x surface area / N so it is grid-intensive and physically meaningful.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Grid invariance: refine the cortex discretization at fixed physiology. node_vol scales as 1/N, so a correctly assembled sigma (Pa) must be invariant; if the reported field moves with N, the normalization rather than the physics is being reported.

instruments.name: assemble_balance force-closure gate (the connectedness gate PI priority 1 depends on)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The global acceptance gate proving reaction + traction = 0, i.e. that the compartments are mechanically connected and Newton's third law closes across connectors.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: |reaction_resultant + traction_resultant|^2 against a tolerance the CALLER must supply — and every caller in the tree defaults tol_sq_d to None, so in practice the gate is not armed. It is also a RESULTANT-only check: a resultant of zero is satisfied by any force pair that cancels, so it cannot distinguish a correctly transmitted load from two independent errors of opposite sign, and it says nothing about moment closure.
instruments.evidence: ledger.py:333-335 "Supplied by the caller so no numerical tolerance is baked in" — defensible design, but cortex_motor_slice.py:626,:646,:662, interior_column_slice.py:544,:581,:597 and erm_cortex_slice.py:298,:319 all default it to None. The ledger has no moment channel and no centroid channel (:14-20,:167-179), so the adjoint/Newton-third-law claim is only ever checked at the level of a net force. Under PI priority 1 (mechanical connectedness IS the gate) this is the load-bearing instrument and it is currently both un-armed and under-specified.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Add a moment channel (M = sum r x f about a declared centroid) and gate BOTH |sum F| and |sum M| — moment closure is the check that actually distinguishes a transmitted load from a coincidental cancellation. Then declare the tolerance in the gate contract, derived the way ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py derives the 0.21 pN, and make tol_sq_d required rather than optional.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Inject a deliberate sign error into ONE connector's adjoint half. |sum F| stays near zero if a second error compensates; |sum M| about the cell centroid will not. A gate nobody has watched fail is not a gate — and this one, as shipped, cannot fail because it is never supplied a tolerance.

magnitude_free_oracles: THREE-ROUTE PRESSURE/TENSION CLOSURE (free, today): the AFM function already computes dP_turgor (internal state), dP_from_force = F_plate/(pi*a^2) (the Fischer-Friedrich measurable), and gamma_apparent = 0.5*dP*R_eq. Gate |dP_from_force/dP_turgor - 1| and |gamma_MoP/(0.5*dP*R_eq) - 1| at convergence. Three independent routes to one quantity; their spread IS the non-equilibrium/instrument error. All three numbers are already in the same metrics dict (network_warp.py:1437-1439) and have never been compared.

RELAXATION CERTIFICATE ON EVERY REPORTED FORCE OR MODULUS: report E(2N)/E(N) (or T(2N)/T(N)) with every number. The retracted AFM chain fails visibly (4127 -> 262 -> 20 -> 19 Pa across n_steps 1600->12800) and so did the retracted T = 1.92 pN. Dimensionless, needs no parameter, and would have caught both retractions before publication.

HERTZ EXPONENT FIT: fit log F vs log delta over the small-strain window and require the exponent = 1.50 +/- 0.05 before any E is quoted. A non-1.5 exponent means the response is not Hertzian and the inverted E is meaningless independent of its magnitude. The existing 'flatness' check (max/min of E_pt across strain) does NOT test this and passed on the retracted result.

CONTACT-POINT SENSITIVITY: re-invert the same F-vs-position data with the contact reference at R0_mean, R0_p95 and R0_max. Report the spread. Since E ~ delta^-1.5, this single ratio bounds the dominant silent error in every small-indentation modulus.

PRESS-SPEED SCALING EXPONENTS: on the viscous branch require d log F / d log v = 1.00 (Newtonian) and on the relaxed branch 0.00. Already observed as 1009/204/41 across v = 5/1/0.2 (FF_RESULTS_LOG.md:249-253) — promote the observation to a gate, and it distinguishes a viscous transient from an elastic modulus with no sourced constant.

DRAG-LAW POSITIVE CONTROL: double eta_bulk_Pa_s and require the recovered eta_eff to double exactly (ratio 2.000). The current check compares eta_eff to eta 'within ~2x' through an invented squeeze-flow geometry factor; a doubling test removes the geometry factor entirely.

ONE-SIDED VS TWO-SIDED INDENTATION CONTRAST: same cell, same delta, top plate only vs both plates. A protocol-faithful local indentation must be insensitive to the far boundary; the current instrument will not be, and the size of the change measures how much of the reported force is the symmetric volumetric constraint.

SIGN-RANDOMIZATION NULL FOR method_of_planes_gamma: randomize element tension signs (or run a thermal-only network). A tension estimator must return ~0; mean(|gamma_n|) returns a positive floor. That floor is the instrument's bias and is directly relevant to a project whose headline deficit is a gamma FLOOR.

PRINCIPAL-TENSION ANISOTROPY RATIO: report hoop and meridional cut tensions separately. Their ratio must be 1 for a sphere and must depart from 1 under flattening or adhesion. A single isotropic scalar cannot be Laplace-inverted on the adherent baseline PI priority 3 asks for, and the ratio exposes that without any absolute value.

TFM INVERSION ROUND-TRIP: forward-project the exact per-bond traction to a half-space displacement field, sample at the target paper's bead spacing with its noise, invert with its regularizer, and report recovered/true for both peak traction and contractile moment. Pure ratios; they quantify how much of any model-vs-published gap is instrument loss rather than physics.

TRACTION-VS-SUBSTRATE-STIFFNESS RESPONSE: sweep E_sub and require a non-degenerate (monotone-then-saturating or biphasic) response. A pinned-anchor instrument returns a flat line BY CONSTRUCTION, so this catches the rigid-substrate substitution in GATE B. Relative sweep only — no absolute traction needed.

MOMENT CLOSURE AND CONTRACTILE-DIPOLE SYMMETRY: with the moment channel added, require sum F = 0, M symmetric, and M negative-definite (contractile). Symmetry and sign are magnitude-free, and they are the checks that distinguish a transmitted load from two coincidentally cancelling errors — exactly what PI priority 1 needs.

BOYLE-VAN'T HOFF PARAMETER RECOVERY: fit V_eq vs 1/r and require the recovered osmotically-inactive fraction b to equal the injected b (VMIN_FRAC = 0.30). Straight-line intercept test, entirely dimensionless.

PIPETTE-RADIUS COLLAPSE (once aspiration exists): aspiration curves from different R_p must collapse onto one L_p/R_p vs dP*R_p/T curve. Failure to collapse proves the reported tension is R_p-dependent and therefore not a material property.

KINETIC-ACCELERATION COLLAPSE FOR SPREADING: run at S and 2S and require A(t/S) — and especially the fitted early power-law exponent — to superimpose. If the exponent moves with S, the fast-forward changed the physics rather than the clock.

HULL-VS-SILHOUETTE RATIO FOR A/A0: hull_area / rasterized_projected_area must stay near 1; construct a two-lobed configuration as the positive control where the hull must inflate and the raster must not.

GRID INVARIANCE OF ALL INTENSIVE FIELDS: refine the discretization and require per-node virial sigma (Pa), local compliance F_total/delta, and per-node drag sum (6*pi*eta*R) to be unchanged. Catches the node_vol normalization in ff_virial_stress and the n_patch-dependent total load in local_load.

result.method:
DESIGN 2 — Tensor networks / MPS (DMRG, stochastic-MPS, tDVP) applied to the simulator's discrete stochastic layer: the per-head NMII bound/unbound configuration s in {0,1}^N (plus crosslinker, ERM, clutch, MT-DI, Arp2/3 states), on the premise that 2^320 (slice) / 2^8840 (native cortex) is structurally a many-body Hilbert space compressible to polynomial size, eliminating MC sampling noise and giving exact rare-event / large-deviation statistics. Audited against the code, not against principle.

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES (the decisive read):
(1) ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:376-411 — SFImplicitCG._stiffness assembles the tangent operator by launching add_segment_crossbridge_stiffness_kernel with t.state.bound_d, seg_a_d, seg_b_d, bary_t_d, abscissa_d, walk_dir_d as INPUTS. The mechanical operator is literally A = A(s): each bound head adds a rank-1 term k_xb*w*w^T coupling its nmii particle to the two target nodes of its segment.
(2) ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:85-90 — the solve runs over a CONCATENATED [SF nodes | NMII particles] scratch (904 nodes / 2712 DOF in the landed slice). One global PCG, all heads and all nodes in one linear system.
(3) ac/engine/sf_motor_slice.py:365-371 — order is solve() THEN connector.compute_loads(). Loads are read off the CONVERGED global geometry.
(4) ac/motor/segment_motor.py:503-533 — head h's load = k_xb*(dot(x_att(port_pos[seg_a[h]], port_pos[seg_b[h]]) - actuator_pos[head_node[h]], w) - r0_bind[h]). A pure function of solved positions.
(5) ac/motor/hand.py:242 and segment_motor.py:186 — off-rate = catch_slip_off_rate(loads_bell[h], ...), the Pereverzev/Kovacs hazard evaluated on that load.

Composing (1)-(5): rate_h = g(load_h(A(s)^{-1} b(s))). Every head's hazard is a functional of the inverse of a matrix that depends on the entire binding configuration. That is the object a tensor network would have to represent, and no finite-bond-dimension MPO represents a configuration-dependent matrix inverse. This obstruction is PRIOR to, and independent of, any entanglement-growth argument: DMRG has no generator to sweep on.

The all-to-all structure is also explicit and physical, not incidental: all 20 heads of one minifilament hang off ONE shared rigid backbone (backbone_bonds k=1000 pN/um, head arms k=100, plus backbone angle-harmonic at rest pi and head-arm angle-harmonic at rest pi/2 — sf_implicit.py:391-406). Twenty heads welded to one rod, binding onto the same two 8-segment filaments, are mechanically all-to-all coupled by construction. Inter-minifilament coupling then runs through the SF/cortex network, the alpha-actinin joints, and the FA/LINC anchors.

Two further global couplings exist by design: the NF2007 inextensibility projector is an exact per-fiber tridiagonal INVERSE (ac/cell/inner_mechanics.py:79-140, dense within a fiber — but fibers are only 7 nodes cortex / 9 nodes SF, so this one is genuinely short-ranged), and CellTransaction gates EVERY discrete commit in the cell on ONE device scalar accept predicate (ac/engine/transaction.py:132-150; the attach kernel reads accepted[0] at segment_motor.py:434). Honesty note: in the landed SF gate that predicate is hard-wired to 1 (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:497), so the global-accept coupling is architectural, not currently exercised. My verdict therefore rests on the mechanical coupling, which IS exercised; the accept predicate would only make locality worse.
result.what_it_buys:
Honest inventory of what MPS/DMRG would deliver here, with each item priced against what already exists:

1. EXACT RARE-EVENT PROBABILITIES — near-zero value in the current regime. Measured GATE-B bound fraction is 301/320 = 0.941 (outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/sf_motor_native_gate.json). The combinatorially rare binding event (a whole minifilament releasing) has p = 0.059^20 = 5e-25, i.e. no relevance on any simulated timescale. The project's real rare events (bleb nucleation a_crit = 2*gamma/dP, cortex rupture) are MECHANICAL instability thresholds, not rare binding configurations. Rare-event value would only appear if the duty sat near 0.5, which no sourced parameter suggests.

2. ELIMINATION OF SEED-TO-SEED NOISE — buys 0.25 to 1.4 percent. Binomial spread at the measured duty: SF slice sd(n_bound) = sqrt(320*0.941*0.059) = 4.2 on 301, i.e. 1.4 percent; native cortex at 8840 heads = 0.25 percent, and it falls as 1/sqrt(n_seeds) with the already-deterministic SeedSequence spawn (ac/engine/ensemble.py:27-30). Compare the live measurement uncertainties on the SAME artifact: residual/tension = 15.5 percent, and a 10x longer relax moved T_max by 3.4x (240 percent). Removing a 1 percent noise term while a 340 percent convergence term is open inverts the priority order. This is the single strongest argument against DO_NOW.

3. EXACT ACCEPTED-STEP PROBABILITIES — does not apply to this codebase. The accept predicate is a DETERMINISTIC function of the converged mechanical state (ledger.assemble_balance on |reaction + traction|^2, transaction.py:132-144), so given a configuration it is 0 or 1. There is no accepted-step probability to compute exactly. This part of the motivation is a mismatch with the actual design.

4. LARGE-DEVIATION STATISTICS (SCGF of cumulative work / total abscissa) — genuinely novel, no existing oracle covers it. But it needs the same mechanical surrogate as everything else, so it inherits the same rejection.

5. The one scientifically real question in the neighbourhood — do N load-sharing CATCH bonds show a mean-field-artifact bistability that a finite-N exact treatment smooths? — is answerable EXACTLY and CHEAPLY without any tensor network, because heads sharing one scalar backbone load are exchangeable, so the exact master equation lumps (in the strict Markov-lumpability sense) from 2^N to the N+1 count states of n_bound. For n_side=10 that is 21 states; for the physiological Billington-scale n_side=30 it is 61. The mechanical closure load(n) is tabulated with N+1 solves, not 2^N. This is exact, five orders cheaper than MPS, and its residual assumption (head exchangeability) is directly measurable from the loads_bell array the code already fills.

Net: every item MPS would buy is either near-zero value at the measured operating point, already covered by a validated closed form (ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py gives the mean-field binomial engaged fraction with its own sanity gate), or reachable exactly by a permutation-symmetric count chain at 1e-5 of the cost.
prerequisites: NONE — this is a REJECT, not a DO_AFTER_PREREQ. The prerequisites below are what a reversal would require, listed so the decision is falsifiable rather than merely negative.

REVERSAL PREREQ 1 (locality): the head-head mechanical sensitivity matrix J[h,h'] = d(load_h)/d(bind state of h') must be measured on real geometry and must show BOTH (a) a finite correlation length shorter than the natural 1D ordering spacing, AND (b) within-minifilament effective rank r_eff <= 4 out of 20. Prediction from the code: J_intra is near-full-rank because 20 heads share one rigid angle-harmonic backbone, so this prereq fails.

REVERSAL PREREQ 2 (generator representability): someone must exhibit a finite-bond-dimension MPO for s -> A(s)^{-1} b(s), or PI must ratify replacing the global solve with a frozen/linearized elastic environment. The latter is a lumped abstraction of a mechanistic process and is forbidden for the runtime by the CLAUDE.md architectural hard rule; it is admissible only as an acceptance oracle.

REVERSAL PREREQ 3 (state-space honesty): the per-head state is NOT a bit. From the connector SoA it is (bound, bound_seg_id, seg_a, seg_b, bary_t in R, abscissa in R+, r0_bind in R, walk_dir in R^3). Any MPS requires discretizing bary_t and abscissa, which introduces bin widths chosen for tractability — new magic numbers that must pass the Magic-Number Block (grid-invariance) before any number is quoted.

REVERSAL PREREQ 4 (hardware): exact representation of even ONE 20-head minifilament block needs chi = 2^10 = 1024, which is 687 GB of MPO environments — 43 A5000s. The mandated minimum hardware cannot represent the smallest available slice exactly, for the reduced binary-only model.
concrete_plan: DO NOT open a tensor-network track. Record the negative result with its arithmetic in docs/v2_audit/ so it is not re-queued, and register the three code facts that make it negative (sf_implicit.py:407-411 A=A(s); sf_implicit.py:85-90 one concatenated global solve; sf_motor_slice.py:365-371 loads read post-solve).

STEP 1 — RUN THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT ANYWAY, because it answers the PI's CURRENT gate (mechanical connectedness), not the MPS question. Instrument: the head-head sensitivity matrix J. Procedure, using only existing code: converge the slice; then for each probe head h', flip state.bound_d[h'] (or add a unit crossbridge force along walk_dir[h']), re-run the SAME SFImplicitCG solve, and read delta(loads_bell) on all 320 heads via connector.compute_loads. One extra solve per probe. 40 probes on the SF slice = 40 solves = seconds of A5000 time. Zero new physics, zero new parameters.

STEP 2 — EMIT THREE MAGNITUDE-FREE OBSERVABLES FROM J, with the decision rule COMMITTED TO DISK BEFORE THE RUN (no gate-loosening): (a) normalized decay J(r)/J(0) versus mechanical graph distance r, log-log, no axis truncation, with the fitted exponent; (b) singular-value spectrum of J restricted to within-minifilament and to across-minifilament blocks, reporting r_eff = count of singular values above 1 percent of sigma_max; (c) block ratio B = ||J_intra||_F / ||J_inter||_F. Pre-registered rule: tensor networks are reconsidered only if a finite xi exists AND r_eff <= 4 for a 20-head block. Otherwise the verdict stands permanently.

STEP 3 — SWEEP THE ONE RATIO THE ANSWER DEPENDS ON. k_xb and k_axial are both PI-GAPs (both 1000 pN/um in the landed run). Report J's decay exponent and r_eff across k_xb/k_axial spanning at least four decades and state whether the locality verdict is ratio-robust. This is a scaling/dimensionless measurement, exactly the kind PI priority 2 asks for; it is NOT a magnitude claim and does not need either constant sourced.

STEP 4 — HARVEST J FOR THE ACTUAL PI GATE. J restricted to (nmii heads) x (sf_arc / cortex / ECM nodes) is a direct, quantitative mechanical-connectedness instrument: a structurally zero block PROVES co-location without connection, which is the exact failure mode the component/connector contract exists to prevent and which no current instrument measures. Extend it to arbitrary component pairs by probing a connector's force channel and reading the other component's node displacement. This deliverable justifies steps 1-3 on its own merit whatever the MPS answer is.

STEP 5 — IF PI WANTS EXACT DISCRETE-STATE STATISTICS, BUILD THE COUNT CHAIN, NOT AN MPS. Exploit head exchangeability within one minifilament: exact master equation on n_bound in {0..N}, N+1 = 21 states now / 61 at Billington-scale n_side=30, with the mechanical closure load(n) tabulated by N+1 real solves. Ship it in validation/oracles/ under the existing runtime-import-forbidden firewall, next to ensemble_stall_analytic.py, which it strictly generalizes (that oracle assumes independence; this one keeps load-sharing correlations exactly).

STEP 6 — SHIP THE EXCHANGEABILITY RESIDUAL ALONGSIDE IT, using an array that already exists. Log CV = sd(loads_bell over the bound heads of one minifilament) / mean, per minifilament, per step. If CV << 1 the count chain is a trustworthy oracle; if CV ~ 1 then neither the count chain nor mean-field is trustworthy and the correct response is more MC seeds, not a tensor network. This residual is the analogue of residual/tension and must be reported with any number the oracle produces, so that the failure mode of the retracted 1.92 pN PASS cannot recur.

STEP 7 — NAME AND CLOSE THE ADJACENT IDEA SO IT IS NOT CONFUSED WITH THIS ONE. QTT/tensor-train compression of the MECHANICAL field (accelerating the 1.5M-DOF solve rather than the binding state space) is a DIFFERENT proposal. It works for smooth fields on regular grids; the actin network is an unstructured graph at 7 nodes per fiber with stiffness spanning 4.6e5 versus 1e3 pN/um, which is the rank-blowup regime, and the project already has a closed audit finding the native solve CG-dominated with a ~9 percent optimization ceiling and a do-not-retry verdict. Record it as closed, separately.
result.cost_arithmetic:
MEASURED SYSTEM SIZES (from disk, not assumed):
- SF motor slice (outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/sf_motor_native_gate.json): 320 heads / 16 minifilaments (20 heads each, n_side=10) / 360 SF nodes / 544 NMII particles / 320 links = 2712 mechanical DOF. Measured 301/320 bound, T_max 0.254 pN, head_load_max 0.0545 pN, residual/tension 0.155.
- Full native cortex (outputs/ac/foundation-hardening/native_resting_70686.json): 70,686 filaments / 494,802 actin nodes / 511,114 total nodes / 442 minifilaments / 8840 heads / 15,028 myosin particles / 70,686 crosslinks / 642 ERM tethers. A5000 16 GB (16,760,569,856 bytes), 452 MB currently used.
- Measured A5000 mechanical cost (outputs/ac/implicit/REPORT.md): full-native explicit 0.02271 s/iteration; accelerated 0.27968 to 0.82235 s/iteration. Scaled to the 2712-DOF slice: about 4e-5 s/iteration, so the entire 6-step / 200-relax GATE-B MC run costs about 0.05 s of solver time.
- The KMC layer is 3 kernel launches over 8840 threads, tens of microseconds. The discrete layer is therefore under 0.1 percent of step cost. There is no runtime there to win, only to add.

MPS/DMRG COST, SF SLICE (320 heads), fp64 on A5000 (27.8 TFLOP/s fp32, fp64 = 1/32 = 0.87 peak, realistic 0.5):
- Memory = [N*d*chi^2 (state) + 2*N*D_W*chi^2 (MPO environments)] * 8 bytes. Environments dominate.
- BINARY-ONLY model (drop abscissa — itself a forbidden lumping), d=2, MPO bond D_W about 128 for a rate that is a product operator over all sites (or D_W about N+1 = 321 with the naive sum-of-products construction).
- chi feasible on 8 GB usable: chi^2 <= 8e9/(2*320*128*8) = 12,207, so chi_max = 110.
- chi REQUIRED for exactness at a mid-block cut of ONE 20-head all-to-all minifilament: chi = 2^10 = 1024.
- Memory at chi=1024: 2*320*128*1024^2*8 = 687 GB = 43 A5000s (or about 9 H100-80GB). The mandated minimum hardware cannot represent even the smallest slice exactly.
- Time per sweep = O(N*d*chi^3*D_W). At chi=110: 320*2*1.33e6*128 = 1.1e11 flops = 0.22 s/sweep, about 2.2 s per outer step at 10 sweeps. At chi=1024 (exact): 320*2*1.07e9*128 = 8.8e13 flops = 176 s/sweep, about 1760 s per outer step (352 s/sweep and 3520 s/step if D_W=321).
- VERSUS MC: about 8e-3 s per outer step for this slice. So feasible-memory MPS is about 275x slower AND still approximate below the exactness threshold; exact MPS is about 2.2e5x slower AND needs 687 GB. The configuration in which MPS fits memory is the configuration in which it loses the one property that justified it.
- INCLUDING the real per-head state (bary_t and abscissa are continuous, ac/motor/segment_motor.py state SoA): d = 1 + N_seg_reach*N_t_bins*N_a_bins, about 1 + 4*8*16 = 513. State memory alone at chi=110 = 320*513*110^2*8 = 15.9 GB, over budget BEFORE environments. Non-starter. Note the abscissa dynamic range is only f_stall/k_xb = 0.5/1000 = 5e-4 um = 0.5 nm (the stall guard at hand.py:199 caps it), so any binning is inside half a nanometre.

MPS/DMRG COST, FULL NMII POPULATION (8840 heads):
- 2^8840 = about 1e2661 configurations. Ordering heads minifilament-contiguously makes the intra-block cut binding at chi=1024, but then inter-minifilament correlations mediated by the elastic network are exactly what gets truncated. Ordering to capture those instead: 442 minifilaments sit on a 2D shell (R=7.5 um, about 707 um^2), so any 1D ordering has cuts crossing about sqrt(442) = 21 minifilaments = about 420 sites, giving area-law chi = 2^420 for exactness.
- Memory at a merely-large chi=1024: 2*8840*128*1024^2*8 = 19 TB. Non-starter by three orders on any plausible hardware.
- And 8840 heads is not the target: the density audit says heads are about 36x under-placed, so the physiological target is about 3e5 heads, alongside 70,686 load-dependent crosslinks, 642 ERM catch-slip tethers, plus clutches, MT catastrophe/rescue and Arp2/3 — a joint discrete state of order 1e5 sites, all committing under one global accept predicate.

THE ALTERNATIVE EXACT METHOD, PRICED (the constructive half):
- Permutation-symmetric count chain: N+1 states per minifilament (21 at n_side=10, 61 at Billington-scale n_side=30). Steady state by a tridiagonal solve, O(N). Mechanical closure load(n) tabulated by N+1 solves: 61*4e-5 s = 2.4 ms for the SF slice, 61*0.023 s = 1.4 s at full native.
- That is about 1e5x to 1e6x cheaper than MPS and EXACT under exchangeability, with a residual that is directly measurable from an array the code already fills.
- Brute-force enumeration is also cheaper than MPS at this block size: 2^20 = 1.05e6 states, sparse generator about 21 nnz/row = about 170 MB. MPS is more expensive than the exact method it was supposed to replace.

THE STRUCTURAL DILEMMA, IN ONE LINE: MPS wins only when coupling is LOCAL. Here coupling within a minifilament is all-to-all through one shared rigid backbone. But all-to-all coupling is precisely the regime where mean-field becomes asymptotically exact with O(1/sqrt(N)) corrections — measured 3.3 percent per minifilament at n_side=30 and duty 0.94, and 0.16 percent aggregated over 442 minifilaments. There is no regime left for MPS: local implies MPS wins but we are not local; all-to-all implies the existing mean-field oracle (ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py) is already asymptotically exact.
failure_modes: THE DECISIVE ONE — the generator is not an MPO. rate_h = g(load_h(A(s)^{-1} b(s))) with A(s) assembled from state.bound_d at sf_implicit.py:407-411. No finite bond dimension represents a configuration-dependent matrix inverse. DMRG would have nothing to sweep on. This is a representability failure, not an entanglement failure, and it cannot be fixed by more bond dimension or better hardware.

The only way past it is to linearize x(s) or freeze the elastic environment, giving a pairwise J[h,h'] = k_xb^2 * w_h . G . w_h'. That is exactly the lumped replacement of a mechanistic process that the CLAUDE.md architectural hard rule forbids for the runtime, and it deletes the load-dependent off-rate that the fine-grained mandate exists to preserve. It is also quantitatively unsafe here: walk_dir is refreshed every step from live geometry (_refresh_bound_walk_dir_kernel), the angle harmonics are geometrically nonlinear, and the accompanying tangents are explicitly Gauss-Newton PSD approximations, not exact Hessians.

Locality fails by construction, not by accident. All 20 heads of one minifilament are welded to ONE rigid backbone with angle harmonics at rest pi and pi/2 and bind onto the same two 8-segment filaments. Any MPS ordering has an all-to-all block of 20 (60 at physiological n_side=30). Exactness needs chi = 2^10 (2^30 at n_side=30). Predicted r_eff for J_intra is near-full-rank.

A NEW MEASUREMENT FAILURE MODE, which is why this matters for the audit that commissioned it: bond-dimension truncation is an unstated convergence error of exactly the same species as the unconverged relaxation that forced the retraction of T = 1.92 pN PASS (residual/tension 15.5 percent, T_max moving 3.4x under a 10x longer relax). At chi=110 — the largest the A5000 fits — the MPS is BELOW the exactness threshold for a single minifilament, so it would emit approximate probabilities under the label exact. Any MPS deliverable must ship a 1/chi extrapolation residual channel or it manufactures confidence.

The state-space framing that motivates the proposal is wrong for this codebase. 2^320 counts a binary layer that does not exist: the connector SoA carries bound, bound_seg_id, seg_a, seg_b, bary_t (continuous), abscissa (continuous), r0_bind (continuous), walk_dir. Discretizing bary_t and abscissa reintroduces bin widths chosen for tractability — new magic numbers that must pass the Magic-Number Block. Silently dropping them to recover d=2 is itself the abstraction the project deletes on sight.

Two of the four claimed benefits do not exist here. Exact accepted-step probabilities: the accept predicate is a deterministic functional of the converged state (transaction.py:132-144), so it is 0 or 1 given a configuration — there is nothing to compute exactly. Exact rare-event probabilities: at the measured duty 0.941 the combinatorially rare event has p = 5e-25 and no physical relevance; the project's real rare events are mechanical instability thresholds.

The noise it removes is 1 to 4 orders of magnitude below the noise that is actually open. Seed noise is 0.25 to 1.4 percent (binomial at measured duty, with deterministic SeedSequence spawning already in place). Live uncertainties on the same artifact are 15.5 percent residual/tension and 240 percent under a relax-length change. Removing the 1 percent term first is a priority inversion, and a project whose dominant failure mode is instrument error should not add an instrument whose truncation error is unbounded.

MPS is beaten by brute force at the only tractable block size. 2^20 = 1.05e6 states, about 170 MB sparse — cheaper and exact. DMRG only pays off for N much greater than 30 with local coupling; here N per block is 20 to 60 with all-to-all coupling, which is the exact regime where either brute-force enumeration (N <= 25) or plain MC wins.

It is arithmetically infeasible on the mandated hardware. Exactness for the smallest slice needs 687 GB (43 A5000s) for the reduced binary model; the full population needs 19 TB at a chi that is still not exact. The larger-hardware escape hatch does not close a 3-order gap.

Warp-CUDA-only runtime blocks the implementation path. No mature fp64 GPU-Warp tensor-network stack exists; a DMRG runtime means writing sweep-mode SVD/QR in Warp from scratch, and running it on CPU is forbidden as a simulation runtime. It could only ever live in validation/oracles/ behind the runtime-import-forbidden firewall — at which point it is competing with ensemble_stall_analytic.py and with the count chain, and losing to both on cost.

Conclusion-scope violation. Any MPS result would be obtained on the 320-head slice, which the PI 2026-07-09 and 2026-07-16 rules make non-authoritative for physics conclusions; and the 320-head slice's own quantitative claim is currently BLOCKED. It would produce an exact answer to a question posed on a configuration that cannot support a conclusion.
result.how_legality_is_mechanically_enforced:
If PI overrides this verdict and any tensor-network code is written, four mechanical enforcements are required and each is already precedented in the repo:

1. IMPORT FIREWALL. Any linearized-mechanics or frozen-environment tensor-network code is an acceptance oracle, never runtime. Place it under validation/oracles/ and extend the existing static runtime-import-forbidden test so importing it from ac/, ff/, or dcm/ fails collection. This is the same mechanism that keeps the v1 closed-form oracles out of the runtime and the static Warp-only contract test that rejects direct and dynamic HOOMD imports in ac/.

2. TRUNCATION-RESIDUAL CHANNEL, MANDATORY IN THE EMITTED JSON. No MPS number may be quoted without its 1/chi extrapolation and the chi sequence that produced it, in the same JSON, in the same units — structurally parallel to residual_over_tension in sf_motor_native_gate.json. Enforce by making the emitter raise if the chi-sweep field is absent, so the number cannot physically be produced without its convergence evidence. Note explicitly for the record that the existing headline-fingerprint guard would NOT catch a swapped chi (it hashes sorted deduplicated bare numeric tokens with no units), so the residual must be a required field, not a hashed one.

3. PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE, COMMITTED BEFORE THE RUN. The locality thresholds (finite xi, and r_eff <= 4 out of 20 for the within-minifilament block) go into the repo as a contract in the same commit as the measurement script and before any output exists. A post-hoc threshold change is a gate-contract change requiring PI sign-off, not an inline edit.

4. MAGIC-NUMBER BLOCK ON EVERY DISCRETIZATION. chi, the SVD truncation threshold, and the bary_t and abscissa bin widths each require a grid-invariance demonstration (result stable as the bin count doubles) recorded in a Sanity Gate docstring section. The abscissa case is the sharp one: its entire dynamic range is f_stall/k_xb = 0.5 nm, so bin-width invariance must be shown inside half a nanometre and both defining constants are unsourced GAPs.
result.hard_rule_interaction:
- WARP-CUDA-ONLY RUNTIME (I0-A): no mature fp64 GPU-Warp tensor-network stack exists. A runtime DMRG means hand-writing sweep-mode SVD/QR in Warp; a CPU implementation is forbidden as a simulation runtime. Oracle-only placement is legal, but then it competes with two cheaper exact objects and loses.
- FINE-GRAINED OVER LUMPED (the top-line architectural rule, PI 2026-05-19): the only route to a finite MPO is linearizing or freezing s -> A(s)^{-1}b(s). Row-by-row, that is the same species of substitution as Metropolis-for-Bell or a single two-head spring for a Stam-Hocky minifilament: a mechanistic global process replaced by a lumped proxy. Forbidden for runtime; permissible only as a PI-ratified acceptance oracle.
- NO EMPIRICAL MAGIC NUMBERS: chi, the truncation threshold, and the bary_t / abscissa bin widths are tractability-chosen constants. They CAN pass the Magic-Number Block via grid-invariance and 1/chi extrapolation, so this rule is satisfiable — but it converts the deliverable from a clean exact number into a convergence study, which removes the elegance that motivates the proposal.
- NO GATE-LOOSENING: the locality decision rule must be written before the measurement. Also note the temptation this design creates: an exact-labelled MPS probability would be an attractive way to declare a distributional gate passed while the underlying inner solve is still at residual/tension 15.5 percent. That is gate substitution, and it is the precise pattern the audit that commissioned this work exists to prevent.
- VALIDATE AT FULL NATIVE POPULATION (PI 2026-07-09 / 2026-07-16): MPS results would exist only on the 320-head slice; the 8840-head native cortex needs 19 TB at a chi that is still inexact. A conclusion drawn from the slice is non-authoritative by rule, and the slice's own quantitative claim is currently BLOCKED.
- PHYSIOLOGICAL BASELINE: the proposal's compression targets the discrete layer, which is under 0.1 percent of step cost. It cannot help reach the physiological baseline, whose blocker is the unconverged 1.5M-DOF mechanical solve.
- PI PRIORITY 2 (magnitudes are NOT the gate): an MPS steady-state distribution is only evaluable once k_on, k_off0, f_stall, f0, k_xb and the four catch-slip constants are all fixed, and every one is an unresolved GAP. By the PI's own stated criterion this is a BAD measurement right now: it cannot be evaluated without unsourced constants. The J-sensitivity measurement recommended instead is dimensionless (normalized decay exponent, effective rank, Frobenius block ratio) and ratio-swept, which is a GOOD measurement by the same criterion. This asymmetry, more than any cost figure, is why the recommended step is the J matrix and not the tensor network.
- PI PRIORITY 1 (mechanical connectedness is the gate): J restricted to cross-component blocks is a direct connectedness instrument, and a structurally zero block would prove co-location-without-connection. That is why the deciding experiment should be run even though the design it was meant to decide is rejected.
open_questions_for_pi: Do you want the J-sensitivity matrix built as a standing instrument regardless of this REJECT? It is the cheapest quantitative answer available to your priority-1 gate (does compartment A actually deform compartment B?), it needs no sourced constant, it reuses the existing solve plus compute_loads with zero new physics, and a structurally zero cross-component block would prove co-location-without-connection — a failure mode the current instrument set cannot detect at all.

Do you want the permutation-symmetric COUNT-SPACE master equation (N+1 states per minifilament, exact under head exchangeability, load(n) tabulated by N+1 real solves) built as an acceptance oracle in validation/oracles/? It strictly generalizes ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py, which currently assumes head independence, and it answers the one genuinely open exactness question in this area: whether load-sharing catch bonds show a real finite-N transition or a mean-field artifact. Cost is milliseconds to about 1.4 s, versus hours to never for MPS.

A by-product finding that needs your call because it is load-bearing for ANY treatment of the discrete layer, tensor-network or not: with the landed f_stall = 0.5 pN and k_xb = 1000 pN/um (both GAPs), the crossbridge stall extension is f_stall/k_xb = 0.5 nm, which is about 10x SMALLER than a single myosin lever-arm power stroke (about 5 nm, Veigel/Finer). The abscissa accumulator therefore never completes one physical step before stalling. Both constants are GAPs so this is a RATIO observation, not a magnitude claim — but if the ratio is wrong then the per-head step-and-stall mechanism is operating below its own step quantum and the fine-grained head model is not resolving what it claims to resolve. Which of the two constants do you want re-sourced first?

The CellTransaction global accept predicate is hard-wired to 1 in the landed SF gate (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:497), so the architecture's designed global coupling of every discrete commit to one whole-cell force-balance scalar is not currently exercised, and assemble_balance still has no declared tolerance anywhere in code or docs. Do you want that tolerance derived and the predicate turned on before further slices land? It changes the correlation structure of the entire discrete layer (it makes every head's commit conditional on a global functional) and no current measurement would notice it being wrong.

Confirm the adjacent idea is closed and separate: QTT / tensor-train compression of the MECHANICAL field to accelerate the 1.5M-DOF solve is a DIFFERENT proposal from compressing the binding state space. I judge it also negative (unstructured graph at 7 nodes per fiber, stiffness contrast 4.6e5 versus 1e3 pN/um, and a prior closed audit finding the native solve CG-dominated with a ~9 percent ceiling and a do-not-retry verdict), but I want it explicitly recorded as separately closed so a future session does not read this REJECT as covering it, or read its non-coverage as an opening.

result.family: FAMILY 4 — how kinetic and state quantities are measured (bound-head fraction, duty ratio, event rates, abscissa/power-stroke, PopulationLedger disjointness, and the accepted-step transaction predicate)

instruments.name: bound-head fraction (the GATE-B headline: 0 -> 85.24%)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The physiological bound-head duty ratio of the NMII population — the quantity Kovacs 2003 / Nagy 2013 report as ~0.1 (NM2A) / 0.2-0.3 (NM2B).
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: int(bound_d.numpy().sum()) — a POST-COMMIT host readback of the count of int32 flags == 1, divided by ALL 8,840 allocated heads, on a run where accepted_d is a constant ones array. The denominator includes heads that are geometrically unable to bind (outside the 0.05 um capture radius), and the reachable subset is never counted. It is a saturation fraction of an unmeasured reachable set, not a duty ratio.
instruments.evidence: bound_d is written only by attach_segment_gated_r0bind_kernel and step_detach_segment_gated_catch_slip_kernel (segment_motor.py:393-458, 186-237); both early-return on accepted[0]==0 and are launched only inside FilamentMotorConnector.commit_irreversible (cortex_motor_slice.py:550-596), which CellTransaction.step invokes exactly once per outer step — so the RISE IS genuinely kinetic and once-per-physical-step. That part is sound. But the committed artifact records 7,535/8,840 = 85.2376%, while the analytic ceiling for the same constants is phi_b = k_on/(k_on+k_catch0+k_slip0) = 50/(50+0.35+0.35) = 0.9862. The 13-point gap is entirely out-of-capture heads, and no array reports how many heads are reachable (query_seg_id_d >= 0 is never counted). The driver's own docstring predicted '~50-65%' from '~60% of heads within capture'; the run returned 85% and nothing reconciled the two.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: (a) Re-run with k_on -> 1e-9 (0 is refused by _require_param, cortex_motor_slice.py:172-184) leaving the query untouched: bound_d must stay identically 0 while count(query_seg_id_d >= 0) stays at its normal value. That separates event-driven binding from query-driven binding — currently nothing does. (b) Report n_reachable each step and check n_bound/n_reachable -> k_on/(k_on+k_off(F_bar)) to within stochastic spread.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Report three numbers, not one: n_reachable/n_heads (a geometry/placement observable), n_bound/n_reachable (phi_b, the duty, compared against the analytic identity in ac/motor/bell_kinetics_analytic.py), and n_bound/n_heads (the raw saturation). Only the middle one may be called a duty ratio or compared to literature.

instruments.name: t0 zero-bound baseline in the cortex GATE-B lane
instruments.what_its_name_implies: 'starting from ZERO bound heads' / 'tension is exactly zero while no head is bound' — a measured negative control anchoring the emergence claim.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing. The first telemetry row is printed AFTER slc.step() has already run one commit. There is no pre-loop measurement of bound_d, gamma, or max|PF|. The zero-baseline claim rests on the config flag resting_bound_myosin_fraction=None plus a code-reading assertion in the docstring.
instruments.evidence: The loop body is: slc.step(...) THEN n_bound = slc.bound_head_count() THEN rep = _measure_gamma(...). No row precedes the first step. Contrast the SF gate (scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:481-495) which measures REST explicitly and raises SystemExit('heads are pre-bound at t0 — the emergence claim would be void') if it is violated. Two sibling gates, one with a hard-failing negative control and one with none.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: The control IS the missing measurement: emit a step-0 row (bound, gamma_source, gamma_network, gamma_total, max|PF|) before the loop and hard-fail if bound != 0 or gamma_source > float-noise.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Copy the SF gate's REST block verbatim into the cortex driver and promote it to a verdict boolean written into the artifact, not a printed line.

instruments.name: the (bound-count, tension) row pairing in the SF gate trace
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Row s reports the bound population and the tension that population is holding — the co-measured pair the causal claim rests on.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Two quantities ONE ACCEPTED STEP OUT OF PHASE. n_bound is read after commit_irreversible (end of step s). Tension/traction/residual are computed from positions and forces produced by the inner solve, which ran with the binding state from the END OF STEP s-1. The record proves it: step 1 reports n_bound = 113 with T_abs_max = 0.0.
instruments.evidence: CellTransaction.step order (transaction.py:113-154) is snapshot -> propose_events -> solve() -> ledger -> finalize(rollback+commit) -> clock.advance. The attach kernel fires inside finalize, i.e. after the solve whose geometry the tension is read from. trace[0] = {n_bound: 113, T_abs_max_pN: 0.0} is exactly this artifact. head_load_max IS in phase with T (compute_loads runs inside the inner wrapper, sf_motor path), so the tension_exceeds_single_head_load oracle is internally consistent — only the n_bound column is shifted.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Record bound_pre (before commit) and bound_post (after commit) in the same row and assert bound_pre[s] == bound_post[s-1]. Any driver that only records one of them cannot detect the shift.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Emit bound_pre alongside every mechanical observable and use bound_pre for all causal pairings; keep bound_post only for the kinetic event bookkeeping.

instruments.name: verdict claim `tension_zero_while_no_head_is_bound`
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A measured causal control: on every step with zero bound heads the tension is below 1e-9 pN, so tension cannot come from anything but the motor.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing. `unbound_steps = bound_series == 0` selects the empty set (step 1 already reports 113 because of the phase shift above), and the code falls through to `else True`. The claim passed with zero applicable samples.
instruments.evidence: trace[].n_bound = [113,184,238,266,287,301] — never 0. The expression is `bool(np.all(tension_series[unbound_steps] < 1e-9)) if unbound_steps.any() else True`.
