The project has ALREADY caught this: GATE_B_sf_motor.yaml states 'In the committed record NO trace row has n_bound == 0 ... this claim is VACUOUSLY true there. The verifier flags it VACUOUS. A claim with zero applicable samples is not evidence.' What the contract does NOT diagnose is the root cause — the post-commit/pre-commit phase shift, not a genuinely fast first step. Recording bound_pre would make step 1 read bound=0, T~1e-14, and the oracle would become live.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A vacuity guard in the verdict machinery itself: any claim whose sample count is 0 must evaluate to FAIL (or to a distinct third state), never to True. Additionally the REST row already supplies the evidence this claim wants (rest.T_abs_max_pN = 5.55e-14 at rest.n_bound = 0) — it should be the measure path.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Replace the conditional-series measure with `all_of([rest.n_bound == 0, rest.T_abs_max_pN < eps])` plus a live per-step version driven by bound_pre; and make empty-sample claims fail closed.

instruments.name: duty ratio
instruments.where: declared at /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/motor/bell_kinetics_analytic.py:200-245 (analytic phi_b) and /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/motor/resting_setpoint.py:60-70 (imposed setpoint); no runtime measurement anywhere
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The engine measures an emergent duty ratio and can compare it to Kovacs 2003 / Nagy 2013.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: There is no duty-ratio instrument in any runtime path. Two things exist and neither is a measurement: (1) closed forms phi_b = k_on/(k_on+k_off0) and its catch-slip variant, present as analytic cross-checks and never evaluated against a run; (2) RestingBoundMyosinSetpoint.fraction — an IMPOSED duty, source-gated and default-off, correctly left unset in GATE B (resting_bound_myosin_fraction=None).
instruments.evidence: grep over ac/ and scripts/ finds no code that computes measured_bound_fraction and compares it to steady_bound_fraction()/catch_slip phi_b. The one gate that computes both (ac/motor/native_gates/ng1_two_filament_stall.py) reports phi_b_analytic in its result dict and then tests against a hand-picked floor instead (see next entry). The comparison the whole family needs is one line away and is not made.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: The oracle IS the control: at fixed k_on/k_off and zero load the reachable-subset bound fraction must equal k_on/(k_on+k_off0) within binomial spread; under load it must move in the CATCH direction (up to F*) for CATCH_SLIP and DOWN monotonically for SLIP. Running both detach modes on the same geometry and confirming the duty moves in OPPOSITE directions is a magnitude-free sign test that no current run performs.
instruments.canonical_replacement: A DutyLedger contributor that emits (n_reachable, n_bound_pre, n_attach_events, n_detach_events, mean_bell_load) per accepted step, plus a gate asserting phi_b_measured == phi_b_analytic(mean_bell_load) within spread and asserting the CATCH_SLIP-vs-SLIP sign inversion.

instruments.name: NG-1 `phi_b_emergent` gate (bound_fraction >= 0.70)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A validated emergent bound fraction — proof that the duty emerges from k_on/k_off rather than being imposed.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A one-sided pass if the tick-averaged bound fraction exceeds an undrived 0.70, while the analytic phi_b (~0.99) sits unused in the same result dict. The gate cannot fail the most important failure mode in this family: a KMC where detachment never fires returns bound_fraction = 1.00 and PASSES.
instruments.evidence: `BOUND_FRAC_LO = 0.70  # emergent phi_b ~ 0.99; allow KMC / mid-cycle spread` — a threshold with no derivation, chosen wide enough to pass, in a codebase whose own audit calls a gate written so a broken build cannot fail it 'worse than an ungated result'. The dict already carries phi_b_analytic from ref.two_filament_isometric(), printed at :358 and never compared. bound_frac is also a mean over ALL ticks including the transient rise, not a steady-state estimator.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Set k_off0 -> 0 (or x_slip -> 0 so the hazard cannot rise): bound_fraction goes to 1.000 and the current gate PASSES. A two-sided band |phi_b_measured - phi_b_analytic| <= binomial 3-sigma fails it immediately.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Two-sided comparison against phi_b_analytic computed from the same k_on/k_off actually loaded into the device struct, with the band derived from binomial sampling error at N_heads and N_ticks (a derivable, not chosen, tolerance); and estimate the fraction over the post-transient window only.

instruments.name: event rates (attach/detach) — the event COUNTER
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The ledger's topology channel counts bonds formed and broken per accepted step, and the NMII connector declares 'binding'/'unbinding'/'stepping' event channels.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing is ever counted. `add_topology_delta` has ZERO production callers (only tests/ac/engine/test_ledger.py). No attach or detach event is ever tallied — only the net resulting bound count is observable. The declared event channels are validated by a STRING SET DIFFERENCE (`NMII_CONNECTOR_EVENT_CHANNELS - connector.event_channels`, nmii_actuator.py:631) with no numeric channel behind them, so a runtime passes the 'has binding/unbinding events' contract while emitting none.
instruments.evidence: grep add_topology_delta over ac/ and scripts/ returns only ledger.py's own definition/docstrings. Same for add_cell_traction. Because only the net count is visible, attach-then-detach within one tick is invisible — and the kernels make that a real occurrence: a head attached by attach_segment_gated_r0bind_kernel is immediately eligible for step_detach_segment_gated_catch_slip_kernel in the SAME commit launch sequence.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: An integer conservation law needing no parameter: N_attach - N_detach must equal delta(bound_count) EXACTLY on every accepted step. If only the net count is recorded this identity cannot be posed at all, so any bookkeeping error is undetectable.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Two device int32 counters per connector, incremented inside the accepted-gated attach and detach kernels, reduced into topology_counts_d, with the N_attach - N_detach == delta(bound) identity as a per-step assertion and the per-unit-time rates as the reported observable.

instruments.name: event rates — the state-conditioned rate FIELD (CellState -> propose_events)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Rates are local, state-conditioned fields set by CellState and consumed by each participant's propose_events — the ratified state-conditioned Event Runtime.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing. CellState 'ships with EMPTY registries' by its own docstring. Every native driver calls slice.step(...) which forwards rates=None, and BOTH implementations of propose_events (FilamentMotorConnector, ERMCortexConnector) ignore the rates argument entirely. Every kinetic rate in the running system is a compile-time scalar baked into a Warp struct (NMIIHandParams.k_on, NMIICatchSlipParams.k_catch0/...).
instruments.evidence: transaction.py:92 `rates: object | None = None`; cortex_motor_slice.py:538 signature takes `rates` and the body never reads it; cell_state.py docstring: 'The first ratified instance ships with EMPTY registries.' So the layer that would make rates measurable, state-dependent, and sweepable is inert — which matters directly for the PI's long-run inference goal, where rates are the parameters to be inferred.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A conformance test that drives propose_events with a rates object whose lookup RAISES: any proposer that passes is proven not to consult it. Today every proposer would pass.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Make the rate a device field the proposer must gather from (per-head or per-site), source it through CellState.rate(component, reaction), and have the kernel read the field rather than a struct scalar — that also makes rate sweeps a data change rather than a recompile.

instruments.name: kinetics-per-accepted-step vs kinetics-per-solver-iteration
instruments.what_its_name_implies: One outer physical clock plus a converged inner solve; solver iterations are never time.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: This is the one thing in Family 4 that is genuinely SOUND and is measured, not asserted. Every kinetic mutation lives inside commit_irreversible, launched once per CellTransaction.step, and every KMC kernel early-returns on accepted[0]==0. The clock kernel increments event_time and accepted_step_index only when accepted[0] != 0, on-device. The SF gate MEASURES it: clock.after - clock.before == clock.steps (6 == 6). Had the clock or the KMC been driven per inner iteration the delta would have read steps x newton and the claim would have failed.
instruments.evidence: attach/detach kernels appear exactly once in FilamentMotorConnector.commit_irreversible (cortex_motor_slice.py:564-596); accumulate_candidate (per-iteration) launches only geometry refresh + the crossbridge force, no state mutation except walk_dir_d which is recomputed at the top of every call. advance_event_clock_kernel gates on accepted[0]. Verdict record: clock_advanced_once_per_accepted_step = true. Answer to the PI's first specific question: NO kinetic measurement is contaminated by solver-iteration count — and unusually, there is an instrument that would have caught it if it were.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Already implemented and passing: clock delta == requested step count (catches iteration-as-time), plus clock_did_not_advance on an injected rejected step (catches ungated advance). This pair is the template guard for every other family.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None needed. Promote the clock-delta assertion from the SF driver into CellTransaction's own test surface so every future slice inherits it.

instruments.name: abscissa (accumulated power stroke)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The accumulated power stroke of a myosin head — a cumulative mechanochemical state advanced only on accepted physical steps.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A PER-BINDING-EPISODE displacement, in um, reset to 0.0 on every detach and on every re-attach, clipped by a k_xb- and f_stall-dependent bound. It is advanced only inside the accepted-gated detach kernel, so its clock is correct. But (a) nothing accumulates it across episodes, so there is no cumulative-stroke or motor-work observable at all; (b) da_max = max(0, (f_stall - loads_hill)/k_xb) makes the measured stroke a function of two PI-GAP magnitudes (f_stall, k_xb) plus v0 and kappa; (c) a head that attaches in step s is advanced in the SAME commit using loads_hill[h] == 0, because compute_loads ran before the attach and explicitly zeroes unbound heads — so every freshly bound head takes a full UNLOADED stroke tau*v0 on its first tick.
instruments.evidence: abscissa[h] = wp.float64(0.0) on attach (segment_motor.py:437) and on detach (:180, :234). compute_head_loads_segment_split_r0bind_kernel:520-527 sets loads[h]=0 and loads_full[h]=0 for bound[h]==0. commit_irreversible launches attach THEN detach in one sequence (cortex_motor_slice.py:564-591), so within one commit a newly-bound head sees the zeroed loads. The first-tick bias is systematic and scales with the attach rate: at k_on=50/s, dt=0.01, P_attach ~ 0.39 per reachable free head per step, so a large fraction of the population takes an unloaded stroke every step during the rise.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: dt-halving: the stroke accumulated per unit BIOLOGICAL time must be dt-invariant. With the current attach-then-step-in-one-tick ordering, halving dt halves the number of spurious unloaded first strokes per unit time, so the measured mean stroke rate will move — a magnitude-free discriminator requiring no sourced constant.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Split the commit: attach in step s, first Hill advance in step s+1 (or recompute loads for newly attached heads before advancing). Add a cumulative abscissa_total_d (never reset) and an event-count-weighted mean stroke as the reported observable, so 'accumulated power stroke' names something accumulated.

instruments.name: atp_consumed_d / atp_cycle_state_d (the motor energy channel)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The engine tracks ATP hydrolysis per head and total ATP consumed — the declared 'atp' ledger channel of NMII_LEDGER_CHANNELS.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing. Both arrays are allocated, dtype/shape validated, listed as authoritative mutable state, D2D-snapshotted every step and reject-restored every step — and NEVER WRITTEN BY ANY KERNEL. The whole transaction machinery faithfully protects a counter that is structurally always zero.
instruments.evidence: grep atp_consumed / atp_cycle_state across ac/ returns only allocation, validation, and snapshot/rollback wiring — no wp.launch writes either array. Consequence: the strongest available magnitude-free oracle for an active motor — a first-law check that mechanical work delivered by the crossbridges is bounded by (ATP events) x (free energy per hydrolysis), and that both scale together — is impossible to pose.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A liveness assertion of the form 'a declared ledger channel must be nonzero after N accepted steps in which the corresponding events fired'. Today the channel-conformance check is a string set-difference and would pass a permanently-zero counter.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Increment atp_consumed_d inside the accepted-gated detach kernel (one hydrolysis per completed stroke), reduce it into the ledger's work/atp channels, and add the work-vs-ATP scaling oracle (a ratio, so magnitude-free in the PI's sense).

instruments.name: PopulationLedger unique-ID disjointness — the BUILD-TIME invariant
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Every physical filament belongs to exactly one component; a filament counted twice is a rejected build.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: At build time: exactly that, and it is one of the best structural instruments in the tree. It rejects overlapping ID blocks AND overlapping active IDs, refuses duplicate component names, and PopulationLedger.allocate raises rather than growing capacity to hit a target density (the no-resample rule made structural). The census pattern of reporting N_unique_sf_fibers AND N_sf_fibers_summed side by side is exemplary: a double-count shows up as a visible discrepancy rather than as a silently-correct number.
instruments.evidence: sf_population.py:513-514,585 and sf_nmii_population.py:314-319 seed and then assert_invariants at build. tests/ac/engine/test_sf_population.py:61-69 constructs an overlapping-block clash and confirms rejection. The committed SF record carries population_ledgers_disjoint = {sf_arc: block [1000000,1000040] active 40, nmii: block [3000000,3000016] active 16}. This is the project's genuine conversion of a failure mode into structure — at build time.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Present and passing: the deliberate overlapping-block ledger in the test suite. Extend it with a duplicate ACTIVE id across non-overlapping blocks (which the function also rejects) so both branches are covered.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None at build time. See the next entry for the runtime half.

instruments.name: PopulationLedger disjointness — the PER-ACCEPTED-STEP invariant
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The no-double-count invariant is promoted from a viz-time check to a hot-loop invariant, re-asserted after every accepted step.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A constant. No production code path calls allocate(), release(), or sever() — only tests do — and no device-side bitmap or free-list exists anywhere in the tree, despite population.py:20 asserting 'the native lane mirrors it with device bitmaps / free-lists'. So the host `_active` sets cannot change during a run, and the per-step assertion re-tests literal constant ID blocks (0 / 1e6 / 2e6 / 3e6). It also does NOT call assert_invariants(), so active+dormant == capacity is not re-checked. It is an O(N) pure-Python frozenset copy plus loop executed inside the physical-time loop for provably zero information — and in the headline 70,686-filament cortex GATE-B run it never executes at all, because that driver passes no population_ledgers.
instruments.evidence: grep for allocate()/release()/sever() across ffn_sim/ hits only population.py itself and tests/. grep for free_list/bitmap/active_mask across ac/engine and ac/cell hits only population.py's own docstrings. active_ids returns frozenset(self._active) — a full copy of 70,686 ints per call. build_cortex_motor_slice defaults population_ledgers=() and ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py never overrides it. Separately, the ID namespace mixes cortex F-actin filaments, ECM collagen SEGMENTS and NMII MINIFILAMENTS, so 'one physical filament, one component' is not the proposition being checked.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Inject a device-side double-claim (have two components' commit kernels both mark the same global id active) and confirm the per-step assertion fires. It cannot, because the assertion never reads device state. That is the whole finding.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Either (a) make it real: a device int32 owner-id array over the global ID space, written by every component's accepted commit, with a per-step kernel asserting no id has two owners and reducing active+dormant == capacity — cost O(N) on-device, not on-host; or (b) demote it honestly to a build-time-only invariant and delete the per-step call. Keeping an O(N) host loop in the hot path that cannot fail is the worst of both.

instruments.name: the accepted-step transaction predicate (the acceptance gate itself)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: One device-resident physical acceptance predicate decides whether a candidate step commits; irreversible kinetics land only on an accepted (converged, force-balanced) step.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: In every run banked so far: nothing. Three independent reasons. (1) The DEFAULT predicate is ledger.balance_ok_d = |reaction_resultant + traction_resultant|^2 <= tol^2, and add_cell_traction has ZERO production callers while add_far_field_reaction is called only by ecm_world — so in every motor slice both channels are identically zero and 0 <= tol evaluates TRUE unconditionally. (2) GlobalCellLedger.reset() has zero callers, so the accumulators are never zeroed between steps: the moment a channel IS filled, the 'residual' becomes a running sum over the whole run rather than a per-step residual. (3) Every native driver bypasses it: accepted_d = wp.array(ones). The cortex driver's --balance-gate flag raises SystemExit rather than faking a predicate — an honest refusal, but it means no run has ever exercised a conditional accept.
instruments.evidence: ledger.py:130-148 computes r = reaction[0] + traction[0] and sets balance_ok = 1 if dot(r,r) <= tol_sq[0]. grep add_cell_traction over ac/ and scripts/ returns only its own definition and tests/ac/engine/test_ledger.py. grep '\.reset()' over ac/ returns only ac/cell/driver.py:605 (an Anderson accelerator, unrelated). ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:509 accepted_ones; ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:497 accepted_d = ones; ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:232 accepted_d = ones. No tol_sq_d is supplied by any driver, and no squared-force tolerance is declared anywhere in code or docs. DIRECT ANSWER to the PI's third question: yes — irreversible Bell/catch-slip commits are landing on unconverged steps, and the SF record proves it self-consistently: residual_over_tension = 0.1553 with inner_solve_converged_relative_to_tension = false, in the same run whose 6 accepted steps all committed the KMC.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A POSITIVE control the gate currently lacks: feed a deliberately unbalanced ledger (nonzero traction, zero reaction) and confirm balance_ok goes to 0 and the step rolls back. Today that path has never run. Also: assert at construction that at least one contributor fills each channel the predicate consumes, so a 0-vs-0 comparison is a rejected build, not a silent pass.
instruments.canonical_replacement: For a slice with no ECM, the predicate must be a CONVERGENCE predicate, not a force-balance one — the SF gate already computes the right dimensionless quantity (max|F| on free nodes / max|T|, i.e. residual_over_tension) but only as a post-hoc report field. Move it on-device as the accepted_d source. The honest consequence must be accepted: at the present explicit relax no step would be accepted and no kinetics would commit, which is exactly the information the current force-accept hides.

instruments.name: rejected-step rollback / bit-restoration of the binding SoA
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A rejected step advances no kinetic counter and no clock; the binding state is bit-restored.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that, on real device data — the best-evidenced measurement in the project. The SF native gate injects a genuinely rejected step (rejected_d = zeros) and checks with np.array_equal that bound_d, seg_id_d and abscissa_d are byte-identical, that BOTH position arrays are byte-identical, and that the accepted-step clock did not advance. All four true in the committed record. Structurally it is also correct: every field in authoritative_pairs() (bound, seg_id, seg_a, seg_b, bary_t, abscissa, walk_dir, rng_epoch) plus r0_bind is snapshotted, and every mutation of them lives inside a kernel that early-returns on accepted[0]==0. ANSWER to the PI's second question: no, a rejected step cannot leave a kinetic counter advanced.
instruments.evidence: rollback_detail = {binding_soa_restored: true, sf_position_bit_restored: true, nmii_position_bit_restored: true, clock_did_not_advance: true}. The driver's own comment is the reason this is trustworthy: 'the slice docstring claims the SF/NMII POSITIONS are bit-restored on rejection too — check it, do not take the claim on trust (the inner solve moves both arrays, so this is the load-bearing half).' Three residual gaps, none load-bearing today but all real: (i) loads_hill_d/loads_bell_d and the attach scratch query_seg_id_d/query_t_d/query_barbed_d are NOT snapshotted, so after a rejected step they hold values derived from a discarded geometry — and they are precisely the inputs the irreversible commit consumes, so they belong in the transaction; (ii) SegmentMotorConnectorRuntime.rollback copies UNCONDITIONALLY, ignoring `accepted`, while the sibling _ActuatorStateTransaction.rollback uses reject-gated kernels — two rollback semantics inside one slice, safe only because walk_dir_d (the sole SoA field the inner solve mutates) is recomputed at the top of every accumulate_candidate; (iii) the CPU test exercises only the reject branch (tests/ac/engine/test_cortex_motor_slice.py:432-444), so a regression that made the accept-branch overwrite matter would not be caught.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Present and passing for the load-bearing half. Missing: run the same rollback assertion with accepted=1 and assert the converged candidate SURVIVES bit-for-bit where it should (the dual control), and extend the byte-equality set to loads_* and query_* after adding them to authoritative_pairs().
instruments.canonical_replacement: Keep the instrument; extend the snapshot set to every array the irreversible commit READS as well as writes, gate the connector rollback on the predicate for symmetry with the state-owner, and add the accept-branch dual control.

instruments.name: r0_bind (per-head attach-unstrained crossbridge reference)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A physical zero-strain length grounded in the bind geometry that removes the coarse-mesh placement artifact resolution-independently — 'never a tuned magnitude'.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The along-walk projection of the head-to-attachment offset evaluated at a DIFFERENT time than the binding decision. The attach candidate (segment id, barycentric t, barbed direction, and the capture-radius admissibility) is computed in propose_events on PRE-solve geometry; r0_bind is captured in commit_irreversible from POST-solve port_pos. Nothing checks that the head is still within capture_radius after the solve, so r0_bind silently absorbs an arbitrarily large offset as 'zero strain' — which is the same artifact class it was introduced to remove, just relocated from the force to the reference.
instruments.evidence: FilamentMotorConnector.propose_events calls fill_attach_scratch(self._actuator_view(), self._port) at pre-solve time; attach_segment_gated_r0bind_kernel:449-451 computes x_att from the post-solve port_pos and actuator_pos. There is no assertion anywhere that |r0_bind| <= capture_radius. Worse, the reference test INSTITUTIONALIZES the inadmissible case: it loops over offsets (0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2) um against a capture radius of 0.05 um (test line 263) and asserts the passive force is zero 'no matter the coarse-mesh placement offset' — certifying correct arithmetic for a head bound 4x outside its own capture reach.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A post-solve admissibility assertion: for every head that transitioned free->bound this step, |r0_bind| <= capture_radius (and, stricter, the head-to-segment distance on the post-solve geometry <= capture_radius). Any head failing it should not have bound. This is a pure geometry check with no magnitude input beyond the capture radius the model already declares.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Re-run the capture test inside the accepted attach kernel against post-solve geometry (the positions are already arguments), reject the bind if it fails, and count rejected-for-drift binds as an observable. Change the reference test's offset sweep to end at capture_radius and add an explicit test that an offset beyond capture is REFUSED.

instruments.name: crosslink KMC kinetic sanity-gate set (host oracle)
instruments.where: /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/weave/crosslink_kmc.py:1-40 (Sanity Gate block), assert_single_channel; wired only at /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/weave/woven_cell.py:368
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A host NumPy oracle for load-dependent crosslinker turnover with a detailed-balance check.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Genuinely what it says, and it is the best-DESIGNED kinetic instrument set in the tree even though it is an oracle rather than a runtime path. Its four oracles are all magnitude-free: unloaded steady bound fraction -> k_on/(k_on+k_off0) (detailed balance, an identity); crosslinker count invariant across the run (conservation); off-rate monotone in |load| (sign-sense); and — the one nothing else in the project has — 'the bound-pair SET differs from the initial set while the bound COUNT is steady', which distinguishes genuine reattachment from on/off flicker. It also carries an explicit double-count guard (assert_single_channel refuses kmc_reattach and r0_creep simultaneously).
instruments.evidence: The Sanity Gate docstring lists all four plus the single-channel guard, and tests/ac/weave/test_crosslink_kmc_oracle.py exercises them. Caveat on reach, not on soundness: assert_single_channel is called only from ac/weave/woven_cell.py:368; the engine lane and the native drivers never invoke it, while xl_turnover_kernel (the competing r0_creep channel) is launched from ff/ecm_mechanics.py:800, ff/network_warp.py:1371, ac/engine/intermediate_filament_rig.py:923 and two scripts — so the double-count guard exists but does not cover the paths that could double-count.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Present: the guard test enables both channels and asserts a raise. Missing: an equivalent guard at the engine/driver level covering the xl_turnover_kernel call sites.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None for the oracle. Port its four-oracle pattern verbatim to the NMII head KMC (detailed balance vs phi_b, head-count conservation, off-rate monotonicity/catch-sign, and bound-PAIR-set turnover at steady count) and lift assert_single_channel to the engine's dispatch layer.

instruments.name: NMII ledger contribution (accumulate_ledger in the production runtime)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Each NMII participant pushes its force / work / atp / population device terms into the GlobalCellLedger before the acceptance predicate is evaluated (NMII_LEDGER_CHANNELS = {force, work, atp, population}).
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing, and it leaks. The SHIPPED production implementation of accumulate_ledger for both NMII participants is `self.ledger_calls.append(ledger)` — a spy recorder left in the runtime — and _ActuatorStateTransaction.commit_irreversible does `self.commit_calls.append((accepted, dt_phys, rng_seed))`. Two unbounded host lists grow by one entry per accepted step inside the physical-time loop, and zero numbers reach any ledger channel. This is the mechanism behind the tautological balance gate above.
instruments.evidence: cortex_motor_slice.py:346-348 docstring: 'Record the ledger handle without deciding acceptance' — the body is a list append. nmii_actuator.py:1118-1120: 'Record the ledger handle; force/work/ATP/population reduction lands with the two-array kernel' — no such kernel is launched anywhere. The channel-conformance check (nmii_actuator.py:486-488) is `missing = NMII_LEDGER_CHANNELS - channels`, a string set difference, so declaring the labels satisfies the contract.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A liveness check in CellWorldTransaction.accumulate_ledgers: after N accepted steps, every declared channel of every contributor must have received at least one nonzero reduction, else raise. Today a contributor that declares all four channels and emits none passes every gate in the tree.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Real reductions: motor force resultant -> add_force_resultant, crossbridge work -> add_work, ATP events -> add_mass/atp channel, bound/attach/detach counts -> add_topology_delta; delete the spy lists from the production classes and keep them only in the test doubles.

magnitude_free_oracles: DUTY IDENTITY (the single highest-value missing oracle): on the reachable subset, n_bound/n_reachable must equal k_on/(k_on + k_off(F_bar)) within binomial 3-sigma at the run's own k_on and k_off — an identity that holds for ANY magnitudes, so it needs no sourced constant. The closed form already exists at ac/motor/bell_kinetics_analytic.py; it is computed and printed in ng1 and never used as the oracle.

CATCH-vs-SLIP SIGN INVERSION: run the identical geometry under SegmentDetachKinetics.CATCH_SLIP and .SLIP and require the steady bound fraction to move in OPPOSITE directions with load (up to F* for catch, monotonically down for slip). Pure sign test; catches a detach law wired to the wrong hazard.

NULL-RATE CONTROL: k_on -> 1e-9 with the attach query untouched must give bound_d identically 0 while count(query_seg_id_d >= 0) is unchanged. Separates event-driven binding from query/capture-driven binding. Note k_on = 0 is currently refused by _require_param, so the null must be approached, not set.
EVENT-COUNT CONSERVATION: N_attach - N_detach == delta(bound_count) EXACTLY on every accepted step. An integer identity, no parameter. Unposeable today because no event is counted.

dt-INVARIANCE: halving dt_phys must leave the steady bound fraction unchanged (it is a rate ratio, not a per-tick probability) and must leave attach/detach events PER UNIT BIOLOGICAL TIME unchanged. Catches Poisson-per-tick discretization error and, independently, the attach-then-step-in-one-tick unloaded-stroke bias.

CLOCK-DELTA: clock.accepted_step_index delta == number of accepted steps, and == 0 across an injected rejected step. Already implemented in the SF gate; the one instrument in the project that would catch solver-iterations-treated-as-time. Promote to CellTransaction's own contract.

BIT-RESTORE ON REJECT (and its dual on accept): every array in authoritative_pairs() byte-identical (np.array_equal) after a rejected step, and the converged candidate byte-identical-to-itself after an accepted step. Extend the covered set to loads_hill/loads_bell and the query_* attach scratch, which the irreversible commit reads.

REJECT-THEN-RETRY DETERMINISM: a step rejected and re-run at the same dt must reproduce the identical binding decision, because rng_epoch did not advance. Claimed in events.py's docstring; never measured.

CAPTURE ADMISSIBILITY: every head transitioning free->bound must satisfy |r0_bind| <= capture_radius on the POST-solve geometry. Pure geometry, no magnitude beyond a radius the model already declares.

POPULATION CONSERVATION: active_count + dormant_count == capacity every accepted step (PopulationLedger.assert_invariants, which the per-step path currently skips), and no global id claimed by two components — the latter checked against DEVICE owner state, not the immutable host mirror.

LEDGER POSITIVE CONTROL: assemble_balance with a nonzero traction and zero reaction must set balance_ok = 0 and the step must roll back. Proves the acceptance gate can fail at all; it has never been exercised.

CHANNEL LIVENESS: any declared event/ledger channel must have emitted at least one nonzero value after N accepted steps, else the build is rejected. Replaces the current string-set-difference conformance check.

WORK-vs-ATP SCALING: crossbridge mechanical work and ATP hydrolysis events must scale together, with work per event bounded by the hydrolysis free energy. A ratio, so magnitude-free — and impossible today because atp_consumed_d is never written.

VACUITY GUARD: any verdict claim evaluated over an empty sample set must FAIL (or report a distinct third state), never default to True. This one guard alone converts tension_zero_while_no_head_is_bound from a passing tautology into a live oracle.
missing_instruments: A reachable-head counter (count of query_seg_id_d >= 0) — without it the 85.24% bound fraction cannot be decomposed into placement geometry vs kinetic duty, and cannot be compared to any literature duty ratio.

Attach and detach EVENT counters per accepted step. GlobalCellLedger.add_topology_delta and topology_counts_d exist with zero production callers; NMII_CONNECTOR_EVENT_CHANNELS = {stepping, binding, unbinding} is validated as a string set only.

Any measured-vs-analytic duty comparison. The closed forms exist (ac/motor/bell_kinetics_analytic.py); no run evaluates them against a measurement. ng1 computes phi_b_analytic into the same dict as the measurement and then gates on an undrived 0.70 floor instead.
A t0 / pre-loop baseline row in the cortex GATE-B driver (bound, gamma_source, gamma_network, max|PF| before the first step). The SF gate has it as a hard-fail; the cortex gate has nothing.

A pre-commit bound count (bound_pre) so mechanical observables and the kinetic population can be paired in phase. Its absence is what silently vacuated the tension-zero oracle and what makes the (n_bound, gamma) column pairing in both drivers off by one accepted step.

A convergence-based acceptance predicate for slices with no ECM. The declared default (force balance) is 0 == 0 there; the SF gate computes the right dimensionless quantity (residual/tension) as a post-hoc report field and never as accepted_d.
A declared, derived squared-force tolerance for assemble_balance. tol_sq_d is caller-supplied by design and no caller supplies it; no value or derivation exists in code or docs.
GlobalCellLedger.reset() being called once per step. Zero callers, so any channel that is ever filled becomes a whole-run running sum rather than a per-step residual.
A device-side owner/free-list mirror of PopulationLedger. population.py:20 claims one exists; nothing in the tree implements it, which is why the per-accepted-step disjointness assertion cannot fail.
population_ledgers wired into the cortex GATE-B driver at all — the headline 70,686-filament dynamic run passes none, so even the tautological invariant does not execute there.

A cumulative power-stroke / motor-work observable. abscissa resets to 0 on every detach and re-attach, and atp_consumed_d is never written, so nothing in the system accumulates motor output over a run.
A liveness gate for declared channels (event or ledger), replacing the string set-difference conformance checks that a permanently-zero channel currently passes.
A vacuity guard in the verdict machinery so zero-sample claims fail closed.

A seed ensemble for the GATE-B bound fraction. GATE A was ensemble-validated across 3 seeds (0.1398/0.1416/0.1586); the GATE-B 0->85% claim rests on a single seed, and neither the seed nor dt_phys nor the relax iteration count is recorded in the SF artifact (the contract yaml flags all three as CONFIG_UNRECORDED / 'the run's physical time is not reconstructible').
open_questions_for_pi: RULE CONFLICT, needs a ruling: the physiological-baseline HARD rule says every compartment starts at its in-vivo setpoint, which for NMII means the resting bound-head duty (~0.1-0.3), not zero. But the emergence MEASUREMENT needs zero bound heads at t0 as its negative control, and GATE B chose zero (resting_bound_myosin_fraction=None). Both cannot hold in one run. Proposal: two runs from the same build — an EMERGENCE run from zero (measurement) and a PRODUCTION run from the sourced resting duty (physics), with the emergence run explicitly labelled a mechanism instrument and never a physiological baseline.

What is the acceptance predicate for a slice with no ECM? Today the declared default is 0 == 0 and every driver force-accepts. If it becomes residual/tension < tol, no step in the current explicit relax would be accepted and no kinetics would commit. Do you want (a) the honest zero-accept result banked as a blocker, (b) the implicit/CG inner solve landed first, or (c) an explicitly disclosed force-accept mode that is forbidden from producing any banked number?

The balance-gate tolerance: assemble_balance takes a caller-supplied squared-force tolerance so that no magic number is baked in — and no caller ever supplies one. What is the value and, more importantly, from what is it derived? Without a derivation this repeats the 0.21 pN situation (a widely-quoted threshold with no derivation site anywhere on disk).

Should the Hill stall-crossing guard da_max = (f_stall - F)/k_xb stay? It makes the abscissa — a state observable — a function of two PI-GAP magnitudes (f_stall, k_xb). The alternative is sub-stepping the stroke within the tick, which keeps the observable magnitude-free at the cost of wall-time. Given that parameters are eventual OUTPUTS of inference, an observable that depends on two of the unknowns is expensive.

Attach uses PRE-solve geometry for admissibility and POST-solve geometry for the zero-strain reference. Should the capture test be re-applied at commit (rejecting heads the solve carried out of reach), or should the query be re-run after the solve? The current CPU reference test certifies zero placement force at 0.2 um against a 0.05 um capture radius, i.e. it certifies the inadmissible case.

Is 8,840 NMII heads (442 minifilaments) the intended population for a 70,686-filament cortex, and against what denominator should the emergent duty be compared to Kovacs 2003 / Nagy 2013? At present 85.24% is bound/all-heads, the analytic ceiling for the same constants is 98.6%, and literature duty is 0.1-0.3 — three numbers that are not comparable to each other and nothing in the code says so.

The per-accepted-step PopulationLedger assertion: make it real on the device (an owner-id array written by every commit, O(N) on-device) or demote it to build-time-only and delete the per-step call? Keeping an O(N) host-side loop in the physical-time loop that provably cannot fail is the one outcome worth avoiding.

Should the ID namespace continue to mix cortex F-actin filaments, ECM collagen segments and NMII minifilaments? 'Every physical filament belongs to exactly one component' and 'every allocated object has a unique global id' are different invariants; the ledger currently checks the second while the docstring claims the first.

result.family: FAMILY 3 — HOW CONVERGENCE IS MEASURED (residual / acceptance / stopping criteria in ac/cell + ac/engine)

instruments.name: max|PF| < 0.21 pN — the reported resting gate
instruments.where: 72 raw literals across ~30 files (ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_a_*.py, ac_resting_converge.py, ac_erm_schwarz_probe.py:33 `GATE = 0.21`, ac/cell/erm_schwarz.py:6,31, ac/cell/erm_gauss_seidel.py:7, ac/cell/assemble.py:242,245,279,282, tests/ac/cell/test_resting_balance_oracle.py:15). NO definition site: no module exports it, no YAML carries it, no ValidationGate row anchors it. Confirmed absent from every runtime decision path (ac/engine/, driver.py, inner_mechanics.py carry no 0.21) — it is a REPORTING contract only.
instruments.what_its_name_implies: "The cell is at mechanical rest to within 0.21 pN" — a physical, biological equilibrium statement.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The largest single nodal projected force, compared against a hand-frozen snapshot of the runtime's float64 ROUND-OFF displacement tolerance, evaluated once at seg=0.5 um with steric ON. Reproduced exactly: F_pred = tolerance_um/dt_mu = 10*sqrt(eps64)*ell*kmax = 10*1.4901161193847656e-08*0.4999048934*2828099.2886817832 = 0.2106697371 pN, and the committed artifact resting_native_probe2_capture0.6_2026-07-23.json carries inner_tolerance_um=7.449163398500275e-09 and inner_dt_mu=3.535943748517097e-08 whose ratio is that number to rel=0.0e+00. So it is machine-precision x a mesh the code itself labels CONVENIENCE (assemble.py:228 "5-10x above the sourced 50-100 nm mesh") x kmax set by the WCA near-core guard whose own constant is labelled "PROVISIONAL Magic-Number-Block scale" (K_EV_PROVISIONAL, assemble.py:159). In float32 the same formula gives 4882 pN; with steric off, 0.0611 pN.
instruments.evidence: I reproduced the identity independently (script + arithmetic, both exact). Independent confirmation that it is NOT a physics threshold: it moves x23,170 under a floating-point-precision change and x3.4 under toggling excluded volume, neither of which changes any biology. Held-fixed across refinement it silently LOOSENS: the runtime's own bound is 0.0843 at seg=0.2 (frozen literal 2.49x looser) and 0.0316 at seg=0.075 (6.64x looser), so the 200 nm rung documented as "the known-good rung (weak solver already reaches 0.21)" (FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:293) is re-opened by arithmetic alone.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Retire it as a CLOSING criterion. Two-channel replacement: (LOCAL) max_i |PF_i| / K_ii <= delta*_i with delta*_i = min(2.7 nm, sqrt(kBT/K_ii)) — a fixed LENGTH, so N- and seg-independent; (GLOBAL) the coherent-mode projection gate below. Interim, if a force gate must be quoted at all, compute tolerance_um/dt_mu per run (both already in every report JSON) and report the dimensionless ratio max|PF|/F_pred — never the literal.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Run the SAME physical state at two seg values and check whether the gate verdict flips with no physics change. seg 0.5 -> 0.2 flips PASS->FAIL against the runtime's own bound while the frozen literal keeps saying PASS. Second control: recompile in float32 and confirm the 'physics gate' moves by 4 decades.

instruments.name: Executing accepted-step predicate: dt_mu*max|PF| <= tolerance_um (AND max_disp <= tol AND max_constraint_err <= tol)
instruments.where: ffn_sim/ac/cell/inner_mechanics.py:296 update_convergence_kernel; tolerance_um = sqrt(eps64)*cell.convergence_length_um set at ffn_sim/ac/cell/driver.py:506 and :1026 and ffn_sim/ac/cell/preload_force_probe.py:341; convergence_length_um = seg_mean (ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:391, :1119); dt_mu from compute_descent_step_kernel (inner_mechanics.py:259)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Mechanical convergence of the inner solve.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly what its own docstring claims: three lengths, all in um, all compared to the smallest position change resolvable in float64 against a segment of length ell. The force limb is a displacement test in disguise and exists specifically to stop a backtracked accelerator from manufacturing convergence with a vanishing step. Honest instrument, honestly documented.
instruments.evidence: Read the kernel and the tolerance construction end to end. The docstring's claim ("derived numerical-resolution criterion, grid-invariant and not tuned to make a biological gate pass") is TRUE of a displacement tolerance. max_constraint_error_kernel (inner_mechanics.py:207-221) computes abs(length(pos[i+1]-pos[i]) - seg_rest) — genuinely um, not um^2, so the three-way comparison is dimensionally consistent. One real caveat the derivation doc misses: dt_mu = 0.1/max(k_mech, |dp|*pressure_edge_um), NOT 0.1/kmax — so the implied force bound is STATE-DEPENDENT and loosens if a transient pressure jump ever exceeds the mechanical kmax. At the native config (40 pN/um^2 x sub-um edge = O(10) vs kmax 2.8e6) the mechanical limb dominates, so it is currently inert, but the derivation's formula omits a live limb.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Keep as the numerical-resolution latch. Rename what is CLAIMED from it: 'the athermal minimiser reached float64 resolution', never 'the cell is at rest to X pN'. Add the pressure limb to any documented formula.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Drive |dp|*pressure_edge_um above mechanical_kmax (a large transient pressure jump) and confirm the implied force bound rises — proving the reported single-number bound is not a constant of the run.

instruments.name: max_displacement <= tolerance_um (the displacement limb, taken alone)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The state has stopped changing, therefore it has converged.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: That the last step was small. A STALLED solver satisfies it by construction. This is on record as a live failure mode, not a hypothetical: 'a scalar-damped Newton stalls at 0.78 pN' (ac/cell/erm_schwarz.py:6) and '0.0% position change over 3,000 iterations' (AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:114).
instruments.evidence: Satisfiable with an arbitrarily large mechanical residual by any solver that stops moving. MITIGATION IS REAL AND MUST BE CREDITED: it is ANDed with the force limb precisely for this reason, and the kernel docstring says so explicitly ('It prevents a backtracked accelerator from manufacturing convergence by taking an arbitrarily small displacement while the mechanical residual remains large'). Flagged here because the displacement number is often quoted on its own in diagnostics.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Never quote the displacement limb alone. Any 'iterations converged' statement must carry the force limb value and the iteration count in the same sentence.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Inject a solver that returns dx=0 unconditionally and confirm the displacement limb latches converged while the force limb rejects it.

instruments.name: GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md + ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py (9/9 checks) — the instrument that certifies the threshold
instruments.what_its_name_implies: 9 independent verifications, negative-control-watched, therefore the derivation is verified.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: 5 checks respond to input; 4 CANNOT FAIL under any input the script exposes. Measured, not asserted: with --assume-kmax 1.0 (a 2.8-million-fold wrong input) it still reports 5/9 PASS; with --assume-seg 1e-4 it reports 6/9. The permanently-passing four are `dimensions` and `dt_mu_units` (exponent algebra over formula tuples the script itself writes — a unit test of the document, not of the code), `limiting_case_sigma_radial` (sqrt(kBT/1e5) vs a hard-coded 0.207 — constant vs constant, no runtime input at all), and `route_c_scales_linearly_in_seg`.
instruments.evidence: The reviewer's ' 3 of 9' is an UNDERCOUNT — it is 4 of 9, and the fourth is the worst one. route_c_scales_linearly_in_seg computes route_c_predicate_floor(c, s, kmax)/s over rungs [0.5,0.2,0.075] holding kmax FIXED (script lines 369-375). Since route_c = 10*sqrt(eps)*s*kmax, dividing by s yields 10*sqrt(eps)*kmax identically — spread is float64 round-off (1.3e-16) for ANY kmax, ANY constants, ANY rungs. It is an algebraic identity dressed as a verification, and it is the check supporting the document's single most load-bearing claim (F_pred ∝ ell^+1). Worse: the script's own kmax table DOES contain the one ell-dependent term (actin_bending_kappa_over_ell3, line 197) but evaluates it at the fixed c.seg_um, so the check hard-codes the very assumption it should test. Substantively the ell^+1 claim survives (bending takes over kmax only below ell=2.95 nm, sub-monomer) — but it survives on my arithmetic, not on that check. Also: negative-control coverage is 2 of ~12 inputs (only --assume-kmax and --assume-seg; kBT, kappa, sigma_EV, k_xb, k_erm, k_xl, Pi_0, R, the 0.1 CFL numerator and eps64 have none).
instruments.canonical_replacement: Rewrite C6 to vary seg AND recompute kmax from the seg-dependent table, so the check can fail when bending takes over; add --assume knobs for the remaining ~10 inputs and record the fail-count per knob. Report per check whether it is input-sensitive; a check that cannot fail must be labelled 'identity', not 'verification'.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Exactly what I ran: sweep every input to an absurd value and count which checks still pass. Any check that survives every sweep is an identity. This should be a standing meta-gate on every *_derivation.py in the repo.

instruments.name: 'Textbook grid convergence' of the membrane residual -> membrane_subdivisions = 8 as the PI-ratified production RESTING config
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Refining the membrane mesh 6->8 reduced the physical Helfrich/Young-Laplace residual 10x; the resting baseline now PASSES GATE A entirely (cortex 0.036 / membrane 0.077 / nucleus 0.16, all < 0.21).
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Only the per-node PARTITION of an unchanged residual field. From the committed table (GATE_A_RESTING_CONVERGENCE_2026-07-23.md:135-136): subdiv 6, N=40,962, max 0.7766, mean 0.644; subdiv 8, N=655,362, max 0.0768, mean 0.040. mean ratio = 16.1 vs N ratio = 16.00 — mean|PF| fell EXACTLY as 1/N. Therefore the L1 total is invariant: 0.644*40,962 = 26,379.5 pN vs 0.040*655,362 = 26,214.5 pN, a 0.63% difference across a 16x refinement. In the only norm with a continuum limit for a surface (nodal force / nodal area = a pressure, using 4*pi*7.5^2 = 706.86 um^2), the error is 37.3 vs 37.1 pN/um^2 — also invariant, and equal to 93% of the resting turgor Pi_0 = 40 pN/um^2. The residual FIELD did not shrink at all.
instruments.evidence: For a smooth shell a nodal force IS a traction x area-per-node, so it falls as 1/N whether or not anything converged; the measured 16.1 vs 16.00 is that identity, not convergence. A genuinely converging Young-Laplace residual would have driven the L1 total and the pressure error DOWN; both stood still. The total residual is 3.71x the entire physiological turgor load (Pi_0*pi*R^2 = 7068.6 pN) at BOTH meshes. Applying the derivation doc's own recommended (d1) gate to the upper bound |S| <= 26,214 pN gives gamma_spur = S/(8*pi*R) = 139.1 pN/um = 93% of gamma_target = 150 pN/um — a 93x failure of its own 1% option, unchanged by the refinement. This is a hard finding computed from committed numbers with no unsourced constant, and it directly contradicts the on-disk claim and the config change (membrane_subdivisions=8, commit ea0babc4) that rests on it. HONEST LIMIT: Sum|PF| bounds the coherent part |S| from above; if the residual signs cancel, S is smaller. But the doc itself calls the residual 'UNIFORM ~0.64 over the whole membrane' from a Helfrich/Young-Laplace mismatch, which is radial and coherent. Either way the refinement improved nothing, and S is unmeasured — which is the point.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Any 'grid convergence' claim must be made in a norm that has a continuum limit: Sum_i |PF_i| (L1 total) and nodal-force/nodal-area (traction, pN/um^2). Per-node max and per-node mean are forbidden as convergence evidence on a mesh-refined body. Re-score the 6->8 sweep in both admissible norms, measure S, and re-surface membrane_subdivisions=8 to PI as a config change whose justification did not hold.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Refine ANY smooth pressurised shell with the solver disabled (zero solver iterations). Per-node max|PF| will still fall ~1/N. If a metric improves when the solver does no work, it is not a convergence metric. This is a 5-minute CPU test on a synthetic sphere and it would have caught this before ratification.

instruments.name: assemble_balance: |reaction_resultant + traction_resultant|^2 <= tol_sq (the only global acceptance criterion)
instruments.where: ffn_sim/ac/engine/ledger.py:20-23, :329-357 (_assemble_force_balance_kernel); wired through ffn_sim/ac/engine/transaction.py:116,135; tol_sq_d threaded as `wp.array | None = None` through sf_motor_slice.py:310,346,363, cortex_motor_slice.py:626,646,662, erm_cortex_slice.py:298,335, interior_column_slice.py:544,597, composed_native.py:375
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The composed cell is in global force balance, checked against a declared gate-contract tolerance.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: NOTHING, currently — the tolerance does not exist. Every production caller defaults tol_sq_d=None. The ONLY value anywhere in the tree is tests/ac/engine/test_ledger.py:145, 1.0e-18 pN^2 (i.e. 1e-9 pN), a structural fixture. ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:506 raises rather than run it: '--balance-gate requires a GlobalCellLedger + tol_sq_d wired by the Lead'. Second, and separate: the criterion is scoped (ledger.py:20) to 'an inertialess ECM sub-body cut at the FA clutches'. That scoping is CORRECT and non-vacuous for auditing the ECM solve — but it is identically zero for a force-free self-propelled cell whether it crawls or sits, and it is blind to line-of-action: relocating every traction to the wrong place leaves Sum(T) unchanged.
instruments.evidence: Grepped every tol_sq site in the repo; no production supplier exists, so balance_ok_d has never been evaluated against a physical tolerance in any committed run. The docstring's 'no numerical tolerance is baked in here' is true and was the right design call, but the caller-side obligation was never discharged. The blindness is architectural, not a bug: ARCHITECTURE_COMPLETENESS_2026-07-25.md:53 already reaches the same conclusion independently ('the single most dangerous zero in the system').
instruments.canonical_replacement: DERIVE THE TOLERANCE AS ROUND-OFF, NOT PHYSICS. reaction + traction = 0 is an exact algebraic identity (Newton's 3rd law across adjoint connectors), not a physical approximation, so the ONLY admissible tolerance is the float64 accumulation error of the reduction itself. Use the RELATIVE form: |R + T| <= eps_bal * max(|R|, |T|, F_floor) with eps_bal = sqrt(N_contrib) * eps64 * 10 (one safety decade). Measured floors: sqrt(494,802)*eps64 = 1.56e-13; sqrt(655,362)*eps64 = 1.80e-13; sqrt(2,898,126)*eps64 = 3.78e-13 — so eps_bal ~ 1e-12 relative, i.e. tol_sq = (1e-12*max(|R|,|T|))^2. Anything looser hides a missing adjoint. The test's 1e-18 pN^2 absolute is ~6400x above the round-off floor: well-posed as a round-off check, but absolute (breaks under N) and not a physics gate. REQUIRED ADDITIONAL CHANNELS for the criterion to have content: (i) FIRST MOMENT M = Sum_i (x_i - x_c) x F_i — an INDEPENDENT identity, because Newton's 3rd law gives Sum F = 0 for equal-and-opposite pairs but gives Sum M = 0 only if they are also COLLINEAR, so the moment channel catches a connector transferring force along the wrong line of action, a class the resultant cannot see; (ii) CENTROID x_c = Sum m_i x_i / Sum m_i and its rate, which is what makes 'the cell moved' an observable; (iii) the TRACTION FIRST-MOMENT (dipole) tensor D = Sum (x_i - x_c) (x) T_i — nonzero for a crawler, zero for a symmetric sitter, while Sum T is zero for both. (iii) is simultaneously the fix for this criterion and the missing crawl-dipole observable the project lists as one of only two surviving real deficits. Note ecm_world.py already PROMISES a moment contribution in four Protocol docstrings (:205, :272, :293, :346) that no ledger channel can receive.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Translate every traction application point by a fixed offset (same forces, wrong locations) and confirm balance_ok stays 1. Then confirm the moment channel flips it to 0. Second control: run a synthetic crawler with a prescribed nonzero net displacement and confirm the criterion never fires — proving it cannot detect motion.

instruments.name: residual_over_tension < 1% (the SF-motor quantitative verdict)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The inner solve converged relative to the tension being reported, so the reported tension is an equilibrium value.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: max over FREE nodes of |F| divided by max over SEGMENTS of |k_axial*(L - r0)|. Four independent defects: (1) numerator and denominator are maxima over DIFFERENT index sets, so the ratio is not the relative residual of any operator; (2) the denominator is T_abs_max_pN — it takes abs(), so a BUCKLED/compressed fiber inflates the denominator and passes the gate on the strength of compression, while the reported observable is T_max; (3) the denominator is proportional to k_axial, which ac/engine/sf_mechanics.py declares an explicit modelling GAP precisely because NF2007 treats the backbone as inextensible and REJECTS an axial penalty spring — so the pass criterion is proportional to an unsourced constant that is not part of the physics being tested; (4) it is structurally uninformative in exactly the observed regime, where numerator and denominator collapse together.
instruments.evidence: The committed record is self-refuting: outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/REPORT.md:74-76 — 'the free-node residual is 15.5% of the reported tension. Decisive control: a 10x longer relax moved T_max by 3.4x (0.451 -> 0.133 pN) at an identical bound population'. Both numerator and denominator fell, so the ratio can be flat or improving while the answer moves 3.4x. Compounding this, the recommended configuration is chosen BY the criterion it certifies: the module docstring at :68 states '--relax 4000 is the value at which the reported residual actually falls below 1% of the tension for the default population'. That is solver-budget selection by gate outcome. FURTHER CONFOUND, from the kinetics: abscissa advances by tau*hill_velocity(load) once per ACCEPTED outer step (ac/motor/segment_motor.py:173), and the load depends on how far the relax got — so a longer relax changes the motor DRIVE, not only the mechanics. 'Identical bound population' is a COUNT; it does not pin motor state. Sum(abscissa) is the missing control, and it was not held. The 3.4x is therefore an unseparated mixture of non-convergence and kinetic feedback, and the record as written cannot attribute it.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Replace with the CUT-PLANE (free-body) TRANSMISSION IDENTITY, which is exact at equilibrium and parameter-free. For each SF segment j, cut the fiber and sum all external forces on the outboard piece: T_j == Sum_{heads outboard} f_h . t_hat_j + Sum_{crosslinks outboard} f_xl . t_hat_j (+ FA reaction if the cut is outboard of an anchor). Report the dimensionless defect eps_j = |T_j - Sum_outboard| / max(|T_j|, |Sum_outboard|, F_floor), with F_floor the round-off floor of the sum so eps_j stays defined as both sides -> 0. THIS IS THE DISCRIMINATOR FOR THE OPEN QUESTION: (a) tension fell because the solve genuinely relaxed to equilibrium with a weaker drive -> BOTH sides fall together, eps_j stays small -> converged, the small tension is real; (b) tension fell because the solve is stuck while heads are still loaded -> Sum_outboard != 0 with T ~ 0 -> eps_j -> 1 -> not converged; (c) tension is large but not motor-generated (build strain, a crosslink) -> eps_j -> 1 unless the crosslink term accounts for it, which forces the report to NAME the force carrying the tension. It is magnitude-free: it holds for any k_axial, k_xb, f_head, because both sides scale, so it cannot be passed by stiffening a GAP parameter. It is the same algebra as the connector-adjoint requirement, so it audits the connector at the same time. WHAT IT CANNOT DO, stated so it is not oversold: it is an AXIAL projection and is blind to transverse non-equilibrium (bending, crosslink shear) — pair it with the per-node displacement channel; it cannot certify the state is PHYSIOLOGICAL, only that it is in equilibrium and the forces are accounted; and it holds at ANY equilibrium, so it cannot detect a solver stalled in the wrong basin — that needs the invariance gate.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Scale k_axial by 10x at fixed geometry and confirm the ratio 'improves' with zero change in convergence. Second control: force the fiber into pure compression (all segments L < r0) and confirm the gate passes on T_abs_max while T_max is negative.

The design intent is exactly right and is the correct answer to the converged-vs-transient question — it was simply never implemented, so the strongest available convergence evidence in the project is uncollected.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Implement it as GATE C (formalised in magnitude_free_oracles). Critically, it must be run KINETICS-FROZEN, otherwise the two arms are not the same physical problem — that is the confound that invalidated the existing 10x-relax control.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Assert in the gate that the run record contains a non-null drift field for every reported observable; a run that emits no drift number cannot claim convergence.

instruments.name: PCG stopping criterion: ||r||^2 <= eps64 * ||r_0||^2
instruments.where: ffn_sim/ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:1386-1401 (_cg_finalize_kernel), called at :2064 with the literal wp.float64(2.220446049250313e-16); docstring claim at :28
instruments.what_its_name_implies: CG residual norm target is sqrt(eps64) RELATIVE.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that, and the claim checks out: rr is the SQUARED norm, so rr_new <= eps64*rr_initial is ||r||/||r_0|| <= sqrt(eps64) = 1.49e-8. Relative, dimensionless, grid-invariant, magnitude-free, no tuned constant. This is the best-formed convergence criterion in the family.
instruments.evidence: Read the kernel and the launch site. Two limitations worth recording without downgrading it: (i) it is PURELY relative, so it never certifies an absolute residual — a large right-hand side converges to a proportionally large remaining absolute force, which is why it must be paired with an absolute per-node channel; (ii) max_iterations defaults to 32 (implicit_mechanics.py:1463) against a system whose Gershgorin-bounded condition number is ~5e6 (alpha-actinin 4.6e5 / bending 0.582), so the latch will rarely set. That interacts with a hard gate: decide_better_line_search_trial_kernel (:422-435) takes NO trial unless linear_converged != 0, which is the mechanism behind the recorded '0.0% position change over 3,000 iterations'. The criterion is sound; the BUDGET is the problem, and it is diagnosable because iterations[0] is recorded.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Keep. Add a companion ABSOLUTE report (||r|| in pN and max_i |r_i|/K_ii in um) and always emit iterations[0] alongside converged_flag, so 'converged=0 because the budget ran out' is never confusable with 'diverged'.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Scale the right-hand side by 1e6 and confirm the relative criterion still latches converged while the absolute residual is 1e6 larger.

instruments.name: PCG zero-RHS convergence latch: if rr_initial <= 0 then converged = 1
instruments.what_its_name_implies: converged = 1 means the linear solve succeeded.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: On an exactly-zero right-hand side it reports CONVERGED without performing or testing anything. That is arithmetically correct (dx = 0 solves A dx = 0) but it means a force field that was masked, zeroed, or never accumulated — a Dirichlet-pinned block, a mis-wired connector that contributed nothing, a force kernel that was not launched — reports 'converged' and then authorises a line-search trial (decide_better_line_search_trial_kernel requires linear_converged != 0). A wiring failure is indistinguishable from equilibrium at this latch.
instruments.evidence: Read the branch: `value = rr[0]; if value <= 0.0: active[0] = 0; converged[0] = 1`. Cannot fail when the RHS is zero, and there is no accompanying record of WHY it latched. This is the same structural pattern as the project's own A/A0 = V/V0 = 1.000 tautology and the 5 um cohesion metric on cells 4 um apart: a criterion satisfied by the ABSENCE of the thing being measured. It is directly load-bearing for the current priority, because 'compartments are connected so they deform each other' is exactly the claim a zero-force-transfer wiring bug would fake here.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Split the flag: converged_nontrivial (rr_initial > floor AND rr_new <= eps64*rr_initial) versus rhs_below_floor (rr_initial <= sqrt(N)*eps64*|F|_typ)^2. Emit both. Any acceptance path and any report must distinguish 'solved' from 'nothing to solve'. In a CONNECTEDNESS gate, rhs_below_floor on a component that is supposed to be loaded is a FAIL, not a pass.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Disconnect one connector (contribute no force) and confirm the slice reports converged=1 with balance_ok=1 and a zero residual — the exact false PASS a connectedness gate must catch. This test should be standing for every connector in the 32-connector graph.

Correct dimension (I checked specifically for the common |L^2 - L0^2| um^2 error — it is not present), per-segment, parameter-free, and its threshold sqrt(eps64)*ell scales correctly with the mesh it is measured on.
instruments.evidence: Read the kernel body. This is the one instrument in the family that is dimensionally, structurally, and scale-wise correct with no caveat, and it should be the template: a geometric error, measured in the units of the constraint it enforces, against a tolerance derived from the discretization it lives on.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None needed. Use as the pattern for the per-node displacement channel.

instruments.name: abscissa — 'accumulated power-stroke'
instruments.where: ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:151-183 (advance :173, RESET :182); ffn_sim/ac/motor/hand.py:165-207, :214-248 (resets at :207, :248); consumed in the crossbridge force via x_att = (1-t)*pos[a] + t*pos[b] + abscissa*walk_dir (segment_motor.py:19)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Accumulated power stroke — a cumulative, monotone record of work the motor has delivered.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: An INSTANTANEOUS per-head strain coordinate. It is RESET TO 0.0 on every detach (segment_motor.py:182, hand.py:207, hand.py:248), so it accumulates only within one continuous attachment episode, not over a run. It is also saturating by construction: the advance is capped by da_max = max(0, (f_stall - load)/k_xb), a derived stall-crossing guard, so it stops growing as the head approaches stall. Sum(abscissa) over a population is therefore neither cumulative work nor a monotone drive history — it is a snapshot of current crossbridge strain, and it silently drops every detachment.
instruments.evidence: Read all three step/detach kernels; the reset is unconditional on detach in every one. Anyone integrating Sum(abscissa) as 'total power stroke delivered' will undercount by every unbinding event, and the undercount grows with k_off0 and with load (Bell) — i.e. it is biased exactly where the physics is most active. This matters right now because abscissa is the leading candidate for the converged-vs-transient discriminator: used as named it would become the project's eighth 'metric measuring something other than its name'.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Keep abscissa as what it is — the per-head strain coordinate, and use it that way: it is the correct, geometry-independent ingredient for the motor side of the cut-plane identity, Sum_h f_h = Sum_h k_xb*(abscissa_h - r0_bind_h) projected on t_hat, computable from motor state ALONE without reading the SF length the solver is moving. If a genuinely cumulative counter is wanted, add a SEPARATE never-reset channel abscissa_cumulative (and a detach counter) and name it so. Do not rename abscissa; too much code reads it.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Run with k_off0 raised 10x (more detachment, same binding) and confirm Sum(abscissa) FALLS while total delivered work rises — proving it is not a cumulative quantity.

instruments.name: rms nodal force
