Case-insensitive word-boundary grep for 'rms' over ac/ and scripts/ returns only ac/emergence/null_model.py:18 (a docstring about eigenvalues), ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py:231 (a docstring), and unrelated h7_*/dcm_*/compartment_smoke scripts on other engines.
instruments.what_its_name_implies: An rms-nodal-force convergence measure exists and is reported.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Does not exist as an instrument in the AC engine. The listed inventory item is not on disk. The only aggregate nodal-force statistics that exist are max (device atomic_max) and the mean values quoted in prose in the GATE-A documents.
instruments.evidence: Direct grep. Recording it because the inventory handed to me listed it, and an assumed-present instrument is more dangerous than an absent one — a report can cite 'rms nodal force' and there is no code to contradict it.
instruments.canonical_replacement: If added, note that rms|PF| is NOT grid-invariant: with PF_i ~ f*h and N ~ 1/h, rms ~ h^+1, so an rms threshold must be re-derived at every mesh. Prefer the two admissible norms: Sum|PF| (L1 total, has a continuum limit) and the signed coherent projection S.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A standing gate that every metric named in a REPORT.md resolves to a definition site in code — the same discipline that would have caught the 0.21 literal having no definition site.

magnitude_free_oracles: (1a) LOCAL RESTING GATE — per-node implied displacement, threshold = a physically meaningless LENGTH. Derivation, using only the code's own quantities: the PI's framing 'residual force whose implied displacement is below a length that cannot matter'. FIRST, REJECT the obvious reading: dt_mu is NOT a mobility. dt_mu = 0.1/max(k_mech, |dp|*edge) is a global CFL stability step in um/pN set by the single stiffest bond in the cell; one descent step is not a relaxation, and there is NO per-node drag in ac/ (driver.py:7 retires the 6*pi*eta*R clock; ac/fluid/__init__.py:14,28 records gamma_solid retirement; mu_pore's own policy field forbids reuse). Reading delta/dt_mu gives F = 10*delta*kmax = 76,359 pN at 2.7 nm and 197,967 pN at 7 nm — 10.8x and 28x the ENTIRE turgor load. That route must be refused, and refused in writing, so nobody re-derives it. CORRECT MOBILITY: the LOCAL EQUILIBRIUM OFFSET. delta_i = |PF_i| / K_ii, where K_ii is the node's Hessian diagonal. IT ALREADY EXISTS ON DEVICE: ProjectedAnalyticCG.preconditioner (implicit_mechanics.py:1525) is a per-node vec3d — a per-node, per-AXIS stiffness diagonal assembled by _build_preconditioner (:1780) from every force family (bending, crosslinks, membrane edge springs, WCA core, NMII backbone/arm/crossbridge, angle Gauss-Newton). One Jacobi apply (apply_preconditioner_kernel, :1935) already forms z = r/diag = the implied-displacement field. The gate is a max-reduction over an array the solver builds every iteration: 5 lines, no new physics, no new constant. GATE: max_i,axis |PF_i| / K_ii <= delta*_i with delta*_i = min(2.7 nm, sqrt(kBT/K_ii)). Both lengths are on disk and sourced: ACTIN_MONOMER_DELTA_UM = 0.0027 (ac/weave/membrane_ratchet.py:65, Pollard axial rise — nothing in the model resolves a sub-monomer position, a node IS a multi-monomer bead) and x_th = sqrt(kBT/K_ii) with kBT = 4.280011900e-3 pN*um (ff/units.py:45) — the node's own thermal position uncertainty, below which a displacement is unobservable in principle. Take the TIGHTER of the two so it can never loosen. Crossover at K = kBT/(2.7 nm)^2 = 587.1 pN/um: below it the monomer length binds, above it the thermal length binds. Implied per-node force bounds: K=0.582 (bending-only actin) -> 1.57e-3 pN; K=587 -> 1.59 pN; K=1e3 (k_xb) -> 2.07 pN; K=4.6e3 (k_erm) -> 4.44 pN; K=4.6e5 (alpha-actinin) -> 44.4 pN; K=2.83e6 (WCA core) -> 110 pN. NOT A BLANKET LOOSENING: it is TIGHTER than 0.21 pN at every node with K < 0.21/0.0027 = 77.8 pN/um — i.e. at essentially all 494,802 pure-actin bending nodes (K ~ 0.58), by x134 — and looser only at the stiff minority where a residual genuinely displaces nothing. That is the right direction, because it is the actin bulk whose geometry the tension measurement reads. MANDATORY IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT: preconditioner is seeded with the IMEX regularizer a = 1/step (set_preconditioner_kernel at :1786), which is a SOLVER knob, not a stiffness. The diagnostic reduction MUST be launched with regularization = 0, or the new instrument inherits a numerical knob exactly the way route (c) inherited kmax — the failure this whole audit exists to stop.

(1b) GLOBAL RESTING GATE — coherent-mode projection onto the observable. A per-node channel is blind to long-wavelength error: one Jacobi step is a LOCAL estimate and underestimates a coherent (breathing) mode by that mode's condition number. Only the coherent radial part of a residual can bias the reported cortical tension; randomly signed local residuals cancel. GATE: S = Sum_i (PF_i . r_hat_i) [SIGNED, not |.|]; dP_spur = S/(4*pi*R^2); gamma_spur = dP_spur*R/2 = S/(8*pi*R); require gamma_spur/gamma_target <= f with gamma_target = Pi_0*R/2. Stated RELATIVE, it is Pi_0-invariant, so it survives the live 3.3x Pi_0 spread (40 / 72 / 133 Pa) that would move any absolute pN budget. It contains neither n_nodes nor seg. Generalisation, and the reason this is the right family: project the residual onto the KERNEL OF THE OBSERVABLE being reported — breathing mode for gamma, dipole mode for traction, translation for centroid motion. A residual orthogonal to the observable cannot bias it and should not gate it. TWO CHANNELS ARE REQUIRED, NOT ONE: local (catches kinks, interpenetration, defects; refinable) plus coherent (catches exactly the mode that biases gamma; grid-invariant). Neither alone is sufficient and neither substitutes for the other.

(1c) THE SCALING STATEMENT — the single most important output, because a per-node gate and a total-residual gate behave OPPOSITELY under refinement. Let N = n_nodes, h = seg_um (or mean_edge_um). THRESHOLD SCALING: (i) incumbent route-(c) per-node force bound F_pred = 10*sqrt(eps64)*h*kmax is proportional to h^+1 and INDEPENDENT of N (kmax is set by the WCA near-core term, a function of f_cap, sigma_EV, epsilon only; bending kappa/h^3 overtakes it only for h < 2.95 nm, sub-monomer, unreachable); (ii) the proposed per-node DISPLACEMENT gate has a threshold that is a fixed LENGTH — independent of N and of h by construction, which is the whole reason for moving to a displacement; (iii) the coherent-projection gate has a threshold that is a dimensionless FRACTION of the physiological load — independent of N and h. MEASUREMENT SCALING (this is what kills per-node force gates): a nodal force is a force DENSITY times the node's share of the domain, so the same refinement moves it in OPPOSITE directions in different compartments. On a 2-D shell PF_i ~ p*A_node = p*4*pi*R^2/N, so PF ~ 1/N ~ h^+2 and Sum|PF| is N-invariant — MEASURED on the committed membrane pair: mean 0.644 -> 0.040 across N 40,962 -> 655,362, ratio 16.1 vs 16.00, and Sum|PF| = 26,379.5 -> 26,214.5 pN, invariant to 0.63%. Consequence: A FIXED PER-NODE FORCE GATE ON A SHELL IS PASSED BY REFINEMENT ALONE with zero physical improvement — that is precisely how 'membrane 0.7766 -> 0.0768, 0 of 655,362 over the 0.21 gate' was produced. On a 1-D filament with a resolved smooth load PF_i ~ f_line*h so PF ~ h^+1 and N ~ 1/h, again Sum|PF| invariant. But against an UNRESOLVED GEOMETRIC DEFECT, bending gives PF ~ kappa*delta/h^3 ~ h^-3, which DIVERGES under refinement — MEASURED: the cortex series gives h^-2.845, and the codebase's own construction comment predicts the mechanism and the size, 'a per-node bending KINK whose cytosim force F = alpha*d (alpha = kappa/seg^3) blows up x288 at the fine 75 nm mesh' (assemble.py:270-274; (0.5/0.075)^3 = 296, matching). Cortex L1 totals from the same series go 0.027*494,802 = 13,360 pN -> 0.129*2,898,126 = 373,858 pN, UP 28x — the opposite direction to the membrane, in the same refinement program (caveat: two different states and cortex_density_per_fil 20->40 confounded, so direction is robust and the exponent is indicative). THEREFORE: the gate/measurement gap moves as h^+1 (shells: guaranteed pass by refining) to h^-4 (cortex defects: guaranteed fail by refining). NO per-node force threshold — frozen OR computed per run — can survive both. A per-node max force gate must be retired as the closing criterion. Admissible refinement-stable norms, and only these: Sum_i |PF_i| (L1 total, continuum limit exists), nodal-force/nodal-area (a traction in pN/um^2), the signed coherent projection S, and the per-node implied DISPLACEMENT (a fixed length). One further statistical point for any max-based gate: max over N samples grows like the tail quantile (~sqrt(2*ln N) for a light-tailed field, and not at all convergent for a defect-dominated one), so a fixed per-node max threshold silently tightens with N even at a fixed physical state — a second, independent reason per-node max is unmaintainable.

(2) ASSEMBLE_BALANCE TOLERANCE — derived as ROUND-OFF, because the criterion is an algebraic identity, not a physical approximation. reaction + traction = 0 follows from Newton's 3rd law across adjoint connectors and equilibrium of the ECM sub-body; it is exact, so the only admissible tolerance is the float64 accumulation error of the reduction. Deriving it from physics would be wrong and would hide missing adjoints. RELATIVE FORM (required, so it does not break under N): |R + T| <= eps_bal * max(|R|, |T|, F_floor), eps_bal = 10 * sqrt(N_contrib) * eps64. Measured floors: sqrt(494,802)*eps64 = 1.56e-13; sqrt(655,362)*eps64 = 1.80e-13; sqrt(2,898,126)*eps64 = 3.78e-13 — so eps_bal ~ 1e-12 relative, tol_sq = (1e-12*max(|R|,|T|))^2. The existing test value 1.0e-18 pN^2 (= 1e-9 pN absolute) is ~6400x above the round-off floor: well-posed as a round-off check but absolute, so it tightens spuriously as N grows and must not be promoted to production. REQUIRED ADDITIONAL CHANNELS (without these the criterion has no content for the current PI priority): FIRST MOMENT M = Sum_i (x_i - x_c) x F_i, an INDEPENDENT identity because Sum F = 0 holds for equal-and-opposite pairs but Sum M = 0 requires them to be COLLINEAR — so the moment channel is the only thing that catches a connector transferring force along the wrong line of action, and ecm_world.py already promises a moment contribution in four Protocol docstrings (:205, :272, :293, :346) that no ledger channel can receive; CENTROID x_c = Sum m_i x_i / Sum m_i plus its rate, which is what makes 'the cell moved' an observable at all; and the TRACTION FIRST-MOMENT (dipole) tensor D = Sum (x_i - x_c) (x) T_i, nonzero for a crawler and zero for a symmetric sitter while Sum T is zero for both. That last one simultaneously gives the balance criterion content and creates the missing crawl-dipole observable — one of only two headline deficits that survived adversarial reading as real physics. Same tolerance logic applies to M (relative round-off), with the extra requirement that the moment arm be measured from a DECLARED centroid, since M is origin-dependent whenever Sum F != 0.

(3) CUT-PLANE TRANSMISSION IDENTITY — the discriminator that replaces residual/tension. For each SF segment j: T_j == Sum_{heads outboard} f_h . t_hat_j + Sum_{crosslinks outboard} f_xl . t_hat_j (+ FA reaction if the cut is outboard of an anchor). Exact at equilibrium, parameter-free, and independent of every GAP magnitude because both sides scale together. Report eps_j = |T_j - Sum_outboard| / max(|T_j|, |Sum_outboard|, F_floor). The right-hand side is computable from MOTOR state alone via abscissa: f_h = k_xb*(abscissa_h - r0_bind_h) projected on t_hat, with no reading of the SF axial length the solver is moving — which is what makes it independent of the k_axial GAP that contaminates the incumbent denominator. DISTINGUISHES: tension fell because the solve genuinely relaxed with a weaker drive (both sides fall together, eps_j small -> the small tension is REAL) from tension fell because the solve is stuck while heads are loaded (Sum != 0 with T ~ 0 -> eps_j -> 1 -> NOT converged) from tension not motor-generated at all (T large, Sum_h f_h ~ 0 -> eps_j -> 1 unless a crosslink accounts for it, which forces the report to NAME the carrier). CANNOT: see transverse non-equilibrium (axial projection only — pair with the per-node displacement channel); certify the state is physiological; distinguish a solver stalled in the WRONG basin (the identity holds at any equilibrium — needs gate C).

(4) GATE C — CONVERGED-vs-TRANSIENT with no physical constant. C1 FREEZE THE PHYSICS (mandatory): take one accepted state, disable ALL kinetics (no binding/unbinding, no abscissa advance, no topology change) and run only the inner solve. Without this the two arms are different physical problems — the exact confound in the existing control, since abscissa advances by tau*hill_velocity(load) once per accepted step, so relax length feeds back into the motor DRIVE, and 'identical bound population' is a COUNT that does not pin motor state. C2 run at effort n and r*n for r = 2 and r = 10, same seed, everything else identical. C3 report the relative drift for EVERY reported component: d_k = |O_k(rn) - O_k(n)| / (|O_k(rn)| + |O_k(n)| + floor_k), with floor_k the round-off floor of that observable's own reduction so d_k stays defined as O_k -> 0. Report the FULL vector (T_max, T_mean, gamma, traction radial mean, bound fraction, S), because a single scalar can be stationary by cancellation. C4 PASS requires max_k d_k <= 10^-p where p = the number of significant figures the closeout intends to QUOTE. This is not a physical constant; it is a declaration about the claim. Applied to the record: 0.451 -> 0.133 gives d = 0.545, which FAILS at p = 1 — the result cannot be quoted to even ONE significant figure. That is the withdrawal, derived with zero constants. C5 SOLVER-INDEPENDENCE (necessary, because C1-C4 is PASSED BY A STALL — a stalled iteration is trivially invariant under iteration count, and this is a live failure mode on record: 'scalar-damped Newton stalls at 0.78 pN', '0.0% position change over 3,000 iterations'). Two structurally DIFFERENT solvers with different fixed-point maps but the same F must agree to the same d; the pair already exists (explicit projected descent vs SFImplicitCG / ProjectedAnalyticCG) and the requirement is already written down as a comment at ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:402-403 and never implemented. C6 MOBILITY-INVARIANCE: --implicit-step-scale multiplies the IMEX regularizer a = 1/step; vary it 10x and require d <= 10^-p. Constant-free, independent, and the knob is already exposed. C7 CAUCHY-CONTRACTING: the sequence O(n), O(2n), O(4n), O(8n) must satisfy |O(4n) - O(2n)| <= |O(2n) - O(n)|. A non-contracting sequence is non-convergent even if two endpoints happen to agree — this is what rules out coincidental agreement. CANNOT: detect a wrong equilibrium that both solvers SHARE (a common modelling error, e.g. both inheriting the wrong projector), or a fixed point correct for the discretization but wrong in the continuum. That needs the grid-refinement channel, which must be ONE-PARAMETER: the committed 3-rung cortex series changed cortex_density_per_fil 20->40 at the finest rung and is unusable as written; the membrane subdiv 6->8 pair IS clean and already fails the L1-invariance test.

(5) META-GATE ON DERIVATIONS AND GATES — no check may be reported as a verification unless it has been observed to FAIL under some input. Sweep every input of every *_derivation.py / gate script to an absurd value and record the per-check fail count; any check surviving every sweep is labelled 'identity', not 'verification'. This is the generalisation of the finding that 4 of the 9 threshold-derivation checks cannot fail, and of the record that a results 'headline fingerprint' was byte-identical after the physics was swapped. Corollary gate: every metric named in a REPORT.md must resolve to a definition site in code (the 0.21 literal, in 72 places, resolves to none).

(6) DISCONNECTION NEGATIVE CONTROL — the standing gate for the current PI priority. For every one of the 32 connectors, run the composed slice with that connector contributing NO force and assert the run FAILS. Today it would pass: the PCG zero-RHS branch latches converged = 1, assemble_balance's |R + T| = 0, and every per-node force metric improves. cortex_overlap_mode='radial_span' has never been run natively. It is the landed, default-off fix for the kink whose kappa/seg^3 blow-up the code itself predicts at x288 and which produced the 3.42 fine-mesh plateau. Until it is run, no cortex grid-invariance statement is available at any mesh.
open_questions_for_pi: DECISION REQUIRED — membrane_subdivisions = 8 rests on a refuted claim. The committed numbers show the membrane residual is mesh-INVARIANT: Sum|PF| 26,379.5 -> 26,214.5 pN (0.63%) and mean pressure error 37.3 -> 37.1 pN/um^2 across a 16x refinement, while mean|PF| fell exactly as 1/N (16.1 vs 16.00). 'Textbook grid convergence' is the per-node partition of an unchanged field, and the residual total is 3.71x the entire turgor load at BOTH meshes. Consequences to rule on: (a) is 'GATE A CLOSED' withdrawn? (b) does membrane_subdivisions = 8 (commit ea0babc4) stand on other grounds — it is defensible on physiological-mesh grounds, just not on this one; (c) the same argument applies to the nucleus, whose 0.16 (the number that dominates the closure) is measured on an UN-refined 642-vertex mesh, so refining it would 'pass' the same way. I recommend: keep subdiv 8 for physiological reasons, withdraw the convergence justification, re-score in the L1 and traction norms, and measure S before any re-closure.

GATE CONTRACT — adopt the two-channel resting gate? LOCAL: max_i |PF_i|/K_ii <= min(2.7 nm, sqrt(kBT/K_ii)) using the Hessian diagonal already on device (regularization zeroed). GLOBAL: gamma_spur/gamma_target <= f, relative form. Note the local channel is TIGHTER than 0.21 pN by x134 at the ~494,802 actin bending nodes and looser only at the stiff minority, so it is not gate-loosening in the region that carries the tension measurement — but it IS a mixed-direction change and only PI can ratify that. Both channels are needed; neither substitutes for the other. Interim and unambiguously safe: replace the 72 frozen 0.21 literals with the per-run tolerance_um/dt_mu (both already in every report JSON) and report the dimensionless ratio — a no-op at seg 0.5 and a tightening at every finer mesh.

GATE CONTRACT — the coherent fraction f. I recommend ratifying the FORM now and the fraction only after S has been measured natively once, because f cannot be ratified from data that has not been taken. Also note f must be stated RELATIVE (gamma_spur/gamma_target), which makes it invariant to the live 3.3x Pi_0 spread (40 / 72 / 133 Pa); any absolute pN budget moves by 3.3x if Pi_0 is re-anchored.

GATE CONTRACT — assemble_balance tolerance. I recommend the ROUND-OFF derivation, relative form, eps_bal = 10*sqrt(N_contrib)*eps64 ~ 1e-12, on the explicit ground that reaction + traction = 0 is an ALGEBRAIC identity and not a physical approximation, so any physics-scaled tolerance would be hiding a missing adjoint. This needs PI ratification because it is a gate contract, and it needs the accompanying ruling that the criterion is INCOMPLETE without the moment and centroid channels — as scoped it audits the ECM solve but is identically zero for a crawling cell and blind to line-of-action.

PRIORITISE the moment + centroid + traction-dipole channels. They are one reduction each, they give the only global acceptance criterion actual content, and the dipole tensor simultaneously closes the missing crawl observable. Under the stated long-run purpose (infer molecular parameters from macroscopic data), a ledger with no moment and no centroid cannot constrain a crawling cell at all, so every inferred parameter for a motile state would be unconstrained in the modes that matter.

RETRACTION CANDIDATE — the 200 nm cortex rung, documented as 'the known-good rung (weak solver already reaches 0.21)', is re-opened by arithmetic alone: the runtime's own bound at seg 0.2 is 0.0843, so the frozen literal was 2.49x looser and the reported 0.21 is a 2.5x FAIL. No new run required.

SCOPE — the fine-mesh 3-rung cortex series (0.14 / 0.21 / 3.42) changed cortex_density_per_fil 20->40 at the finest rung and so cannot support any grid-invariance argument as written. Separately, the codebase's own comment predicts the 3.42 plateau mechanically (transverse-shove kink, kappa/seg^3, x288 predicted vs (0.5/0.075)^3 = 296 measured) and ships a default-off fix (cortex_overlap_mode='radial_span') that has never been run natively. Decision: re-run the series as a ONE-PARAMETER refinement with radial_span before any statement about fine-mesh convergence.

AUDIT CORRECTION — GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md needs three fixes before it can be cited: (a) 4 of 9 checks cannot fail under any exposed input, not 3, and the fourth (route_c_scales_linearly_in_seg) is an algebraic identity that hard-codes the very assumption it claims to verify while the script's own kmax table contains the term that would break it; (b) its dt_mu formula omits a live limb — the executing dt_mu = 0.1/max(k_mech, |dp|*pressure_edge_um), so the implied force bound is state-dependent, not a constant of the run; (c) it rejects route (b) as 'ill-posed for a multi-stiffness network' by collapsing a per-node criterion into one scalar and then objecting that the scalar spans 5 decades — the per-node form is the correct answer and its heterogeneity is the physics. The document is otherwise the most useful thing on disk in this family and its central finding (the gate is a machine-precision criterion wearing a physics label) is correct and independently confirmed.

MODELLING DECISION, now with two numbers attached. f_head = 1.5 pN is 0.73x sqrt(kBT*k_xb) = 2.07 pN — the resting load is smaller than the thermal force noise of the spring applying it — and the residual/tension instrument that was supposed to certify the SF tension has a denominator proportional to k_axial, a constant sf_mechanics.py declares a GAP because NF2007 REJECTS an axial penalty spring. Either k_xb (the PI-GAP 'MASTER knob') is too stiff, or a single resting crossbridge is not a meaningful mechanical unit and the resting prestress must be represented as a coarse-grained mean field. This is the same escalation as project-ac-gate-a-p02-p03-native, and it now blocks the convergence instrument as well as the physics.

WORDING RULE — every GATE-A/B closeout should say 'the athermal mechanical equilibrium was located to <numerical criterion>; thermal force noise at the loaded bonds is <value>' and never 'the cell is at rest to within X pN'. The second sentence is not supportable at 310 K at any threshold, since 0.21 pN is below the thermal force floor of every stiff bond in the model (x9.8 below a crossbridge, x210 below an alpha-actinin crosslink). Corollary rule: a residual below sqrt(kBT*K_ii) may be reported only as an unconverged athermal minimisation, never as a physical non-equilibrium — and this ceiling must NEVER be swapped in as a pass criterion, since it is looser than 0.21 by x9.8 to x210.

STANDING META-GATES, two, both cheap and both aimed at the failure mode that commissioned this audit: (i) no check may be called a verification unless it has been watched failing under some input — report per-check fail counts; (ii) every metric named in a REPORT.md must resolve to a definition site in code. The 0.21 literal, in 72 places across ~30 files, resolves to none, and that is how a reporting contract with no derivation survived for weeks as the project's blocking gate.

THE DISCONNECTION CONTROL is the gate for your stated priority and it would fail today. With one connector contributing zero force, the PCG zero-RHS branch latches converged = 1, assemble_balance's |R + T| = 0, and every per-node force metric IMPROVES. Until a zero-transfer connector is a hard FAIL, 'compartments are mechanically connected so they deform each other' cannot be measured — only asserted. I recommend this as the first instrument built, ahead of any magnitude work, because it is the cheapest test that converts the current priority into an observable.

result.family: FAMILY 1 — force and stress instruments in the live ffn_cellsim tree

instruments.name: method_of_planes_gamma — the outer rectification mean|γ_n|
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Cortical tension γ [pN/µm]: a signed surface tension that is 0 for an unloaded network and negative for a network in compression.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: mean over 64 diametral planes of the ABSOLUTE per-plane cut force divided by a fixed 2πR. Because the absolute value is taken AFTER the per-plane sum, the estimator is a rectifier: it cannot return zero for any network with tension scatter, it grows as sqrt(M_crossing), and it is blind to the sign of the whole network.
instruments.evidence: Measured on this Mac (numpy only, no CUDA). Zero-mean random per-element tensions, sd(T)=1 pN, on a 7.5 µm shell: M=1e2 → γ=0.016; 1e3 → 0.071; 1e4 → 0.223; 1e5 → 0.631 pN/µm — a network carrying literally NO net tension reports positive γ that grows as sqrt(M). At the native element counts the floor is γ=1.32 pN/µm for the 424,116 actin segments alone (494,802 nodes / 70,686 filaments = 6 seg each) and 2.14 pN/µm for the 1,413,720 inter-fiber crosslinks, per 1 pN of per-element tension scatter. The flagship GATE-B number is γ_network = 3.7043 pN/µm (AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:70) — i.e. the instrument's own rectified zero-tension floor is of the SAME ORDER as the reported observable, and the per-element scatter needed to evaluate it is recorded nowhere. Separately: all-T=−1 (pure compression) and all-T=+1 (pure tension) both return γ=0.3560 — identical, so a fully buckled cortex is indistinguishable from a tensed one. The port from archive/hoomd_legacy/cortex/cortical_tension.py:288 is faithful, so the defect is inherited, not introduced. No test in tests/ff/test_gamma_estimator.py or tests/ac/cell/test_cortical_tension.py feeds a zero-mean or compressive tension set.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Feed the estimator per-element tensions drawn from N(0, sd) with sd = the run's own measured per-element tension scatter. It must return γ ≈ 0. It returns 0.6–2.7 pN/µm. Second control: negate every tension; γ must change sign. It does not change at all.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Return the SIGNED across-plane mean plus its across-plane standard deviation, and require |mean|/sd >> 1 as the detection criterion. Measured on the same shells: a null network gives |mean|/sd = 0.07 while a genuinely tensed one gives 6.0–52. This is magnitude-free, costs nothing, restores sign-sense, and makes the noise floor a reported number instead of an unknown.

instruments.name: method_of_planes_gamma applied as CORTICAL tension (fixed input R, label-blind element set)
instruments.where: /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ff/gamma_estimator.py:79 (R is a scalar argument, never measured); /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/cell/assembled_cortical_stress.py:121-129 (all fibers, no compartment filter); /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:306 (R_CORTEX_UM constant)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The in-plane tension of the cortical SHELL, normalised by the actual cut circumference of that shell.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The total force crossing a whole-cell mid-plane — from ANY element, cortex or interior — divided by 2π × a radius supplied by the caller as a constant. For a deformed or adherent cell the true cut length is not 2πR, and for a composed cell the crossing set is not the cortex.
instruments.evidence: (a) Interior contamination, measured: 2,000 cortical tangential segments at T=1 pN give γ=0.7201; adding just 20 straight interior fibres at 50 pN gives γ=11.33 — a 1,473 % inflation of a quantity named 'cortical tension'. assembled_cortical_stress.measure_assembled_cortical_stress builds its families from pos[:n_actin] over cell.foff_d with NO compartment label, so the moment SF / lamellipodium / filopodium filaments enter the same array (which the ac/engine roadmap requires), every one of them is counted as cortical tension. (b) R is an input: the same physical isotropic tension on an oblate (spread) shell reads 1.4552 / 1.2699 / 0.9953 pN/µm at aspect scale 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 with R held at 7.5 — a 32 % swing from geometry alone, in the direction that UNDERSTATES tension as the cell spreads. The PI's stated baseline is an adherent cell on 2D collagen, i.e. exactly the configuration where this breaks. (c) This was already diagnosed and the fix never landed: docs/v2_audit/H7_SURFACE_MANIFOLD_EXPLICIT_CORTEX_2026-06-07.md:121 says 'Demote flat-plane MOP to cross-check … both become ill-defined on a spread/deformed cell'. It is still the γ instrument ac/ imports today.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Scale the cell to an oblate shape at FIXED per-element tension and require γ to be invariant. It moves 32 %. Second control: run the estimator twice, once on cortex-labelled elements only and once on all elements, and require agreement within the noise floor; on a composed cell they will differ by >10×.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Measure the cut length geometrically per plane (sum of the arc lengths of the cortex-surface ∩ plane intersection from the live triangulation) instead of assuming 2πR, and restrict the crossing set by component ID from the PopulationLedger. Both are already available on device.

instruments.name: measure_cortical_stress — the γ_source / γ_network / γ_total split
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A decomposition of cortical stress into what myosin injects, what the network carries, and the AFM-comparable total.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that, and it correctly retired the earlier Σ F_i·r̂_i 'tension' that self-cancelled ~1015× (docstring :3-9). It keeps the legacy radial scalar and the net-force vector but explicitly labels them Newton-closure diagnostics, NOT tensions. Including the actin inextensibility (Lagrange) tension in the element set is CORRECT here — a rigid rod under tension transmits real force across a plane.
instruments.evidence: The construction is right and the split is the physically meaningful one. The 1015× self-cancellation artifact it replaced is documented and the replaced observable is retained under an honest name. Its defects are inherited from the kernel it wraps (entries 1 and 2), not introduced here. One genuine internal asymmetry worth noting: assembled_cortical_stress.py:17-20 claims the reconstructed actin tension 'carries EVERYTHING the myosin injects and the crosslinks transmit — no double-count' and then adds crosslinks as a SEPARATE family into γ_total. For method-of-planes that is legitimate (both element types genuinely cross the plane), but the docstring's justification is wrong and invites a future double-count fix that would be the actual error.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: On a shell with a KNOWN analytic tension (uniform Π₀ balanced by a hoop), require γ_total = Π₀R/2 within the reported across-plane sd. This is the one place a Young-Laplace comparison is a real oracle rather than a tautology.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None needed. Fix the entry-1/2 kernel underneath it and correct the assembled_cortical_stress docstring's no-double-count sentence.

instruments.name: actin_axial_tension — Lagrange tension reconstructed as a one-ended running sum
instruments.where: /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/ac/cell/assembled_cortical_stress.py:42-75 (T_k = −(Σ_{j≤k} f_ext[j])·û_k, always accumulated from the LOW-index end at :66-71)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The per-segment axial tension of the inextensible actin backbone — the primary cortical load path.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The running sum of external nodal force from one arbitrarily chosen filament end. This equals the true constraint tension ONLY if the filament's net external force is zero. Off equilibrium it is systematically biased, and the bias is exactly the unbalanced net force, applied with the OPPOSITE sign depending on which end you start from. The module's own docstring names the required check ('A per-filament net force of ≈0 at equilibrium is the physical consistency check') and the code never performs it.
instruments.evidence: Measured: a 7-node filament in true balance gives T = 3.0 pN uniformly from either end. Add a 0.1398 pN/node residual — the exact value GATE-A recorded as its PASS state — and the reconstruction gives T = [2.86 … 2.16] from end A and [3.14 … 3.84] from end B: a 0.9786 pN end-to-end disagreement on a nominal 3 pN tension, 32.6 %. The disagreement equals |Σ f_ext| on the filament, i.e. the residual is silently converted into tension. This instrument is the source of 99.5 % of the flagship GATE-B number (γ_network 3.7043 vs γ_source 0.0191 pN/µm), and the state it was measured on has max|PF| plateauing near 0.5 pN — 2.4× the static gate. It is also the same failure mode as the already-withdrawn 'T = 1.92 pN PASS' (outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/sf_motor_native_gate.json: residual_over_tension = 0.1553, and a 10× longer relax moved T_max by 3.4×).
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Reconstruct from BOTH ends and report max|T_A − reverse(T_B)| alongside T. On a converged state it is ~0; on the committed states it is of order the reported tension. Free, deterministic, and it is the same quantity as the per-filament |Σ f_ext| the docstring already asks for.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Read the Lagrange multipliers λ directly out of project_constraint_forces_kernel (inner_mechanics.py:126-136 already computes them by Thomas solve) instead of re-deriving them by quadrature on the host. λ is the tension, needs no equilibrium assumption, and is end-symmetric by construction.

instruments.name: cortex_node_stress — per-node virial Cauchy / von-Mises stress
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The full per-node Cauchy stress of the cortex, in Pa, with a pressure channel and a von-Mises channel.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The virial of crosslink + myosin bonds ONLY, with the bond term carrying the OPPOSITE sign convention from the turgor term in the same tensor, divided by a caller-supplied uniform per-node volume.
instruments.evidence: Three measured defects. (1) SIGN: one crosslink stretched to F = +5 pN tension gives σ_xx = −2.500 Pa in this code, while the turgor term at :55 adds −ΔP to the diagonal and the pressure at :60 is −tr(σ)/3, which returns +40 Pa for ΔP=40 — i.e. the turgor limb uses the standard σ = −pI convention and the bond limb uses its negation. The two are SUMMED into one tensor, so a tensile network's contribution to 'pressure' has the same sign as a compressive one: the reported pressure for a tensile bond is +0.833 Pa. σ_vm is immune because von-Mises is invariant under σ → −σ (verified: vm(s) = vm(−s) = 3.763236), so the vm field cannot detect this and every existing viewer reads only vm. (2) OMISSION: the actin inextensibility (Lagrange) tension — which assembled_cortical_stress.py:17 calls the carrier of 'EVERYTHING the myosin injects' — is not a carrier here at all, and bending is excluded by design (:11). So 'cortex node stress' is a crosslink+myosin-only stress. (3) NORMALISATION: every caller passes node_vol = np.full(Nc, V0/Nc) (scripts/ff_resting_full_compartment.py:50, ff_crawl_on_substrate.py:803, ff_s1_sphere.py:113), an arbitrary uniform partition; the Pa magnitude scales as 1/V_node and is therefore not grid-invariant.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Uniaxially stretch a two-node bond and require σ_xx > 0 (it is negative). Then apply an isotropic tension plus a turgor and require the pressure channel to be the DIFFERENCE of the two contributions (it is the sum). Then double the node count at fixed physical state and require σ to be invariant (it halves).
instruments.canonical_replacement: Fix the bond sign to σ = −(1/V) Σ r_ij ⊗ f_ij (force on i from j), add the actin constraint tension as a carrier, and derive node_vol from the local mesh (cortex thickness × dual-cell area) rather than V0/Nc. Rename to crosslink_myosin_node_stress until the constraint carrier is in.

instruments.name: max|PF| as the constrained stationarity residual (the NF2007 projector)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The unbalanced force at a constrained equilibrium: PF = F − Jᵀλ = 0.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that, and the |F| → |PF| change at GATE A is physically CORRECT. Verified independently: the constraints are internal (C_k = g_k·g_k − L²), so every per-fiber rigid translation AND rotation lies in null(J) — J row k contracts g_k with (δx_{k+1} − δx_k), which is zero for a translation and equals g·(ω×g) = 0 for a rotation. Therefore the projector CANNOT annihilate a genuine unbalanced net force or torque on a filament; what it removes is precisely the part of the force field that would produce axial strain, which a rigid rod legitimately absorbs.
instruments.evidence: The GATE-A split 5.7892 = 4.4820 (|Jᵀλ|) + 1.7399 (|PF|) with |C| = 1.1e-16 (GATE_A_RESTING_CONVERGENCE_2026-07-23.md:263-265) is a correct decomposition, not a metric change of convenience: 4.48 pN was real backbone tension held by the constraint, not residual. Numerical soundness also checks out — I computed cond(JJᵀ) for the tridiagonal system at 3 µm filament length: 19.2 at seg=500 nm, 681 at 75 nm, 6.5e4 at 8 nm, giving float64 relative errors of 4e-15 / 1.5e-13 / 1.4e-11. So projector conditioning can be POSITIVELY EXCLUDED as an explanation for the fine-mesh 3.42 pN plateau; the construction-kink attribution stands. CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH |PF| IS RIGHT: (i) the backbone is modelled as a hard length constraint, (ii) max|C| is bounded in the SAME predicate (it is, at :295), (iii) the J used to build P is the identical constraint set the runtime enforces, and (iv) no other constraint (Dirichlet pin, weld) is active on the same node outside J. CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH IT IS WRONG: whenever the backbone is an extensible spring — which is the case in the SF lane RIGHT NOW (ac/engine/sf_mechanics.py:251-284 models the same actin backbone as a Hookean k_axial and states 'NF2007 treats the actin backbone as INEXTENSIBLE … no sourced EA_actin'). There, projecting would delete real elastic force and raw |F| is the correct residual. So the tree contains two incompatible models of one physical object and therefore two incompatible correct residual norms, with no cross-calibration test on disk.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Apply a pure rigid-body force to one filament and require |PF| = |F| (nothing is projected away). Then apply a pure axial stretch couple at the two ends and require |PF| = 0 while |Jᵀλ| = the applied force. Then take k_axial → ∞ in the SF lane and require its k(L−r0) tension to converge to the cortex lane's λ — this cross-calibration does not exist.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Keep |PF|, but report it PER COMPONENT rather than as one whole-cell max. The current max is taken over n_total, mixing projected fiber nodes with UNPROJECTED membrane/nucleus nodes (the projector only overwrites fiber nodes, :93), so one scalar conflates two different quantities and cannot say which compartment is unconverged.

instruments.name: max|PF| < 0.21 pN as the warrant that a reported γ is uncontaminated
instruments.where: gate literal in 54 sites / 22 files (e.g. /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/scripts/ac_resting_converge.py:1,40,57); derivation in /Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim/ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md
instruments.what_its_name_implies: That a state passing the gate can be measured on: the reported cortical tension is not an artifact of an unconverged solve.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A per-node max of a force density × mesh spacing, at a threshold that is the float64 round-off displacement tolerance divided by the CFL step. It places NO bound whatsoever on the coherent radial part of the residual, which is the only part that contaminates γ.
instruments.evidence: Arithmetic I ran: at R = 7.5 µm and N = 494,802 nodes, a worst-case coherent radial residual at the gate value gives a spurious γ_spur = N·|PF|/(8πR) of 367 pN/µm at max|PF| = 0.1398 (the GATE-A PASS), 551 at 0.21, 1654 at 0.63, 8978 at 3.42. For scale, γ_target = Π₀R/2 = 150 pN/µm, the whole physiological load Π₀πR² = 7069 pN, and the reported γ_network is 3.70 pN/µm. So the PASSING gate leaves headroom for ~100× the flagship observable and ~2.4× the entire physiological tension. instruments.name: _fa_traction — Dirichlet reaction read as focal-adhesion traction

instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The reaction of an infinitely stiff, infinitely strong kinematic constraint. There is no integrin, no bond lifetime, no substrate compliance and no area in this measurement: the number is whatever the (unconverged) network happens to pull with, and 'F_total_pN' at :189 is a sum of MAGNITUDES, not a resultant, so it cannot see a sign split.
instruments.evidence: The reported magnitude is contaminated at the same level as the tension: committed run outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/sf_motor_native_gate.json final step gives fa_radial_mean_pN = −0.1320 with residual_sf_free_pN = 0.0395 — 30 % of the reaction, on a state whose own verdict field says inner_solve_converged_relative_to_tension = false and whose quantitative_claim_status is BLOCKED. instruments.name: fa_inward_fraction — the contractile sign test
instruments.what_its_name_implies: That the emergent adhesion load is contractile rather than sign-flipped.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that — the sign of ⟨F, r̂⟩ at each pinned anchor against a fixed centroid of the initial population. It is a genuine sign-sense check and it is the right CLASS of check: magnitude-free, cheap, and it catches the sign-flip bug it was written for.
instruments.evidence: Reported 100 % inward at the final step, 0 % at step 1 where 113 heads are bound but no power stroke has accumulated (T_abs_max = 5.6e-14) — so the metric does discriminate. Caveats, not defects: it is weak evidence (any closed dipole with both ends held pulls inward, so only a sign-flipped motor can fail it); the centroid is the mean of INITIAL positions and does not track deformation; anchors near the centroid get r̂ = 0 and are counted as not-inward, which is conservative. The one thing worth changing is that the verdict reads only the final step, so a non-monotone or early sign inversion is invisible to the verdict even though it is in the trace.

instruments.name: gamma_apparent_pN_um = 0.5 * dP * R_eq
instruments.what_its_name_implies: An apparent cortical tension measured from a parallel-plate / AFM compression, comparable to the published liquid-drop tension.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The imposed turgor ΔP multiplied by a geometric radius, divided by two. It contains no mechanical measurement at all — no plate force, no cortex state, no myosin. It is the Young-Laplace identity evaluated on its own input.
instruments.evidence: This is the 120.0000-degree class, and it has already produced a false result. Reported γ = 0.150 mN/m as an interphase match (FF_STAGE6V_TENSION_IS_PRESSURE_BORNE_2026-07-01.md:24-27, 'ΔP=40 → γ=0.150 ≈ experimental interphase'), invariant at 0.1502 across 0.05→0.45 strain (FF_STAGE6W:63-66) and across confinement (FF_STAGE6Z:40-51) — invariance that was read as a physical 'confinement-independent γ' result but is the arithmetic signature of an identity. AUDIT_WHOLE_REPO_2026-07-25.md:40 already states it: 'γ = ΔP·R/2 IS an identity at ΔP=40 Pa, R=7.5 µm — an exact match means the active myosin contribution was indistinguishable from zero (P3.2 records γ_active = 0.0064 pN/µm)', i.e. 4e-5 of the reported γ. The circularity is doubled because ΔP itself is not sourced: forces_manifest.py:376-383 classifies Π₀ as CONVENIENCE (40 Pa HeLa proxy) and gamma_floor.py:470 records that the 133 Pa variant is 'band-implied / tuned … so ΔP·R/2 reproducing the band is CIRCULAR'. instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Vary myosin activity (or f_head) over a decade at fixed ΔP and require gamma_apparent to move. It cannot move by construction. instruments.canonical_replacement: Report gamma_from_plate_force = (F_plate/(π a²))·R_eq/2 as the observable — that is the real protocol an AFM/plate experiment uses — and keep ΔP·R/2 only as a labelled analytic prediction to compare against. Rename the current field gamma_laplace_identity_from_imposed_dP.

instruments.name: GlobalCellLedger.assemble_balance — the global force-balance acceptance gate
instruments.what_its_name_implies: A genuine Newton's-third-law check on the cell↔ECM coupling — the docstring at :10-22 explicitly claims the two channels are 'independently sourced so the global force-balance gate is a genuine check, not a tautology'.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: |Σreaction + Σtraction|², where reaction is defined as R = −f at each pinned ECM node (ecm_world.py:403-411). Summing over the ECM body, internal forces cancel pairwise and Σ(external loads) + Σ(reaction) = 0 IDENTICALLY the moment the ECM solve is at equilibrium. Both channels are ECM-side quantities, so the gate tests the ECM solve's convergence, not the adjointness of the connector.
instruments.evidence: A connector that applied T to the ECM and received T' ≠ −T on the cell side would pass this gate unchanged, because no cell-side force enters it — and connector adjointness is the single property the whole component/connector architecture rests on. Three further findings stack on top: (1) NO TOLERANCE EXISTS. tol_sq_d defaults to None in sf_motor_slice.py:310, erm_cortex_slice.py:298 and cortex_motor_slice.py:626, and transaction.py:134 only assembles the gate `if tol_sq_d is not None`. No value is defined in any code, YAML, or doc. (2) THE GATE HAS NEVER RUN. The committed GATE-B driver passes accepted_d = wp.array(np.ones(1, np.int32)) (:497) — every step is force-accepted and the balance gate is skipped entirely, which AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:70 also records. (3) NO MOMENT CHANNEL. Three LedgerContributor docstrings promise one — ecm_world.py:205 ('equal/opposite force, moment, energy'), :272, :293, :346 — and GlobalCellLedger has no moment accumulator to receive it. A force resultant is identically zero for ANY force dipole, so this gate cannot distinguish a contractile cell from a spreading one from no cell at all.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Deliberately break the adjoint: scale the cell-side reaction of one connector by 0.9 and require the gate to fail. It will pass. Then apply an equal-and-opposite pair at ±x and require the gate to detect a nonzero dipole. It cannot.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Two channels per CONNECTOR, not per body: sum the force the connector scatters on side A and on side B and gate |F_A + F_B|² (a true adjointness test), plus a work-conjugacy test W_A + W_B ≈ 0. Add moment_resultant_d (Σ x × F, and the symmetric contractile moment Σ (x·â)(F·â)) so the ledger can see a dipole. Ratify a tolerance and stop passing accepted_d = 1.

instruments.name: _anchor_dipole — 'traction-dipole magnitude'
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The traction dipole a stress fiber delivers to the substrate — the quantity comparable to a published contractile moment.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The larger of the two end reactions, a FORCE in units of f_head [pN], not a dipole moment [pN·µm]. Taking the max rather than the antisymmetric part means a strongly asymmetric configuration that hands net force to the network reports the same 'dipole' as a self-equilibrated one.
instruments.evidence: Dimensional: a force dipole / contractile moment is Σ_a (x_a·â)(F_a·â) with units pN·µm; this returns pN. The companion residual = |R_lo + R_hi| at :299 is genuinely useful and correctly described (~0 for a ventral both-ends fiber, ≈ the dipole for a dorsal one-end fiber), so the balance information is there — only the dipole is misnamed and mis-formed. This is also the surviving-deficit instrument: the absence of a crawl force dipole is one of the only two headline deficits that survived adversarial reading, and the tree's one thing named 'dipole' is not a dipole.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Rigidly translate the whole fiber population. A true dipole moment about the population centroid is invariant; a max-of-end-reactions is too, so instead: hold the two end forces fixed and double the fiber LENGTH. A dipole moment must double; this quantity does not change at all.
instruments.canonical_replacement: P = Σ_a (x_a − x_c)·â × (F_a·â) in pN·µm, reported with the net resultant |Σ F_a| beside it, computed from real clutch forces rather than anchor reactions. Rename the present field larger_end_reaction_pN.

instruments.name: SF-lane residual _max_force_norm(force, free_mask) — raw max|F| over free nodes
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The inner solve's residual on the free (non-Dirichlet) nodes.
