instruments.name: spread_eval verdict logic (the only spreading GATE in the repo)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Discriminates GENUINE COLLECTIVE SPREAD from PEELING from no-spread.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A boolean combination of six undeclared constants over metrics it does not itself define: spreads = aa0_final > 1.10; flattens = maxZ_drop_pct > 3.0 OR psi_final < psi_init - 0.01; cohesive = peeling_index < 8.0; stable = |vv0_final - 1| < 0.05; and PEELING if peeling_index > 20. It reads `aa0`, `maxZ`, `vv0`, `pen_frac` straight out of the npz, so it inherits whatever definition produced them.
instruments.evidence: Six thresholds (1.10, 3.0, 0.01, 8.0, 20, 0.05) with no derivation and no reference anywhere on disk — the same class of defect as the undocumented max|PF| < 0.21 pN resting gate. The 'flattens' criterion is an OR, and its second branch (sphericity drop) is satisfied by ANY shape change including mesh degeneration: in the committed runs psi_final = 0.322 against psi_init ~ 1.0, so those runs pass 'flattens' even though maxZ did NOT drop (15.00 -> 15.10/15.63/16.01). Sphericity itself is mesh-dependent (psi = pi^(1/3)(6V)^(2/3)/A_mesh with A_mesh < A_true, so psi is biased HIGH on coarse meshes and drifts with refinement). And the whole module is DCM-scoped and unreachable from ac/.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Replace the OR with an AND on the two independent flattening channels (h_mean = V/A_sil must decrease AND z_p99-p1 must decrease), derive each threshold from a stated published spread-cell geometry (e.g. adherent MCF7 h_mean ~3-5 um) with the citation recorded next to the constant, and compute psi from the CLOSED-mesh area of the same triangulation used for V so the two are discretization-consistent. Port the gate into ac/ so it is reachable from the canonical engine.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Feed it the committed native_spread_C_sub2 npz (z-extent 15.00 -> 16.01, area inflation 3.17x) and assert the verdict is NOT 'GENUINE COLLECTIVE SPREAD'. Also feed it a synthetic pure area-inflation state (surface area x3, height unchanged) and assert rejection.

instruments.name: validation/oracles/osmotic_response.shape_factors.area_ratio — the only closed-form geometric oracle in the repo
instruments.where: ffn_sim/validation/oracles/osmotic_response.py:222-247 (ShapeFactors.area_ratio documented in-line as 'A/A_0 = v^(2*alpha)  (top-down footprint)'), gated by ffn_sim/tests/ac/fluid/test_osmotic_response_oracle.py:125-137
instruments.what_its_name_implies: An independent analytic target a measured A/A0 could be validated against.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A kinematic identity of an ASSUMED affine stretch decomposition: lam_x = lam_y = v^alpha, lam_z = v^(1-2alpha), A/A0 = v^(2alpha), h/h0 = v^(1-2alpha), with alpha a free parameter in [0, 0.5]. Given any measured (A/A0, V/V0) pair one can always solve alpha = ln(A/A0) / (2 ln(V/V0)) — so the relation cannot fail unless alpha is independently fixed.
instruments.evidence: The test suite only checks the two corner cases (alpha = 1/3 isotropic; alpha = 0 fixed-footprint) and the volume-conservation identity lam_x*lam_y*lam_z == v, which holds by construction (:245). With alpha free the oracle has one adjustable parameter and one equation, so as an ACCEPTANCE oracle for a measured A/A0 it is vacuous. Compounding it, the docstring at :228 calls the sanctioned quantity a 'top-down FOOTPRINT' — 'footprint' is a member of FORBIDDEN_METRICS. Whoever wires this oracle to a spreading gate will be comparing a top-down silhouette against a formula documented as a footprint, with no code-level check that they are the same thing. This is the exact naming-collision shape of the two historical basal-vs-top-down failures.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Use it only as a CONSTRAINT, never as a gate: fix alpha from the boundary condition (alpha = 0 for a pinned adhesion footprint, alpha = 1/3 for a free suspended cell) BEFORE the run, then assert the measured (A_sil/A_sil0, h_mean/h_mean0, V/V0) triple satisfies both v^(2alpha) and v^(1-2alpha) simultaneously — two equations, zero free parameters. And rename `area_ratio` to `projected_area_ratio` with the docstring word 'footprint' removed.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Feed the oracle a physically impossible pair (A/A0 = 5 with V/V0 = 1.0) and assert it raises or fails. Today it silently returns alpha = infinity's limit and the volume identity still passes.

instruments.name: node control volume reused as the virial stress normalisation
instruments.where: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:920-933 (node_vol[:n_actin] = cell_vol / max(n_actin,1)); the same uniform partition is passed as the stress denominator at ffn_sim/scripts/ff_resting_full_compartment.py:49-50 and ffn_sim/scripts/ff_cortex_deform_viewer.py:35/54 (np.full(Nc, V0/Nc)); consumed by ffn_sim/ff/ff_virial_stress.py:33-61
instruments.what_its_name_implies: sigma_node = (1/V_node) * sum(1/2 r_ij (x) f_ij) — a per-node Cauchy stress in Pa, comparable to published cortical stress values.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: A stress normalised by V_cell/N_actin, which is the correct partition for the Biot body force -alpha*V*grad(p) (the skeleton must carry the whole domain's pressure gradient) but is the WRONG volume for a virial: the cortical bonds occupy a 0.2 um shell, not the whole cell. The same array serves two incompatible physical roles. It is also frozen at the reference configuration, so the reported quantity is a nominal, not a Cauchy, stress.
instruments.evidence: cell_vol = 1767 um^3 over n_actin = 494,802 gives V_node = 3.571e-3 um^3. The shell-consistent value is 4*pi*(7.40)^2*0.20 / 494,802 = 2.78e-4 um^3 — 12.8x smaller. So every reported cortical von-Mises stress in Pa is understated by ~12.8x relative to a shell-volume normalisation, and the factor changes if the cortex thickness or the node count changes, i.e. it is not grid-invariant. The correct pattern already exists in the canonical engine: ffn_sim/ac/engine/fluid_core.py:654-682 lumped_surface_control_volumes builds a mesh-derived partition-of-unity control volume V_node = (1/3)*sum(incident face area)*dx with the stated identity sum(V_node) == total_surface_area * dx, asserted to rtol 1e-12 at ffn_sim/tests/ac/engine/test_fluid_core.py:565. That is exactly the construction ff_virial_stress needs and does not use.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Two DISTINCT arrays with distinct names: node_volume_biot (um^3, partition of the cell domain, sum == V_cell) for the pressure body force; and node_volume_material (um^3, the material volume the node's bonds occupy: for the cortex a lumped one-ring shell volume, sum == 4*pi*R^2*h_cortex) for the virial normalisation. Update node_volume_material each accepted step if the reported quantity is to be called a Cauchy stress; otherwise rename it nominal_stress.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Assert sum(node_volume_material) == the cortical shell volume to rtol 1e-12 (it currently equals the whole cell volume, 12.8x too large). Second control: refine the cortex from seg_um 0.5 to 0.075 and assert the reported p95 sigma_vm is unchanged to <5%; with a V_cell/N normalisation it will shift because N changes while the shell volume does not.

instruments.name: basal_frac and splay (the auxiliary spreading shape descriptors)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The fraction of the cell in basal contact, and how splayed the cell is.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: basal_frac = mean(z < z.min() + 2e-6) — the fraction of NODES within an undeclared 2 um of the lowest node, referenced to the lowest NODE rather than to the substrate plane. splay = A_hull / (pi * p90(r_xy)^2) — a convex-hull numerator divided by a 90th-percentile-radius denominator, so it is neither an area ratio nor a shape factor and its value depends on how the node density is distributed radially.
instruments.evidence: The 2 um contact band has no derivation and is ~13% of the cell radius — an order of magnitude above any adhesion length scale (the clutch capture radius and adh_energy_range are sub-um). Because the reference is z.min() (a single node) rather than the substrate plane z = 0, a single node punching below the floor shifts the whole band. basal_frac is also a NODE-count fraction, so it changes with mesh refinement even for identical geometry: in the committed runs it reads 0.265 / 0.354 / 0.348 across subdiv 2/3/4 with the same physics — a 34% swing. splay mixes definitions and has no analytic reference value for any shape.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Replace basal_frac with A_contact (um^2, defined below in missing_instruments) — an AREA, not a node count, referenced to the substrate plane, not to the lowest node. Delete splay, or replace it with the dimensionless shape anisotropy sqrt(lambda_1/lambda_2) from the projected second-moment tensor, which has an analytic value of 1 for a disc.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Assert every contact descriptor is unchanged to <2% between subdiv 3 and subdiv 4 on identical physics. basal_frac moves 0.354 -> 0.348 in the committed runs and 0.265 -> 0.354 from subdiv 2 -> 3 (a 34% jump).

instruments.name: interpenetration count (n_interpenetrating_pre / _post)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The number of interpenetrating nodes the cortex builder produced.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: The number of nodes with nonzero WCA steric force, i.e. nodes closer than r_cut = 2^(1/6)*sigma_EV = 7.86 nm to a node on another fiber. This IS geometric (WCA force > 0 iff r < r_cut), so it is sound in kind, but it is a raw COUNT and therefore not comparable across mesh resolutions.
instruments.evidence: Refining seg_um from 0.5 um to 0.075 um multiplies the node count per filament ~6.7x (494,802 -> ~2.9M nodes) while the physical overlap geometry is unchanged, so the raw count grows ~6.7x for the same physics. The historically quoted 64,517 -> 0 improvement is therefore only interpretable at a fixed mesh. The instrument also counts NODES, not overlapping PAIRS or overlap volume, so two fibers crossing once and two fibers crossing ten times can produce the same count.
instruments.canonical_replacement: Report the dimensionless overlap fraction f_overlap := n_overlapping_pairs / n_candidate_pairs, plus the maximum penetration depth normalised by sigma_EV (max(1 - r_min/r_cut), dimensionless, 0 = touching, 1 = coincident). Both are grid-invariant: the first because both counts scale together, the second because it is a length ratio at a mesh-independent physical scale.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Build the SAME cortex geometry at seg_um 0.5 and 0.075 and assert the overlap observable agrees to <10%. The raw count will differ ~6.7x.

instruments.name: curvature as a measured observable
instruments.where: searched all of ffn_sim/ac/: curvature appears only as an INPUT (rest dihedral angles / ARP23_THETA0_RAD in ac/weave/branch_angle.py:62, bending stiffness kappa) or as an analytic reference value (ffn_sim/ac/nucleus/lamina_analytic.py:111-122 sphere_willmore_energy = 8*pi*kappa). There is no function that MEASURES mean or Gaussian curvature from a deformed state anywhere in ac/.
instruments.what_its_name_implies: n/a — the inventory lists curvature as a geometry/deformation instrument.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing. No mean-curvature field, no Gaussian-curvature field, no discrete per-node turning angle is computed as an observable.
instruments.evidence: The cost of the absence is already documented: the fine-75nm max|PF| ~= 3.42 pN plateau, treated for a period as a solver wall, was diagnosed as a GEOMETRIC construction defect — 5-degree single-node kinks at crosslink loci created by the mesh-independent 7.86 nm WCA build-relaxation shove, with 119 of the 200 worst nodes at crosslink loci (ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/CORTEX_KINK_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md:70-100; the same doc tabulates natural turn per node = 3.82 deg at 0.5 um vs 0.57 deg at 75 nm, and alpha = kappa/seg^3 amplifying x288). A committed per-node turning-angle observable compared against the natural turn seg/R would have flagged this at BUILD time instead of after a multi-session solver investigation.
instruments.canonical_replacement: For every filament, per interior node: theta_i := angle between consecutive segment vectors (rad), and the grid-invariant discrete curvature kappa_i := 2*sin(theta_i/2)/seg (um^-1) plus the dimensionless kink ratio theta_i / (seg/R_shell). Report max and p99 of the kink ratio at build. For the membrane and nuclear envelope: per-vertex mean curvature H via the cotangent Laplace-Beltrami operator (um^-1), validated to converge to 1/R on a sphere at every subdivision level, plus the dimensionless Willmore ratio E_bend/(8*pi*kappa) which equals 1 for ANY sphere independent of R.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: On the pristine great-circle-arc cortex assert max kink ratio < 1.2 (no node turns more than 20% above the natural arc turn); the transverse-relaxed fine mesh gives ~8.8 (5.0 deg vs 0.57 deg) and fails immediately. On a sphere assert measured H*R == 1 to <1% at subdiv 3..8.

instruments.name: mesh_volume + its grid-convergence and gradient gates (nucleus geometry)
instruments.where: ffn_sim/ac/nucleus/geometry.py:105-129 (mesh_volume divergence-theorem signed volume, mesh_volume_gradient exact vertex gradient); gated by ffn_sim/tests/ac/nucleus/test_volume.py:20-26 (tolerance RATCHETED 0.02 / 0.005 / 0.0015 across subdiv 3/4/5), :29-33 (oblate vs continuum), :36-50 (analytic gradient vs FD to 1e-6 relative), plus translation invariance
instruments.what_its_name_implies: The enclosed volume of a closed triangulated surface and its exact derivative.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that. sum(x_i . (x_j x x_k))/6 over outward-wound faces.
instruments.evidence: This is the ONE geometric instrument in the repo with a real grid-invariance contract: the test parametrizes (subdiv, tol) = (3, 0.02), (4, 0.005), (5, 0.0015), which is a ratcheted O(h^2) convergence assertion rather than a single loose tolerance — a coarse-mesh regression cannot hide, and a claimed refinement that does not actually converge fails. The gradient is verified against finite differences at max|g_ana - g_fd| < 1e-6 * max|g_ana| on a RANDOMLY PERTURBED oblate mesh (not the symmetric sphere, so the test is not degenerate), and translation invariance is asserted separately. Independently confirmed: my icosphere computation reproduces the same convergence rates. This should be the template every other Family-2 instrument is rewritten against.
instruments.canonical_replacement: None needed. Generalise the PATTERN: every geometric observable gets a (resolution, tolerance) ratchet table plus a rigid-motion invariance assertion plus an analytic-limit assertion.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Already present: reverse one face's winding and the signed volume flips sign; the oblate continuum comparison catches a wrong aspect convention; the FD comparison catches a wrong gradient. The one gap: the mesh is always built by build_oblate_mesh, so a DEGENERATE (self-intersecting) mesh is never fed in — add a self-intersection / positive-orientation check.

instruments.name: ac/emergence structural detectors (nematic S, condensation localisation)
instruments.where: ffn_sim/ac/emergence/nematic.py, condensation.py; gated by ffn_sim/tests/ac/emergence/test_nematic_oracle.py:67-90 (rotational invariance of S, permutation-label invariance, polarity-flip invariance) and test_condensation_oracle.py:54-115 (rotation EQUIVARIANCE of the recovered centroid, permutation invariance, recovery across the neighbourhood-scale plateau = grid-invariance, derived radius scales linearly with the config spacing)
instruments.what_its_name_implies: Label-blind detectors of emergent nematic order and localised bundling.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Exactly that, and it is the only place in the repo where a geometric/structural detector carries the full invariance battery: rotation, permutation, polarity, and an explicit grid/scale plateau.
instruments.evidence: test_rotational_invariance_of_S asserts S(R.config) == S(config) to machine precision over random rotations; test_localization_is_rotation_equivariant asserts the recovered centroid rotates by the SAME R with the same member count; the neighbourhood-scale plateau test is an explicit grid-invariance assertion; and the null model E[sum lambda^2] = 3/(2N) with a z > 5 threshold gives the detector a magnitude-free significance criterion. No other geometric instrument in the repo has a rotation-invariance test at all (repo-wide grep over ffn_sim/tests/ac/ returns only these two modules).
instruments.canonical_replacement: None needed. Reuse the same synthetic-config + random_rotation + permutation harness (ffn_sim/ac/emergence/synthetic.py) to build the invariance negative controls for A_sil, V, h_mean, displacement, and connectivity.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: Already present and adequate.

instruments.name: contact area / contact radius / adhesion footprint in the canonical ac/ engine
instruments.where: repo-wide grep over ffn_sim/ac/ for contact_area / contact_radius / n_contact / contact_frac returns ZERO hits, despite a declared connector `membrane_ecm_contact` (ConnectorFamily.CONTACT, membrane<->ecm) at ffn_sim/ac/engine/contracts.py:446. Likewise no silhouette, no projected area, no A0, no spreading observable; `substrate` in ac/ means only the poroelastic Biot FLUID substrate (ffn_sim/ac/fluid/biot_substrate.py), a field grid, not an adhesion plane. The ECM is a 3D Mikado box (ffn_sim/ac/ecm/mikado_topology.py:72-91), not a 2D coated surface, and ffn_sim/ac/solid/adhesion_clutch.py:64-78 explicitly DISCARDS the reaction scattered onto the substrate ('rigid substrate -> discarded').
instruments.what_its_name_implies: n/a — the PI's stated baseline (cell in media, adherent on 2D collagen-coated ECM) presupposes these exist.
instruments.what_it_actually_measures: Nothing. The canonical engine has no geometric observable of adhesion at all.
instruments.evidence: Four independent confirmations: (1) zero grep hits for any contact-area name in ac/; (2) `A/A0`, `spread`, `silhouette`, `projected` all absent from ac/; (3) the clutch discards its substrate reaction, so traction cannot even be integrated over a contact region; (4) the ECM builder requires three box coordinates with every hi > lo (mikado_topology.py:90), so a genuinely 2D coated plane is representable only as a thin slab with no ligand-areal-density observable. Consequence: the PI's requested baseline cannot currently be OBSERVED in the engine that is supposed to run it, independent of whether the physics works.
instruments.canonical_replacement: See missing_instruments: A_contact, A_sil, h_mean, R_contact, and the substrate-plane definition must all be authored before any spreading claim is possible in ac/.
instruments.negative_control_that_would_catch_it: A structural test asserting that for every declared CONTACT-family connector there exists at least one committed geometric observable of that contact. It would fail today on membrane_ecm_contact and on the two other CONTACT instances.

magnitude_free_oracles: EXACT ANALYTIC LIMITS, ratcheted by resolution (the ac/nucleus/test_volume.py pattern, the only one in the repo today). For a sphere of radius R at every mesh level: enclosed volume -> (4/3)piR^3, surface area -> 4piR^2, silhouette -> piR^2, mean curvature H*R -> 1, Willmore energy / (8*pi*kappa) -> 1 (independent of R — a pure shape oracle). Each assertion gets a (resolution, tolerance) table whose tolerances shrink as O(h^2), so a claimed refinement that does not actually converge FAILS instead of passing a single loose bound. Measured reference values I generated for the icosphere at R=7.5: silhouette/piR^2 = 0.7454 / 0.9238 / 0.9800 / 0.9949 / 0.9987 / 0.9997 and surface/4piR^2 = 0.9812 / 0.9952 / 0.9988 / 0.9997 for subdiv 0..5 and 2..5 respectively.

RIGID-MOTION INVARIANCE. Every geometric scalar must be unchanged to 1e-10 under a random rotation + translation of the whole state; every geometric vector/tensor must be equivariant. This single control kills the displacement instrument (a 1-degree rotation injects 131 nm of fake deformation, 3.3x the 39.8 nm headline) and the z_half flattening instrument, and it is already implemented and passing in ac/emergence (test_nematic_oracle.py:67, test_condensation_oracle.py:54) so the harness exists.

AFFINE-DEFORMATION EXACTNESS. Apply a known affine map F to the state; every deformation observable must return the analytically implied value: uniform dilation (1+e) -> areal strain exactly (1+e)^2-1, volume ratio exactly (1+e)^3; oblate flatten at constant volume with aspect A -> equatorial radius exactly (3V0*A/4pi)^(1/3) and height ratio exactly A^(-2/3) (the closed forms already sit unused at ac/nucleus/linc_analytic.py:99-114). This control returns 2.2% of truth for cortex_node_areal_strain at native resolution and 0.9% at the fine mesh — an unambiguous, resolution-scaling failure.

GRID-INVARIANCE AS A GATE, NOT A REPORT. For each geometric observable, run identical physics at two resolutions and assert agreement to a declared tolerance. Concrete failures this catches today: A0 mesh bias 0.97996/0.99493/0.99873 of piR^2 across DCM subdiv 2/3/4; height 16.01/15.63/15.10 um (6%); basal_frac 0.265/0.354/0.348 (34%); areal-strain coverage 2.246%/1.440%/0.921% at 494,802/1.2M/2.9M nodes (exponent -0.504, i.e. N^-1/2). Corollary rule: NEVER gate on a per-node quantity, because per-node force and per-node area both scale as 1/N and a refinement then looks like convergence — the 0.7766 -> 0.0768 'grid convergence' of the membrane residual across a 16x face increase is 10.1x, i.e. mostly A_node shrinking (residual_mean = (dP - 2*gamma/R)*A_node, RESTING_BASELINE_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-23c.md:98). Gate on integrated resultants and on tensions.

DISCRETIZATION CONSISTENCY (reference and current must be the SAME surface). Assert every X/X0 ratio equals exactly 1.0 at build, to 1e-12, at every resolution. This is the rule ac/cell/assemble.py:922-930 states and obeys ('mixing the analytic sphere volume with the triangle pressure load creates a deterministic internal net force') and ff/membrane_surface.py:58 violates (A0 = 4piR^2 continuum against a mesh-area numerator -> -0.476% strain at zero strain at the code default subdiv 3).

CONVEXITY / SHAPE-CLASS SEPARATION. For any projected-area or volume instrument, assert it returns the correct answer on a known NON-CONVEX shape. Analytic targets: 5-lobed star volume = int pi(R^2-z^2)(1+amp^2/2)dz; sphere-minus-spherical-cap volume = V_sphere - pi*h^2(3R-h)/3. Node-hull instruments fail by +16.6 to +59.3% on volume and +13.6 to +98.3% on projected area, and the error does NOT shrink with refinement — which is precisely what distinguishes a definitional error from a discretization artifact.

ABSOLUTE TOPOLOGICAL INVARIANTS instead of relative ones. n_components == 1 and an explicit antipodal-cap spanning path, rather than giant >= 0.60 with giant/second > 10. Absolute connectivity has no free constant, cannot be satisfied by a dominant fragment among thousands, and is exactly grid-invariant.

PER-ACCEPTED-STEP GEOMETRIC CONSERVATION inside the transaction. With enclosed_volume, surface_area, centroid and the second-moment tensor in GlobalCellLedger, the step can assert: |dV|/V0 within the declared incompressibility; centroid displacement consistent with the net impulse; remesh events area-conserving. All four are magnitude-free (ratios and identities) and none needs a sourced parameter.

SIGN-SENSE AND MONOTONICITY. Spreading must show A_sil UP and h_mean DOWN together (the committed 3.38/3.62/3.44 result fails: A up, height flat-to-UP). Osmotic shrink must show V down and h down. Compression must show V down and radial extent up. Each is a sign assertion with no magnitude.

DIMENSIONLESS SHAPE FACTORS with known limits: sphericity psi = pi^(1/3)(6V)^(2/3)/A_surf (= 1 for a sphere, computed from the SAME mesh for both V and A); circularity of the projection 4*pi*A_sil/P_sil^2 (= 1 for a disc); anisotropy sqrt(lambda_1/lambda_2) of the projected second-moment tensor (= 1 for a disc); aspect sqrt(lambda_1/lambda_3) of the 3D gyration tensor (= 1 for a sphere). All are parameter-free and rotation-covariant.
missing_instruments: A_sil — TOP-DOWN PROJECTED SILHOUETTE AREA. Definition: the area of the UNION of the xy-projections of all triangles of the PLASMA-MEMBRANE closed triangulation, computed as an exact polygon union or by raster with a declared cell size h_pix and a declared refinement check (A_sil(h_pix/2) within 0.1% of A_sil(h_pix)). Projection axis: +z, defined as the outward normal of the SUBSTRATE PLANE, which must itself be a declared entity (see substrate_plane below) — never the simulation z axis by convention and never the cell's own principal axis. INCLUDED: every membrane triangle, whether or not it touches the substrate; overlapping projections counted ONCE (it is a union, not a sum). EXCLUDED: cortex nodes, filament nodes, ECM fibers, nucleus, any node cloud, and any convex hull. Units: um^2. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) 5-lobed star with analytic projected area -> match to <1%; a node convex hull overstates by 38.5%. (b) One node displaced 2R along +x -> A_sil changes <1e-3 relative; a hull changes +51%. (c) Rigid rotation about z -> unchanged to 1e-10. (d) Rigid translation in xy -> unchanged to 1e-10. (e) Mesh refinement subdiv n -> n+1 -> agreement <0.5%. (f) Forcing the degenerate branch must RAISE, never silently return a different definition.

A_sil0 — THE REFERENCE SILHOUETTE, and it must NOT be A_sil(frame 0). Definition: A_sil evaluated on the PHYSIOLOGICAL ADHERENT RESTING STATE — the converged state of the cell in media on the collagen substrate at Pi_0, before any perturbation — stored as a named checkpoint artifact with its own hash, not recomputed per run. Rationale: in every committed run today A0 := A_sil(frames[0]) so A/A0_first == 1.000 by construction (verified: all 11 committed spreading jsons report A/A0_first = 1.0 exactly) and cross-run comparison is invalid because each run carries its own denominator; and in the C_sub runs frame 0 is the PRISTINE SUSPENDED SPHERE (z-extent exactly 15.00 = 2R, A_surf/4piR^2 = exactly the icosphere ratio), which violates the physiological-baseline rule. Units: um^2. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) assert A_sil0 is loaded from the checkpoint, not computed from the run's own frame 0 — a test that mutates frame 0 must not change A_sil0. (b) assert A_sil/A_sil0 != 1.000 at t=0 unless the run genuinely starts from that checkpoint. (c) assert the checkpoint's own resting residual and turgor are recorded alongside it, so a non-converged baseline is visible.

substrate_plane — THE SUBSTRATE AS A DECLARED GEOMETRIC ENTITY. Definition: an oriented plane (point p0, unit normal n_hat) owned by the ECM component and exposed through the membrane_ecm_contact connector, plus a ligand areal density rho_lig (um^-2) on that plane. Everything that today says 'z' or 'z.min()' or 'the floor' must reference this object. Units: um for p0, dimensionless for n_hat, um^-2 for rho_lig. Rationale: `substrate` in ac/ currently means only the Biot fluid field grid; there is no adhesion plane, and basal_frac references z.min() (a single node) instead of a plane. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) rotate the entire world by 30 degrees including the plane and assert every substrate-referenced observable is unchanged to 1e-10 — impossible today because the axis is hard-coded. (b) assert sum over contact clutches of the reaction onto the plane equals minus the integrated traction (adhesion_clutch.py currently DISCARDS this reaction, so the identity is untestable). (c) assert rho_lig * A_contact equals the number of available ligand sites in the contact region.

A_contact — BASAL CONTACT AREA, named so it can never be confused with A_sil. Definition: the area of the union of xy-projections of membrane triangles whose CENTROID lies within d_contact of substrate_plane, where d_contact is the adhesion interaction range taken from the clutch/adhesion-energy law (adh_energy_range), not a round number. Units: um^2. Reported ALWAYS as a pair with A_sil and with the ratio A_contact/A_sil (dimensionless, in [0,1]). Rationale: this is the FORBIDDEN quantity when used as A/A0, and the fix is not to hide it but to name it unmistakably and always co-report it with A_sil so the 10-20x inflation is visible in the same row. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) suspended sphere touching at a point -> A_contact/A_sil -> 0. (b) fully spread pancake -> A_contact/A_sil -> 1. (c) assert d_contact is read from the adhesion law object, and a test that changes the adhesion range must change A_contact. (d) assert A_contact NEVER appears in any ratio whose key matches /a.?over.?a0|aa0/i.

h_mean — MEAN CELL THICKNESS. Definition: h_mean := V_enclosed / A_sil, where V_enclosed is the divergence-theorem signed volume of the SAME membrane triangulation used for A_sil. Units: um. Rationale: this is the flattening channel that A/A0 lacks and whose absence let the 3.4x 'spreading' result pass with the z-extent UNCHANGED (15.00 -> 15.10/15.63/16.01 um) while h_mean was 2.83-3.02 um — a 5x internal inconsistency the report never surfaced. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) uniform affine flattening by factor s in z at constant footprint -> h_mean scales exactly by s. (b) mesh refinement -> agreement <0.5% (V and A_sil both converge O(h^2) and the ratio converges faster). (c) rigid rotation about z -> unchanged. (d) assert h_mean and z_extent are BOTH reported; a state where h_mean falls while z_extent does not must be flagged, not passed.

A_surf / A_surf0 — MEMBRANE SURFACE-AREA BUDGET. Definition: A_surf := sum of triangle areas of the membrane mesh; A_surf0 := the same sum on the SAME mesh at the reference configuration (never 4piR^2). Report A_surf/A_surf0 alongside the declared area reservoir cap (1 + f_excess) on every spreading row. Units: um^2 and dimensionless. Rationale: the committed headline runs realized A_surf/4piR^2 = 3.106/3.118/3.119 against a declared reservoir of 1.4 — the area constraint was exceeded ~2.2x and no gate saw it, because A/A0 has no area-budget companion. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) A_surf/A_surf0 == 1.0 to 1e-12 at build, at every subdivision level (currently -0.476% at the code default). (b) assert A_surf/A_surf0 <= 1 + f_excess on every accepted step, or the step is flagged as a membrane-budget violation. (c) mesh refinement invariance <0.1%.

V_enclosed and V/V0 — TRUE ENCLOSED VOLUME. Definition: divergence-theorem signed volume of the closed, outward-wound MEMBRANE triangulation (ac/cell/membrane_pressure.signed_volume already implements it); V0 := the same on the same mesh at the physiological adherent resting checkpoint. Units: um^3. INCLUDED: the membrane surface only. EXCLUDED: any convex hull of cortex nodes (the current ff definition), any analytic sphere, any R_mean^3 surrogate. Rationale: the ff runtime computes V, A and hence the osmotic turgor from ConvexHull(cortex nodes) re-hulled every 5 refreshes, which is blind to every concave feature the PI's baseline will produce and which captures only 19-37% of the volume change under a concave indentation. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) sphere-minus-spherical-cap with analytic volume -> match <0.5%; the hull returns +0.02% instead of -0.98%. (b) 5-lobed star with analytic volume -> match <1%; the hull overstates 16.6-59.3%. (c) reverse one face winding -> the sign flips (orientation check). (d) assert V/V0 == 1.0 to 1e-12 at the checkpoint. (e) assert the instrument is NOT cross-validated only against another hull implementation — the existing check at ff/network_warp.py:831 validates divergence-on-hull-faces against ConvexHull.volume, i.e. the same definition twice.

R_contact and the contact-edge curve. Definition: the boundary polygon of the A_contact union; R_contact := sqrt(A_contact/pi) as the equivalent contact radius (um), and P_contact := the polygon perimeter (um), with the dimensionless circularity 4*pi*A_contact/P_contact^2 (= 1 for a disc, < 1 for a lobed/ruffled front). Rationale: the published macroscopic data the PI wants to sweep against (spreading kinetics, contact radius vs time, Hertz/JKR-type contact scalings) is expressed in contact radius, and a lobed front must be distinguishable from a circular one. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) analytic disc -> circularity 1.000 to <0.5%. (b) 5-lobed contact -> circularity analytically known and matched. (c) refinement invariance <1%. (d) rotation about z -> unchanged.

per-bond stretch lambda_e — THE DEFORMATION FIELD, replacing the hull-triangulation areal strain. Definition: for every mechanical bond (intra-filament segment, crosslink, motor link, membrane edge) lambda_e := |x_i - x_j| / r0_e, reported as a distribution (p1/p50/p99/max) per BOND CLASS separately, plus a per-node mean over INCIDENT BONDS. Units: dimensionless. INCLUDED: every bond in the real topology, so coverage is 100% by construction. EXCLUDED: any hull or Delaunay triangulation of the node cloud; any triangle spanning mechanically unbonded nodes. Rationale: the current cortex areal-strain field covers 2.23% of nodes at native and 0.92% at the fine mesh, reports 2.2% of the true value under a uniform dilation, and its triangles connect unbonded filaments. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) uniform dilation (1+e) -> every lambda_e == 1+e to 1e-12, and the per-node mean == 1+e (currently returns 2.2% of truth). (b) rigid motion -> all lambda_e unchanged to 1e-12. (c) coverage == 100% of nodes at 494,802 AND at 2.9M. (d) the reported statistics must agree between the two resolutions to <2% for the same physics.

per-node discrete curvature and the KINK RATIO. Definition: for every interior filament node, theta_i := angle between consecutive segment vectors (rad); kappa_i := 2*sin(theta_i/2)/seg (um^-1); kink_ratio_i := theta_i / (seg/R_shell) (dimensionless, 1 = the natural great-circle turn). For the membrane and nuclear envelope: per-vertex mean curvature H via cotangent Laplace-Beltrami (um^-1) plus the dimensionless Willmore ratio E_bend/(8*pi*kappa). Report max and p99 of kink_ratio at BUILD, before any solve. Rationale: the 3.42 pN fine-mesh plateau was a build-time 5-degree kink at crosslink loci (natural turn 0.57 degrees at 75 nm -> kink_ratio ~8.8) that no committed observable measured; it consumed a multi-session solver investigation. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) pristine great-circle arcs -> max kink_ratio < 1.2; the transverse-relaxed fine build gives ~8.8 and fails immediately. (b) sphere -> measured H*R == 1 to <1% at subdiv 3..8. (c) sphere -> Willmore ratio == 1 to a ratcheted tolerance per subdivision. (d) rigid rotation -> all curvatures unchanged.

gyration / second-moment tensor of every compartment, and derived shape scalars. Definition: G := (1/N) sum (x - x_bar)(x - x_bar)^T over the compartment's own nodes (um^2), eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= lambda_3; report Rg := sqrt(tr G) (um), aspect := sqrt(lambda_1/lambda_3), oblateness/asphericity, and the principal axes. For the nucleus this REPLACES z_half as the flattening instrument. Units: um^2 / um / dimensionless. Rationale: z_half is a single-node extremum referenced to the cell's own centroid and is not rotation-invariant; the closed-form flatten kinematics that would validate an aspect measurement already exist unused at ac/nucleus/linc_analytic.py:99-114. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) sphere -> aspect 1.000 to 1e-6. (b) analytic oblate with aspect A -> recovered aspect matches A to <1%. (c) random rigid rotation -> eigenvalues unchanged to 1e-10, eigenvectors rotate by the same R (equivariance). (d) mesh refinement -> <0.5%.

absolute cortex connectivity, authored in ac/ (it exists nowhere there today). Definition: over the union of intra-filament segment bonds and crosslink/motor bonds, n_components (int) and a boolean spans[axis] for axis in {x,y,z} = 'a path exists between the +axis and -axis polar caps'. Gate on n_components == 1 (computed on the 2-core if dangling filament ends are physically expected, so the exclusion is structural rather than a tolerance) AND spans[x] and spans[y] and spans[z]. Units: count / boolean. Rationale: cortex_density_per_fil = 20 is justified in forces_manifest.py:518 solely by 'keeps the network single-spanning', and that property is measured by nothing in ac/; the only measurement anywhere (engine_reval.py:546) gates on relative fractions that the 11,430-fragment build satisfies. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) feed the known-fragmented build (density_per_fil = 1.0) and assert FAIL — the current gate passes it. (b) sever all crosslinks in one hemisphere and assert FAIL. (c) assert the result is identical at seg_um 0.5 and 0.075 for the same density (topological quantities must be exactly grid-invariant).

GEOMETRIC LEDGER CHANNELS in the accepted-step transaction: enclosed_volume_d (um^3), surface_area_d (um^2), centroid_d (vec3d um), second_moment_d (3x3 um^2), contact_area_d (um^2). Rationale: GlobalCellLedger today has eight channels and none is geometric, so no accepted step can be rejected for a geometric violation and no remesh can be checked for area/volume conservation. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) inject a step that changes enclosed volume by 10% at zero net force and assert the transaction REJECTS it. (b) inject a remesh that changes surface area by 5% and assert rejection. (c) assert centroid displacement over a step equals the net impulse / total drag to a declared tolerance. (d) assert every channel is reduced on device with no host read, matching the existing I0-A contract.
open_questions_for_pi: The sanctioned A/A0 implementation IS a 2D convex hull, and `convex-hull` is a member of FORBIDDEN_METRICS with an automatic-RETRACT test asserting it. Do you want the RULE changed (convex hull explicitly sanctioned as the definition of 'top-down silhouette') or the IMPLEMENTATION changed (facet-union silhouette, 6 call sites)? Measured stake: on lobed adherent morphologies the hull overstates the true silhouette by 14-98%, and one escaped node overstates it by up to 51%. My recommendation is to change the implementation, because the hull error is definitional and does not shrink under refinement.

The committed headline spreading result — A/A0 = 3.38/3.62/3.44 across subdiv 2/3/4, called 'the cleanest single result in the dimension' — has, recomputed from its own npz: z-extent 15.00 -> 16.01/15.63/15.10 um (NO flattening; taller at subdiv 2), membrane surface area 3.11-3.12x 4piR^2 against a declared reservoir cap of 1.4, V/V0 ~ 1.01-1.03, and 26-32% of nodes above z = 10 um. Under refinement the height converges monotonically to 15.00 = zero flattening while A/A0 scatters non-monotonically by +-3.4%. Do you want this RETRACTED as 'area inflation, not spreading', or re-declared with the joint (A_sil, h_mean, A_surf-budget, V/V0) tuple and re-run? It is currently the only quantitative spreading evidence in the repo.

FORBIDDEN_METRICS is an exact-string set matched against a self-declared YAML label. I verified live that 'basal_contact', 'basal contact area', 'contact-area', 'basal-footprint-area', 'footprint_um2' (the literal key the forbidden code writes) and 'convex hull' (with a space) all return VERIFIED. Two live scripts still compute the forbidden basal-footprint A/A0 and emit it under the neutral key A_over_A0 (committed: outputs/h_dcm_gpu_lod/metrics_n400_s20000_GPU.json lod.A_over_A0 = 3.1467, numerically indistinguishable from the sanctioned 3.38). Do you want (a) code-level enforcement (AST/grep ban on point-cloud-hull areas and substrate-proximity node filters in production paths), (b) an artifact-level `area_definition` enum plus the git blob hash of the producing function recorded in every json, or both? A label-only guard is the same class of defect as the fingerprint that survived a physics swap.

The ff runtime computes cell volume, cell surface area and hence the osmotic turgor from ConvexHull(cortex nodes), re-hulled every 5 refreshes (network_warp.py:830-835, :1016-1036, :1056-1064). This is not just an observable — dP_osm and dP_solid key off it. It is exact for the resting sphere and for flat-plate compression, but overstates a 5-lobed cell by 17-59%, a bleb by up to 2.9%, and captures only 19-37% of the true volume change under a concave (spherical-tip) indentation. The other engine already does it correctly (ac/cell/assemble.py:925-930, discrete signed_volume, with a comment explaining exactly why). Your baseline is an adherent cell with lamellipodia, i.e. non-convex. Do I open a P0 to replace the hull with the membrane-mesh signed volume in ff, and does any previously accepted ff result (gamma-floor, AFM, crawl, blebbing) need re-derivation with the corrected volume?

The per-node areal-strain field that colours the PI-mandated visual-verification viewers reports areal strain on 2.23% of nodes at the native 494,802-node cortex and 0.92% at the fine 2.9M mesh; 97.8-99.1% of nodes report exactly 0.0 by construction, and the all-node mean under a uniform 5% dilation returns 2.2% of the true value, scaling as N^(-1/2). Your visual gate is therefore reading a field that is structurally blank on ~98% of the cell. Do you want the per-stage visualization gate BLOCKED until the field is replaced by per-bond stretch (100% coverage, exact under affine dilation, grid-invariant), or do you accept the current colouring as a qualitative-only overlay with an explicit caveat rendered into the HTML?

The internal-displacement instrument removes rigid TRANSLATION but not rigid ROTATION. A 0.39-degree rotation of the cortex reproduces exactly the 39.8 nm mean displacement that the architecture-completeness audit uses as its 'the cortex deformed / the nucleus did not' evidence, and a 1-degree rotation gives 131 nm — 3.3x the headline. The nucleus 0.0 nm side is independently corroborated by the absence of any cortex<->nucleus contact connector, so the CONCLUSION is probably safe, but the NUMBER is not. Do you want the diagnostic re-run with a Kabsch fit per compartment before the 32->33 connector decision is finalised on that evidence?

The cortex percolation gate is `giant >= 0.60 and giant/second > 10`, while its own docstring states the contract as 'giant component >= 99% of nodes'. n_components is computed and printed but never asserted, so the historically fragmented 11,430-component build cannot fail it. Separately, NOTHING in ac/ measures connectivity at all, even though cortex_density_per_fil = 20 is justified in forces_manifest.py:518 solely by 'keeps the network single-spanning'. Will you ratify the absolute form (n_components == 1 on the 2-core, plus a three-axis antipodal spanning test) as the gate, and does it need to run inside ac/ before any component may claim CONNECTED?

GlobalCellLedger has eight channels and none is geometric — no volume, area, centroid or moment — so no accepted step can be rejected for a geometric violation and no remesh can be checked for area/volume conservation. Given that MECHANICAL CONNECTEDNESS is now the gate and connectedness means 'compartments deform each other', do you want the four geometric channels (enclosed_volume, surface_area, centroid, second_moment) added to the transaction before the next component is promoted, so that deformation coupling is asserted on an accepted step rather than measured post-hoc in a script?

`ac/` has no substrate plane, no contact area, no silhouette, no A0, and adhesion_clutch.py explicitly DISCARDS the reaction scattered onto the substrate; the ECM is a 3D Mikado box, not a 2D coated surface. Your requested baseline therefore cannot be OBSERVED in the canonical engine at all, independent of whether the physics works. Do you want the 13 geometric instruments specified above authored as a numbered unit (with their negative controls, CPU-testable against analytic shapes on this Mac, before any CUDA run), and do you want the substrate_plane authored as an ECM-owned entity exposed through membrane_ecm_contact rather than as a hard-coded z?

The only closed-form geometric oracle in the repo (validation/oracles/osmotic_response.shape_factors) documents A/A0 = v^(2*alpha) as a 'top-down FOOTPRINT' — the forbidden word — and with alpha free in [0, 0.5] any measured (A/A0, V/V0) pair can be fit, so it is tautological as an acceptance gate. Do you want alpha FIXED by the boundary condition before each run (0 for a pinned footprint, 1/3 for a free suspended cell) so the oracle becomes two equations with zero free parameters, and the word 'footprint' struck from the docstring?

Cross-family, geometric in origin: the same node_volume array is used both as the Biot pressure control volume (correct: partitions the cell domain) and as the virial stress normalisation (incorrect: cortical bonds occupy a 0.2 um shell, so V_node is 12.8x too large and every reported cortical von-Mises stress in Pa is ~12.8x too low, with the factor changing if thickness or node count changes). Relatedly, the max|PF| < 0.21 pN resting gate is a PER-NODE force, and residual_mean = (dP - 2*gamma/R)*A_node, so the 0.7766 -> 0.0768 'grid convergence' across a 16x face increase is largely A_node shrinking (10.1x of the 16x). Do you want (a) node_volume split into node_volume_biot and node_volume_material, and (b) the resting gate restated on an integrated resultant or a tension rather than a per-node force, so refinement stops looking like convergence?

instruments.name: rest_force_free / relaxed_is_force_free / 'REST max|F| ~ 0' — the emergent-not-lumped premise
instruments.where: ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:578 mechanism['rest_force_free']; ac_gate_b_ecm_forces_native.py:212 verdict['relaxed_is_force_free']; ac_gate_b_sf_arc_native.py:187; ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:214-220

instruments.what_it_actually_measures: That r0 was defined as the build geometry. T = k(L - r0) is identically zero at t0 because r0 IS the initial |pos[j]-pos[i]|.
instruments.evidence: sf_mechanics.py:337 link_r0 = norm(pos[j]-pos[i]) over the SAME pos array uploaded as position_d; :343 arc_r0 likewise; mikado_topology.py:355 segment_rest_length[segment] = s1 - s0 where s0/s1 are the arclengths the nodes are placed at. This is the A/A0 = V/V0 = 1.000 pattern: the reference is derived from the state being measured. Secondary consequence: it also HARD-CODES a zero-prestress start, which violates the physiological-baseline rule (real SF and collagen are pre-tensioned) — so the gate rewards the unphysical baseline. The max|F| < 1e-6 half retains a little power (it would fire on a constant added force) but the T_abs_max < 1e-6 half is pure identity.

instruments.what_its_name_implies: Its own comment: 'What DOES separate "the heads produced this tension" from "a still-relaxing transient" is: (a) while NO head is bound the tension must be zero'.

magnitude_free_oracles: Connector reciprocity per step: for every connector, sum(force scattered onto A) + sum(force scattered onto B) = 0 to machine precision. Magnitude-free, needs no sourced constant, and cannot be satisfied by construction when the two endpoint arrays are separate allocations. This is the single cheapest replacement for the dead assemble_balance.

Adjoint virtual-work consistency: the work a connector reports must equal sum(f . dx) accumulated over BOTH endpoint arrays. Catches sign errors, factor-of-two errors, and one-sided scatters that reciprocity alone can miss when both sides are wrong symmetrically.

Total moment about the centroid: add moment_resultant_d and centroid_d channels to GlobalCellLedger and gate sum(r x f) = 0 at equilibrium. Independent of |f|, and it is the channel that would make the acceptance predicate non-trivial for a force-free self-propelled cell. ac_gate_a_total_moment.py already computes something like this but has zero failure paths.

Rigid-body null-space test: translate the entire composed state by a constant vector and rotate it by a rotation matrix. Every connector force must be exactly invariant under translation and must rotate covariantly. This is the definitive test that co-location is not being used as a connection, and it needs no parameter values at all.

Two-sided deformation response (the real CONNECTEDNESS oracle): displace component A's nodes by delta and require a non-zero, sign-correct force response in component B's array, with the response vanishing identically when the connector is unbound. This replaces all 102 substring-in-source coupling assertions and is exactly what PI priority #1 asks for.

Prestressed-reference oracle: define rest lengths from a sourced resting strain rather than from the build geometry, then gate T(t0) against the closed form k*L*eps0/(1+eps0). Converts today's tautological 'rest force-free' check into a real measurement AND fixes the physiological-baseline violation in the same edit.

Grid invariance of the OBSERVABLE, not of the tolerance: require the reported gamma or T to be ell-independent within a declared band across at least three mesh rungs, with the residual criterion expressed as a force density (mean|PF|/ell), since a nodal force is a density times ell. The threshold-derivation script already reports the measured exponents (ell^-2.845, ell^-0.443) that such a gate would flag.

FD-vs-operator on every connector tangent: the connector's Jacobian action must match a central finite difference of its own force to O(h^2). Self-normalizing, so no sourced magnitude is needed, and it is the same technique that already refuted the tangent hypothesis at the resting baseline.

Rejected-step bit-identity for EVERY driver: with accepted_d = zeros, every authoritative array must be restored bit-exactly and no clock may advance. ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:532-551 is the working template; five other drivers need it.

Per-channel contributor counters on the ledger: assemble_balance must REFUSE (balance_ok = 0) when either force channel had zero contributors this step. This single change turns the current unconditional accept into a loud failure and is the cheapest way to make the global predicate honest before the PI has to author a tolerance.
missing_instruments: No moment channel and no centroid channel in GlobalCellLedger (grep 'moment' in ledger.py: zero hits), while ecm_world.py:346 already promises to contribute one. Consequence: 'the cell moves forward' is ungateable, and the only registered global criterion is identically zero for a crawler.
No declared value for the assemble_balance tolerance anywhere in code or docs. tol_sq_d is caller-owned by design and there is no caller, so the number has never had to exist.
No producer for add_cell_traction anywhere in the tree. The traction half of the force-balance gate is dead code, which is why the residual is identically zero rather than merely small.

No mass-conservation GATE. mass_d, work_d, force_resultant_d and topology_counts_d are write-only accumulators that nothing ever reads or compares. monomer_flux.py even sums three unrelated quantities into mass_d.

No instrument linking PopulationLedger integer IDs to device array contents. The ledger DEFINES n_filaments (composed_native.py:273), so the no-double-count invariant is structurally incapable of detecting a physical double count.
No two-sided deformation-response instrument for ANY connector. Mechanical connectedness is currently evidenced by source substrings and by pointer-forwarding spies.

No CUDA CI lane. Every kernel-level negative control in tests/ac is @skipif-gated and therefore does not run in the loop that produces the green claims; the one real negative control on the balance gate has, in practice, never executed.

No exit-code contract for gate drivers: 11 of 19 ac_gate_* drivers cannot return non-zero, including the resting GATE-A driver and the two drivers behind the emergent-gamma and interior-column-coupling headlines.
open_questions_for_pi: The assemble_balance tolerance is a gate-contract number only you can author — but authoring it does not help yet, because both channels have no producer and |reaction + traction| is identically zero for a force-free cell. Do you want (a) the contributor-counter refusal wired first so the gate goes loud instead of green, and (b) a moment + centroid channel added before any tolerance is chosen?

Rest-length convention: r0 is currently defined AS the build geometry (sf_mechanics.py:337, mikado_topology.py:355), which makes every 'rest force-free' verdict a tautology AND hard-codes a zero-prestress, non-physiological baseline. result.summary: The bottom-line REJECT is CORRECT and should stand, and its decisive mechanism — the mechanical tangent is assembled FROM the binding state, so every head's hazard is a functional of a configuration-dependent matrix inverse — is real and verified in code (ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:407-411 launches add_segment_crossbridge_stiffness_kernel with t.state.bound_d as an INPUT; ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_motor_slice.py:365-371 reads loads off the CONVERGED geometry; ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:504-533 makes load_h a pure function of solved positions; ffn_sim/ac/motor/hand.py:242 feeds it to the hazard). But the supporting structure fails in four ways I verified by rebuilding the slice host-side. (1) ITS CENTRAL FACTUAL CLAIM IS WRONG IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION: coupling is NOT global. I rebuilt the landed population and computed connected components of the real mechanical graph (links + arc joints + backbone/head bonds + every geometrically reachable crossbridge): 12 head-bearing blocks — ELEVEN of 20 heads and ONE of 100 heads (five minifilaments welded by the 4 alpha-actinin arc joints, all four terminating on SF node 242). 11x20+100=320. A(s)^-1 is block-diagonal, so a head's hazard depends on ~20 or ~100 other heads, not on "the entire binding configuration". Worse, the audit cites "one concatenated global solve" as its evidence of coupling — the project's own co-location-is-not-connection error committed in reverse: a monolithic PCG over a block-diagonal operator is exactly decoupled. And the largest real block is 100 heads, not the 20 its pre-registered threshold is written against, so exact chi at a mid-cut is up to 2^50, not 2^10. The corrected fact STRENGTHENS the REJECT while invalidating the contract it wants committed to disk. (2) TWO ARITHMETIC PILLARS FLIP ON UNDEFENDED PARAMETERS. Memory is linear in the MPO bond D_W, and D_W~128 is asserted with no derivation; with the textbook sum-of-local-jumps D_W=2 the same formula gives 10.7 GB at chi=1024 (FITS one A5000) instead of 687 GB / 43 A5000s. And d=1+4*8*16=513 assumes 4 reachable segments per head; I measured mean 1.0, max 1 on the built geometry (capture 0.21 um vs 0.4 um sarcomere lateral), giving d=129 and 4.0 GB state memory, which also FITS, flipping the "non-starter BEFORE environments" verdict. The SPEED argument survives both (~220x MC at D_W=2), so the robust headline is "the configuration where MPS fits memory is the configuration where it is not exact" — not the GB table. (3) ITS SELF-DECLARED "single strongest argument against DO_NOW" IS INADMISSIBLE BY ITS OWN CRITERION. "Measured duty 0.941" is not a duty: it is a 6-step attach-only transient (dt=0.01, k_on=50/s gives 1-exp(-3)=0.950 vs 301/320=0.941, loads at 11% of f_stall so almost nothing detaches). The code's own steady state is phi_b=k_on/(k_on+k_off)=0.993, and ffn_sim/ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py:26-30 ALREADY records the conflict with the sourced Kovacs duty ~0.1. At the sourced NM2A duty 0.05-0.1 the binomial noise is 79% per minifilament / 24% for the slice / 4.6% for 8840 heads — comparable to or LARGER than the 15.5% residual it is compared against. Arguments 2 and 5 both invert at the sourced duty, and both hinge on k_on=50/s, which ffn_sim/ac/motor/params_i0b3.yaml:248-260 marks "GAP - PI ... NOT an audited head-level SourceEvidence row". (4) THE CONSTRUCTIVE HALF SHIPS AN "EXACT" ORACLE WHOSE SYMMETRY THE CODE REFUTES. Head exchangeability is false by construction: the 20 heads of minifilament 0 hang from 14 DISTINCT backbone beads at 20 distinct axial offsets and split into two head_side groups of 10 on the two DIFFERENT anti-parallel filaments with OPPOSITE walk_dir. Strict Markov lumping gives ~1.9e5 states, not 21 — a 5.6x reduction from 2^20, not 5e4x — and load(n) is not even well-defined. That reproduces the audit's own failure-mode #4 (an exact-labelled approximation) in its constructive half. On enforcement, item #1 describes a guard that does not exist: there is NO static test forbidding validation/oracles imports from a runtime path; ffn_sim/tests/ac/test_warp_only_contract.py:13-16,60-69 checks HOOMD names only, and the closest real analogue (ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py) is an acceptance oracle living INSIDE the runtime package. Recommendation: keep the REJECT, re-found it on the measured 12-block structure plus the representability obstruction (both magnitude-free), delete the D_W/d-dependent GB table as decisive, demote arguments 2 and 5 to duty-conditional, fix the pre-registered threshold to the real 100-head block BEFORE commit, and do not ship the count chain until exchangeability is measured rather than assumed.
