The slice has three participants only (sf_arc, nmii, connector) per ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_motor_slice.py:477-488; there is no cortex component. The 'N_cortex_sites: 280' in the landed json is population metadata, and ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_motor_slice.py:160-166 states in the code's own words that the carried identity/material metadata is consumed by NO kernel today.

NF2007 INEXTENSIBILITY AS A 'GLOBAL COUPLING THAT EXISTS BY DESIGN' HERE - NOT PRESENT. ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:46-64 explicitly REPLACES the parent's NF2007 projector with the FA Dirichlet mask, and :370-374 implements _project as mask_vec3_kernel only. The exact tridiagonal projector the audit cites (ffn_sim/ac/cell/inner_mechanics.py:78-140 - real, verified as a per-fiber Thomas solve) never runs in the SF slice. The audit hedges it as short-ranged but frames it as one of 'two further global couplings [that] exist by design'.

'THE ABSCISSA DYNAMIC RANGE IS ONLY f_stall/k_xb = 0.5 nm (the stall guard at hand.py:199 caps it)' - MISREADS THE GUARD. ffn_sim/ac/motor/hand.py:199-200 (identical at ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:167-169 and 222-224) caps the PER-TICK INCREMENT, abscissa += min(tau*v_Hill, (f_stall-F)/k_xb). The accumulator itself is unbounded whenever the actin yields, since the crossbridge extension - not the abscissa - is what saturates. The landed run confirms the heads are nowhere near stall: head_load_max = 0.0545 pN = 11% of f_stall = 0.5 pN. So open_question 3's stated mechanism ('the abscissa accumulator therefore never completes one physical step before stalling') is not what the code does. The underlying RATIO observation (extension at stall = 0.5 nm is ~10x below a ~5 nm lever-arm stroke, so f_stall is inconsistent with k_xb x d_stroke) IS real and worth surfacing to PI; only the attributed mechanism is wrong, and enforcement item #4's demand for grid-invariance 'inside half a nanometre' inherits the same error.

CITATION SLIPS in the facts it wants registered: the off-rate the landed run actually used is ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:225 (catch_slip_off_rate; the json records detach = CATCH_SLIP_PROXY), with the Bell variant at :174 - not :186, which is docstring prose. The load kernel is ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:504-533 (audit says 503-533). The 'sf_implicit.py:85-90' cite for the concatenated solve points at docstring prose; the code is at :341-355 and :481-491.
missed_defects: THE PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE MEASURES THE WRONG OBJECT. Step 2 commits 'r_eff <= 4 out of 20 for a 20-head block' to disk before the run. Measured, five of sixteen minifilaments live in a single 100-head block (see false_alarms #1). A contract naming a 20-head block when the object is 100 heads is exactly the 'gate that measures something other than its name' pattern this commission exists to stop, and once committed, fixing it becomes a gate-contract change requiring PI sign-off. Fix before commit: state the threshold per measured block, with the block partition emitted as a required field.

THE 'EXACT' COUNT CHAIN IS NOT EXACT - head exchangeability is refuted by the built topology, with no run needed. I dumped minifilament 0: its 20 heads attach to 14 DISTINCT backbone beads (head_bonds [[14,0],[15,0],[16,1],[17,2],[18,2],...,[33,7]]) at 20 distinct axial offsets (+0.1505 down to +0.0116 um on one side, -0.1505 to -0.0116 on the other), and head_side splits them 10/10 onto the two DIFFERENT anti-parallel filaments (y = -3.4812 vs -3.0812, 0.4 um apart) with OPPOSITE walk_dir. Heads at opposite ends of an angle-harmonic rod, on opposite-polarity filaments, are not exchangeable, so load is not a function of n_bound. Strict Markov lumping gives 3^3*2^4 = 432 states per side, 432^2 = 186,624 total - a 5.6x reduction from 2^20, not the claimed 5e4x - and the 'load(n) tabulated with N+1 solves' closure is undefined. Shipping this as 'exact' in validation/oracles/ reproduces the audit's own failure_mode #4 in its constructive half.

ITS PRICED ALTERNATIVE FAILS ON THE LARGEST REAL BLOCK. 'Brute-force enumeration is also cheaper than MPS at this block size (2^20 = 1.05e6, ~170 MB)' holds only for the 11 isolated minifilaments. For the measured 100-head block brute force is 2^100, and the count chain over 5 mechanically coupled minifilaments needs a closure over (n1..n5), i.e. 21^5 ~ 4.1e6 mechanical solves, not 21 - the claimed 2.4 ms closure understates by ~1e5 for that block.

'ALREADY COVERED BY A VALIDATED CLOSED FORM' IS FALSE FOR THE HAZARD THE RUN USED. ffn_sim/ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py:48 imports ONLY engaged_fraction_steady, which is pure Bell SLIP (ffn_sim/ac/motor/bell_kinetics_analytic.py:199-223 calls bell_off_rate), and its own sanity gate asserts a slip-only monotonicity ('E[F] decreases if k_off0 rises'). The landed GATE-B run used CATCH_SLIP (json params_pi_gap.detach = CATCH_SLIP_PROXY; ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:225). A catch-slip hazard is NON-MONOTONE in load, which is precisely the load-sharing bistability the audit calls 'the one scientifically real question in the neighbourhood'. So the oracle it prices MPS against cannot represent the runtime's bond law; engaged_fraction_catch_slip EXISTS at ffn_sim/ac/motor/bell_kinetics_analytic.py:226 but is not wired into the ensemble oracle. The 'no regime left for MPS' dilemma is argued against the wrong oracle.

J IS BLIND TO THE FAILURE MODE THE CONNECTOR CONTRACT ACTUALLY FORBIDS. Step 4 is sold as the deliverable that 'justifies steps 1-3 on its own merit' because a structurally zero cross-component block PROVES co-location without connection. True - but the converse is silent: a NONZERO block cannot distinguish an explicit adjoint connector from an illegal co-location weld. The repo has exactly such an alias: ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_motor_slice.py:28-32 records that 'the cortex lane has the actuator and the port ALIAS one global cell.pos_d'. J measures influence, not whether influence is routed through a legal connector, so it detects absence-of-connection and is blind to illegal-connection. Offering it as THE priority-1 instrument without that caveat is an over-claim.

THE FREE RECIPROCITY TEST IS OMITTED. For SPD A the force-probe Green's function obeys a Maxwell-Betti symmetry, so measured asymmetry in J is a pure magnitude-free bug signal - and 'reciprocity' is named explicitly in PI priority 2. The plan emits decay exponent, r_eff and a Frobenius block ratio but never checks J's symmetry, which is the cheapest and strongest thing the same solves would buy and the only one that directly tests the bidirectional+adjoint connector contract.

STEP 1'S TWO PROBES MEASURE DIFFERENT OBJECTS, OFFERED WITH 'or'. Flipping state.bound_d[h'] changes BOTH the right-hand side and the operator (the rank-1 k_xb*w*w^T term at ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:407-411); adding a unit crossbridge force along walk_dir changes only the right-hand side. The force-probe version is exactly the frozen/linearized-environment surrogate the audit itself declares forbidden for the runtime (its failure_modes #2 and hard_rule_interaction 'FINE-GRAINED OVER LUMPED'). Drawing a representability conclusion from it would be self-contradictory. Also, flipping an UNBOUND head to bound is a no-op unless seg_a/seg_b/bary_t/walk_dir/r0_bind are all synthesized (ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:489-491 returns early on a<0 or b<0), and any synthesized r0_bind injects a force of arbitrary magnitude.

STEP 1 READS THE WRONG ARRAY. It says 'read delta(loads_bell)'. ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:531-533 sets loads[h] = signed k_xb*(...) and loads_full[h] = wp.abs(loads[h]), and ffn_sim/ac/engine/cortex_motor_slice.py:520-525 routes those to loads_hill_d and loads_bell_d respectively. loads_bell is therefore |load|: sign-blind and non-differentiable at 0, which is where most loads sit (head_load_max 0.0545 pN over 301 bound heads). The sensitivity must be read off loads_hill.

STEP 1 HAS NO CONVERGED BASE STATE AND DOES NOT REQUIRE ONE. It opens with 'converge the slice', but the only landed artifact has residual_over_tension = 0.155 (explicit path, 200 relax), and the implicit solver it would use is UNTRACKED in git (git ls-files errors on ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_implicit.py) with no native run anywhere in ffn_sim/outputs/ (no artifact contains 'implicit_pcg'; the landed json has no solver key). J measured about an unconverged base state inherits exactly the defect that forced the retraction of T = 1.92 pN. The plan requires no convergence receipt and no check that the probe response exceeds the residual drift.

ITS OWN UNCERTAINTY YARDSTICK IS AN UNAUDITED MAX/MAX RATIO. Everything is priced against 'residual/tension = 15.5 percent', but ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:519 defines it as _max_force_norm over FREE nodes divided by T_abs_max over ALL links - two maxima over different index sets at different locations, not a residual-to-scale ratio in any norm. At step 1 it reports 1.029 from 5.714e-14 / 5.551e-14, a 0/0 artifact printed as '102.94% of T'. In a commission whose subject is measurement definitions, adopting this number as the reference uncertainty without auditing its definition is a gap.

STEP 3 SWEEPS THE WRONG RATIO AND OVERSTATES UNIQUENESS. 'k_xb and k_axial ... the ONE ratio the answer depends on' - I read the assembled operator: link_k = 1000 uniformly, arc_k = 460000 (all four joints), bend_alpha in 0.1296-1.1504, k_backbone = 1000, k_head_arm = 100. That is at least four independent dimensionless ratios, and the one that controls INTER-minifilament coupling is arc_k/k_axial = 460 - it is what welds five minifilaments into the 100-head block. So the proposed sweep does not probe the ratio that determines the very block structure steps 2(b) and 2(c) measure. Ratio-robustness cannot be claimed from a one-ratio sweep.
arithmetic_corrections: D_W ~ 128 IS UNDERIVED AND THE HARDWARE HEADLINE FLIPS ON IT. Memory = 2*N*D_W*chi^2*8 is linear in D_W. Their numbers reproduce exactly (2*320*128*1024^2*8 = 6.87e11 B = 687 GB; 687/16 = 43 A5000s; 8840 heads gives 18.98 TB; chi_feasible = sqrt(8e9/(2*320*128*8)) = 110.5). But with the textbook sum-of-local-jumps MPO bond D_W = 2 the same formula gives 2*320*2*1024^2*8 = 10.7 GB at chi = 1024 - FITS one A5000 (16,760,569,856 B total, 452 MB used per native_resting_70686.json) - and chi_feasible = 884. So '687 GB / 43 A5000s / 19 TB' is not a feasibility verdict; it is a consequence of an undefended parameter, and a reviewer plugging D_W = 2 would read the opposite conclusion. The honest statement is that D_W is UNDEFINED because the generator is not an MPO at any finite bond dimension - which makes the memory table decorative rather than load-bearing. The SPEED argument survives: at D_W = 2, chi = 884, N*d*chi^3*D_W = 320*2*6.906e8*2 = 8.84e11 flops = 1.77 s/sweep at 0.5 TFLOP/s fp64, still ~220x MC.

d = 1 + 4*8*16 = 513 ASSUMES 4 REACHABLE SEGMENTS PER HEAD; I MEASURED 1. On the built geometry with capture_radius = 0.21 um and sarcomere lateral separation 0.4 um, the mean number of segments within capture per head is exactly 1.0 (max 1), with nearest distance median 0.000 um and max 1.665e-16 um. So d = 1 + 1*8*16 = 129 and state memory at chi = 110 is 320*129*110^2*8 = 4.0 GB, which FITS - flipping the stated 'over budget BEFORE environments. Non-starter'. (Over a trajectory the bound-segment alphabet is up to 8 per 9-node fiber, giving d up to 1025 and 31.7 GB, so it can also go the other way. The defect is that it was asserted rather than measured while the conclusion flips on it.)

'MEASURED DUTY 0.941' IS A TRANSIENT, NOT A DUTY, AND THE PRIORITY ARGUMENT INVERTS AT THE SOURCED VALUE. The landed run is 6 accepted steps at dt = 0.01 s with k_on = 50/s, so attach-only gives 1 - exp(-50*0.06) = 0.950 vs the measured 301/320 = 0.9406 - the ramp is 113/184/238/266/287/301 and loads sit at 11% of f_stall, so detachment is negligible. The code's own steady state is phi_b = k_on/(k_on + k_off) = 50/50.35 = 0.993, and ffn_sim/ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py:26-30 ALREADY flags the conflict with the sourced Kovacs duty ~0.1 as a PI reconciliation item. Their binomial arithmetic at p = 0.941 is correct (sd = sqrt(320*0.941*0.059) = 4.21 = 1.40% of 301; 8840 heads gives 22.2 = 0.267%; 3.2% at n_side = 30 and 3.2/sqrt(442) = 0.154%). At the SOURCED NM2A duty 0.05-0.1 (ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/PI_GAP_LITERATURE_SOURCING_2026-07-23.md:30, NM2B 0.2-0.3 at :32) the relative binomial noise is sqrt((1-p)/(N*p)) = 79% per 20-head minifilament, 24% for the 320-head slice, 4.6% for 8840 heads - comparable to or larger than the 15.5% residual it is compared against. Both argument 2 ('the single strongest argument against DO_NOW') and argument 5's mean-field-is-already-exact claim are duty-conditional, and both hinge on k_on = 50/s, which ffn_sim/ac/motor/params_i0b3.yaml:248-260 records as 'GAP - PI', 'config-chosen, NOT an audited head-level SourceEvidence row'. By the audit's own criterion ('a measurement that cannot be evaluated without an unsourced constant is a bad measurement right now') its own priority argument is inadmissible.

EXACT-chi IS UNDERSTATED BY THE BLOCK STRUCTURE. chi = 2^10 = 1024 is right for a mid-cut of a 20-head all-to-all block, but the measured maximum block is 100 heads, whose mid-cut bound is up to 2^50 ~ 1.1e15. The direction is conservative (infeasibility only deepens), but the quoted exactness threshold and every figure derived from it are 40 orders of magnitude off for five of sixteen minifilaments.

MINOR, ALL VERIFIED CORRECT: 320 heads / 16 minifilaments / 544 NMII particles / 360 SF nodes / 904 nodes / 2712 DOF (I rebuilt all of these); 0.059^20 = 2.6e-25 (they say 5e-25, a factor-2 rounding, immaterial); 4e-5 s/iteration by linear scaling of 0.02271 s at 511,114 nodes (ffn_sim/outputs/ac/implicit/REPORT.md:123, with 0.27968 and 0.82235 at :124 and :130 also confirmed); 176 s/sweep and 1760 s/step at chi = 1024; 275x and 2.2e5x vs MC; f_stall/k_xb = 0.5 nm; A5000 fp64 = 27.8/32 = 0.87 TFLOP/s; 8840 = 442*20; every native count matches ffn_sim/outputs/ac/foundation-hardening/native_resting_70686.json (70686 filaments, 494802 actin nodes, 511114 total nodes, 442 minifilaments, 8840 heads, 15028 myosin particles, 70686 crosslinks, 642 ERM tethers, gpu_bytes_total 16760569856, used 452001792).

TWO SMALL SOURCING SLIPS. (a) '2^20 sparse generator ~21 nnz/row = ~170 MB': 1.05e6 * 21 nnz at 8 B value + 4 B index = 264 MB; 170 MB implies ~8 B/nnz. (b) 'heads are about 36x under-placed' is the CORTICAL engaged-head density figure; the SF-side deficit on record is ~180x (floor) / ~360x (centre) cross-sectional NMII count per stress fiber (ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/SF_GENERATION_LIMIT_SYNTHESIS_2026-06-09.md:82), so the physiological target for the SF discrete layer is understated.
hard_rule_problems: ENFORCEMENT ITEM #1 CLAIMS A PRECEDENT THAT DOES NOT EXIST. 'Place it under validation/oracles/ and extend the existing static runtime-import-forbidden test so importing it from ac/, ff/, or dcm/ fails collection. This is the same mechanism that keeps the v1 closed-form oracles out of the runtime.' There is no such test. The only static import gate in scope is ffn_sim/tests/ac/test_warp_only_contract.py, whose _is_hoomd_module (:13-16) and single test (:60-69) match HOOMD names ONLY. I grepped ffn_sim/tests/ for any assertion forbidding a validation/oracles import from a runtime path: none. And the repo's actual practice is the opposite of the claimed precedent - the closest analogue, ffn_sim/ac/motor/ensemble_stall_analytic.py ('Host-side acceptance oracle (pure NumPy, NO Warp)'), lives INSIDE the runtime package ac/, as do bell_kinetics_analytic.py, hill_fv_analytic.py and powerstroke_analytic.py. The firewall is convention, not mechanism, so the audit's safety rests on remembering.

ENFORCEMENT ITEM #1 IS ALSO SELF-CONTRADICTORY. Step 5 says 'Ship it in validation/oracles/ under the existing runtime-import-forbidden firewall, next to ensemble_stall_analytic.py'. Those are different directories: ensemble_stall_analytic.py is at ffn_sim/ac/motor/, not ffn_sim/validation/oracles/ (whose contents are __init__.py, bridge, common, configs, ecm, junction, mechanics, osmotic_response.py, spheroid, young_dupre.py).

ENFORCEMENT ITEM #2 IS ONE ONE-LINE EDIT FROM SILENCE. Requiring the emitter to raise when the chi-sweep field is absent is the right idea, and the observation that the headline fingerprint would NOT catch a swapped chi (it hashes sorted deduplicated bare numeric tokens with no units) is correct and valuable. But an emitter-side branch is exactly the guard shape that just returned CONFIRMED 0 of 7 because a one-line edit silenced it. It must be a collected test that fails when any emitted artifact lacks the chi sequence, not a raise inside the producer.

ENFORCEMENT ITEM #4's SHARPEST CASE RESTS ON THE MISREAD GUARD. 'the abscissa case is the sharp one: its entire dynamic range is f_stall/k_xb = 0.5 nm, so bin-width invariance must be shown inside half a nanometre'. ffn_sim/ac/motor/hand.py:199-200 caps the per-tick increment, not the accumulator (see false_alarms). The grid-invariance demonstration would be specified over an interval that does not exist - a Magic-Number Block satisfied against the wrong bound.

STEP 5 IS A DE-FACTO GATE CHANGE PRESENTED AS A BUILD ITEM. Shipping a count chain labelled 'exact under exchangeability' that 'strictly generalizes' ensemble_stall_analytic.py positions it to serve as the acceptance oracle for the emergent engaged-fraction gate. Since exchangeability is refuted by the topology (missed_defects #2), that oracle would loosen the gate without any threshold moving - the hardest kind of loosening to notice. It needs PI sign-off framing plus the exchangeability measurement FIRST, not 'ship it in validation/oracles/'.

WHAT IS COMPLIANT, AND IT IS THE PLAN'S BEST FEATURE: none of the proposed replacement observables requires an unsourced magnitude as a gate. Normalized decay J(r)/J(0) with a fitted exponent, r_eff as a count of singular values above 1% of sigma_max, and the Frobenius block ratio are all dimensionless and ratio-swept, exactly PI priority 2. Committing the threshold before the run is correct process and is a NEW gate, not a loosening - provided the block size is corrected to the measured partition before the contract lands (missed_defects #1). The audit is also honest and correct that the CellTransaction accept predicate is hard-wired to 1 in the landed run (ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:497 accepted_d = ones), that the attach kernel gates on it (ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:434), and that assemble_balance has no declared tolerance anywhere (ffn_sim/ac/engine/ledger.py:329-357 takes tol_sq_d from the caller; ffn_sim/ac/engine/transaction.py:137-144 falls back to balance_ok_d; the gate script never supplies either).
feasibility_corrections: THE DECIDING FACT - DOES MECHANICAL LOAD COUPLE ALL BINDING STATES GLOBALLY? - INDEPENDENTLY DETERMINED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. I did not take the auditor's reading. I rebuilt the landed slice host-side and computed connected components of the real mechanical graph (320 axial links + 4 alpha-actinin arc joints + NMII backbone bonds + head-arm bonds + every crossbridge the capture radius permits): 12 head-bearing blocks, eleven of 20 heads and one of 100 heads. Passive-only (no crossbridges) the graph is 52 components with 16 disjoint 20-head minifilament blocks, so it is the crossbridges plus the four arc joints at node 242 that assemble the single 100-head cluster. The state-dependent operator claim IS real (ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:407-411 passes t.state.bound_d, seg_a_d, seg_b_d, bary_t_d, abscissa_d, walk_dir_d as INPUTS to the tangent, and :277-280 references the connector's LIVE state rather than copying it, so the tangent sees the same bound set the force saw) - but it is state-dependent PER BLOCK, not globally. The verdict survives on the representability obstruction, which holds block-wise; the 'entire configuration' framing does not.

MPS TRACK - INFEASIBLE ON ONE A5000, BUT FOR A DIFFERENT AND MORE ROBUST REASON THAN GIVEN. The stated reason (687 GB, 43 A5000s) collapses by ~64x under D_W = 2 to 10.7 GB, which fits. The reason that does NOT collapse is the corrected block size: a mid-cut of the measured 100-head block needs chi up to 2^50, infeasible at any D_W on any hardware. The audit's own best sentence - 'the configuration in which MPS fits memory is the configuration in which it loses the one property that justified it' - is D_W-independent and should be the headline instead of the GB table.

COUNT-CHAIN TRACK - NOT FEASIBLE AS AN 'EXACT' OBJECT FOR THE COUPLED BLOCK, AND MISPRICED FOR THE ISOLATED ONES. Per isolated minifilament, strict lumping yields ~1.9e5 states rather than 21, and 21 is unreachable because heads are not exchangeable (14 distinct backbone beads, two opposite-polarity sides). For the 100-head block the closure is over (n1..n5), i.e. 21^5 ~ 4.1e6 solves at ~4e-5 s = ~160 s if lumping were valid, against the claimed 2.4 ms. And brute force is 2^20 (feasible) for isolated blocks but 2^100 (never) for the coupled one, so 'MPS is beaten by brute force at this block size' is true for 11 of 16 minifilaments and false for the block that matters.

THE RECOMMENDED J MEASUREMENT IS FEASIBLE ON ONE A5000, BUT NOT AT THE STATED BUDGET. Step 1 budgets 40 probes; Step 2 asks for within- AND across-minifilament singular-value spectra plus ||J_intra||_F / ||J_inter||_F, which need all 320 columns. Re-priced honestly: 320 probes x (4 Newton x 200 CG) at ~4e-5 s/iteration = ~10 s of solver time on 2712 DOF, plus 320 compute_loads launches. Comfortably feasible - the plan under-specifies its own budget by 8x. Three prerequisites must be added or the run is not interpretable: (a) the base state must be converged, which today requires the UNTRACKED ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_implicit.py and has no native artifact (nothing in ffn_sim/outputs/ contains 'implicit_pcg'; the landed json has no solver key and sits at residual_over_tension 0.155); (b) J must be read from the signed loads_hill_d, not loads_bell_d = |load|; (c) J is J(s), so the decay exponent and r_eff must be reported at more than one bound fraction (the landed 0.94 transient and something near the sourced 0.05-0.1) or the numbers are state-conditional in exactly the way that makes inferred parameters drift.

QTT / TENSOR-TRAIN ON THE MECHANICAL FIELD - the request to record it as separately closed is sound, and its cited grounds check out: 7 actin nodes per cortex fiber (494,802/70,686 = 7.0) and 9 per SF fiber (360/40 = 9), and the stiffness contrast is real and worse than an unstructured-graph argument needs - I measured arc_k = 460000 pN/um against link_k = 1000 and k_head_arm = 100, a 4600x spread inside one operator. The prior CG-dominated ~9% optimization ceiling with a do-not-retry verdict is consistent with ffn_sim/outputs/ac/implicit/REPORT.md. Recording it as closed and separate is the right call.

result.summary:
The audit is unusually disciplined and most of its disk citations check out — I re-verified 12/18 null params in ac/motor/params_i0b3.yaml (it said 12/19), the 70-param/29-result coverage_baseline debt, the real hoomd meta_path blocker at repo-root conftest.py:231-256/279, the AST scan at tests/ac/test_warp_only_contract.py:5-60, ensemble.py's EnsembleRunner, results_manifest.yaml + SUSPICION + FORBIDDEN_METRICS, the missing ledger moment/centroid channels, composed_native.solve_candidate having no integrator, the FIXMAN B1 rejection at briefs/FIXMAN_LAZY_EVAL_DESIGN.md:103, the Makefile/CI wiring, EVERY cited wall time, and the fact that the 938 s anchor genuinely is not on disk. The gradient rejection and the enforcement-first sequencing are the right calls.

But it fails on its own terms in four places. (1) Its #1 summary statistic, adjoint-work closure, is the linear-algebra identity <Wv,g>=<v,Wᵗg> computed from ONE matrix (ac/fluid/coupled_boundary_reference.py:196-198) — it cannot fail for any real matrix; the LINC "second instance" is a validator on caller-supplied data in a module with zero non-test importers. (2) Its #2 summary statistic has never executed on physics: add_cell_traction has no production caller anywhere, so traction_resultant_d is identically zero and assemble_balance degenerates to |reaction|²≤tol², which an UNCOUPLED build passes trivially; and no driver passes tol_sq_d (ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:506-507 explicitly refuses). (3) Its primary architectural choice — block-factorized NRE summing per-block log-ratios — rests on a locality assumption the code refutes: one global displacement solve (implicit_mechanics.py:1575) sets every head's load, which then drives every catch-slip hazard, and the committed artifact shows 99.5% of motor-driven γ is carried by the passive network (γ_source 0.0191 of γ_total 3.7234). The factorization is a mean-field/lumped substitute for a globally coupled likelihood, which is the hard rule it claims to satisfy. (4) Its enforcement chain has an unwired link and a wrong filename: verify_forces.py and verify_gate_contracts.py are in NO gate (Makefile, ci.yml, .githooks/pre-commit all run only verify_runs + verify_params), and the provenance ranking G6 asks for does not exist in verify_params.py — it lives in the unwired verify_forces.py.

Parameter and cost counts are wrong in the direction that makes the plan look cheaper: 44 free scalars not ~37, largest block 13 not 9, 71 (not 124) KU-tagged runtime constants of which exactly 1 is declared, and the 940 s C_solve prices an operation that has never completed (the one committed full-compartment outer step rolled back with residual_end == residual_start exactly).
false_alarms: max|PF| blacklist — the STATED reason is a category error. The audit blacklists the observable because 'GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md measures it as ... a float64 round-off criterion (float32 recompile gives 4882 pN, x23170)'. That doc's finding is about the THRESHOLD, not the quantity: §7/G1 (GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md:427-434) explicitly RECOMMENDS keeping route (c) and reporting max|PF|/F_pred per run as a dimensionless ratio, i.e. it retires the frozen 0.21 literal, not the measurement. I recomputed the float32 figure (10*sqrt(1.1920929e-07)*0.4999048934*2828099.2886817832 = 4881.3 pN, ratio 23170.5) — correct, but it is a property of sqrt(eps)*ell/dt_mu, not of max|PF|.

The empirical evidence cited for max|PF| non-grid-invariance is confounded, and the same document says so one paragraph away. The 0.14/0.21/3.42 series (GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md:333-335) carries the doc's own §6.3 caveat that the 0.075 um rung ALSO changed cortex_density_per_fil 20->40, 'so the three rungs are not a clean one-parameter refinement'; and line 364 attributes the 3.42 plateau to 'a geometric kink being resolved', i.e. an 8 nm construction artifact, not a refinement measurement. missed_defects: SUMMARY STATISTIC #1 IS A TAUTOLOGY. ac/fluid/coupled_boundary_reference.py:179-198 computes adjoint_work_residual = |<Wv,g> - <v,W^T g>| from a SINGLE argument `spread`. lhs = np.dot(w @ v, g), rhs = np.dot(v, w.T @ g) (lines 196-197). That identity holds exactly for every real matrix; it can only fail if numpy's transpose is broken. The test asserts < 1e-12 (tests/ac/fluid/test_coupled_boundary_reference.py:70) and is guaranteed to pass. The physics question — do the ENGINE's scatter and gather use the same stencil — is precisely what this cannot test, because both inner products are built from the same W. It is also not a dimensionless ratio: it returns an absolute work difference with no normalizer. This is the Young-Dupre-120.0000-by-construction pattern, and the audit ranked it its first summary statistic.

THE 'SECOND INSTANCE' OF ADJOINT CLOSURE IS DEAD CODE. ac/engine/linc_connector.py:884-887 raises if abs(self.force_residual_pn)/abs(self.work_residual_pn_um) exceed caller tolerances — but the residuals are DATA handed to a frozen dataclass, and LINC has zero non-test importers (grep for 'linc_connector' outside tests returns only tests/ac/engine/test_linc_connector.py) and is not exported from ac/engine/__init__.py. SUMMARY STATISTIC #2 HAS NEVER SEEN PHYSICS, AND IS A GATE A BROKEN BUILD PASSES. GlobalCellLedger.add_cell_traction (ac/engine/ledger.py:265-283) has NO production caller — a repo-wide grep finds it only in ledger.py and tests/ac/engine/test_ledger.py:112,148,160. Only add_far_field_reaction is ever called in production (ac/engine/ecm_world.py:570). Therefore traction_resultant_d is identically zero in every run and _assemble_force_balance_kernel (ledger.py:140-146) computes |reaction + 0|^2, i.e. it degenerates from a Newton's-third-law check into 'the far-field boundary reaction resultant is zero'. The ledger docstring's claim that the two channels are 'independently sourced so the balance gate cannot self-satisfy' (ledger.py:12-22) is true of the API and false of the wiring. assemble_balance HAS NEVER EXECUTED IN A NATIVE RUN, AND THE AUDIT'S REPORTED OBSERVABLE IS NOT WHAT IT COMPUTES. PHASE 2'S CORE RULE IS UNSATISFIABLE TODAY AND CONTRADICTS EVERY EXISTING MEASUREMENT. Phase 2 mandates 'Emit the summary vector ONLY from the accepted-step ledger, never from a driver-side host computation.' But (a) every native driver force-accepts: accepted_d = ones at ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:515, ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:497-501, ac_gate_b_erm_cortex_native.py:360, ac_gate_b_interior_column_native.py:303, ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:232 — so 'accepted-step' carries no acceptance information; (b) no native driver accumulates a real ledger (ac_gate_b_ecm_forces_native.py:165 passes _NoOpLedger()); and (c) every quoted native number is a driver-side host readback (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:181-182 force_d.numpy()/pos_d.numpy(), :509 _max_force_norm). 'FA REACTION INWARD FRACTION = 100%' IS A TAUTOLOGY OF ITS OWN REFERENCE FRAME. ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:387 sets centroid = np.asarray(population.pos).mean(axis=0) — the mean of the very SF nodes whose forces are then projected on (pos - centroid) at :183-191. For any uniformly contracting point cloud every force points toward its own mean by definition of the mean, so inward_fraction = 1.0 is arithmetic, not physics. The driver's own docstring says so: ':171-178 A ventral SF is a closed dipole ... so a contracting fiber pulls each anchor TOWARD the fiber's interior. The radial projection is THEREFORE NEGATIVE for contraction.' Compounding it: the metric is saturated at 1.0, so as an NRE summary it has zero variance and zero Fisher information; the test is `projection < 0.0` (strict), so an exactly-unloaded FA counts as not-inward, making it a boolean dressed as a fraction; and `force_d` at a Dirichlet-pinned FA node is the WHOLE residual there (bending + links + WCA + crossbridge), not the clutch load — the 'FA Dirichlet reaction read as traction' item in the PI's inventory, which the audit admitted without inspecting.

'BIPOLAR DOT (GEOMETRIC IDENTITY -1)' IS ADMITTED AS A SUMMARY WHILE BEING LABELLED AN IDENTITY IN THE SAME SENTENCE. A quantity that is -1 by construction is a constant column in the design matrix — it contributes exactly zero to any log-ratio. The audit forbids tautological metrics in list (i)-(iv) and then puts two of them (this and FA inward fraction) in its own Family-3.

ff_virial_stress OMITS THE DOMINANT CORTICAL STRESS CARRIER AND USES A LUMPED MOTOR. ff/ff_virial_stress.py:33-62 assembles sigma_node from crosslinks (k_xl(L-r0)) + myosin + turgor ONLY. It omits the actin BACKBONE axial tension — the principal deviatoric carrier in a cortex, and the same Lagrange-multiplier term the project separately measures as ~77% of the raw residual — and omits ERM tethers and WCA. Worse, its myosin term is a CONSTANT scalar f_myo applied per link (:33, :47-49), i.e. an aggregate/lumped motor: the reported 'per-node virial von-Mises stress' does not measure the head-resolved crossbridge forces the engine computes, it re-derives them from a swept constant. The audit admitted this as Family-6 without reading it. (Its formula transcription 'sigma = (1/V)*sum 0.5*(r x f)' is also wrong notation — the code is an outer product at :26, not a cross product.)

method_of_planes_gamma IS NORMALISED BY A NOMINAL RADIUS AND RETURNS A POSITIVELY BIASED |mean|. ff/gamma_estimator.py:92 sets circ = 2.0*np.pi*R with R a CALLER-SUPPLIED scalar, not the deformed cut perimeter. Line 103 returns np.mean(np.abs(gammas)), the mean of ABSOLUTE per-orientation sums, so a zero-mean tension field yields gamma > 0: a positive bias floor on the project's one surviving headline deficit. And `tension` is passed in as data (:68), so what gamma measures depends entirely on the caller. Rated 'intensive' and admitted without inspection.

THE AUDIT'S STRUCTURAL PROOF AGAINST AGGREGATE SUBSTITUTES IS A SELF-DECLARED ATTRIBUTE CHECK. ac/engine/nmii_actuator.py:460-482 tests getattr(mechanics, 'explicit_stam_hocky_backbone', False) is not True, ... arithmetic_corrections: THE raw-|F| DECOMPOSITION IS FALSE AS AN EQUATION AND THE AUDIT PROPAGATED IT. It writes 'raw 5.7892 = |J^T lambda| 4.4820 + max|PF| 1.7399'. 4.4820 + 1.7399 = 6.2219, which is 7.47% ABOVE 5.7892. These are maxima of three different fields taken at different nodes; the only valid relation is max|F| <= max|J^T lambda| + max|PF| (which holds: 5.7892 <= 6.2219). Downstream, contract_changes.yaml:112 derives '~70-80% of the residual is constraint tension' as 4.4820/5.7892 = 77.42% — a ratio of two unrelated cross-node maxima presented as a per-node partition.
