feasibility_corrections: DECISIVE, AND THE AUDIT NEVER CHECKED IT: MECHANICAL LOAD COUPLES ALL BINDING STATES GLOBALLY, SO THE BLOCK FACTORIZATION IS INVALID. The primary design is a 'hierarchical/factorized NRE, trained per compartment-block, summing per-observable log-ratios'. That sum requires log r(theta|y) = sum_b log r_b(theta_b|y_b), i.e. block-wise parameter separation AND conditional independence of block observables. The code refutes both: (a) the inner mechanics is ONE global solve over an augmented actin + ERM-membrane block (ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:952-1115, and :1575 'membrane, ERM anchors, fibers and nucleus through one smooth global displacement'); (b) per-head crossbridge loads are computed FROM the converged global geometry (compute_head_loads_segment_split_r0bind_kernel, ac/engine/cortex_motor_slice.py:520, dispatched after the pipeline in composed_native.solve_candidate:347-359); (c) each head's detach hazard then consumes that global load (head_load_bell_d at cortex_motor_slice.py:752-753, catch-slip default at :424-425). The magnitude of the coupling is measured in the audit's own headline artifact: gate_b_dynamic_v2.npz gives gamma_total 3.7234 = gamma_source 0.0191 + gamma_network 3.7043, i.e. 99.5% of motor-driven cortical tension is carried by the passive network responding to the motor load. A per-block NMII surrogate therefore cannot observe the quantity its own parameters move. The audit framed this risk exclusively as population coarseness (its M5 'deepest trap') and mitigated it statistically in Phase 4; the defect is structural and Phase 4 cannot repair it.

THE 'SLICES ARE CHEAP' PREMISE IS FALSE FOR THE FLAGSHIP BLOCK. The audit assumes 10 blocks x 5,000 sims x 30 s. But the cortex-motor 'slice' — the block carrying its largest parameter cluster — runs at FULL native 70,686 filaments / 494,802 nodes (gate_b_dynamic_v2.npz manifest: cmp_cortex_pos shape (494802,3), n_actors 70686). Its wall time is recorded nowhere in the artifact. So the 17.4-GPU-day estimate cannot apply to at least one and plausibly several blocks; P5 should have named this specific contradiction rather than a generic 'slice wall time is unmeasured'.

C_solve = 940 s PRICES AN OPERATION THAT HAS NEVER COMPLETED. The audit marks 940 s 'PARENT-ASSERTED, UNVERIFIED' and proceeds. The disk says something stronger: the only committed full-compartment native outer step reports inner_converged=false, outer_rolled_back=true, and residual_end == residual_start == 2634.1191655118346 EXACTLY (outputs/ac/resting_native/resting_native_probe_2026-07-23.json) — 182.5 s that changed no state. Every accelerated probe on disk also ends converged=false (163.586 s tournament, 1274.588 s kxb, both fine-mesh runs). There is therefore no measured cost anywhere for one ACCEPTED, CONVERGED native step, and the entire budget (92 solves/day, 1,378 3-seed adjudication points/quarter) is priced on an unachieved operation. This is a strictly stronger version of the audit's own P5/OQ4 and it did not make it.

PHASE 1 IS SEQUENCED AGAINST ITS OWN FAILURE MODE. Phase 1 (CRN sensitivity) is declared 'IMMEDIATE, no surrogate needed' and placed BEFORE P1 (a converging coupled lane), which the audit itself calls 'BLOCKING for any training label'. But a sensitivity matrix IS a measurement, and common-random-number finite differences on unconverged solves measure d(relaxation transient)/d(theta), not d(equilibrium observable)/d(theta). The audit's own failure mode 'UNCONVERGED LABELS' and the recorded fact that a 10x longer relax moved T_max by 3.4x at identical bound population (gate_contracts/GATE_B_sf_motor.yaml, explicit_relax_iterations note) apply verbatim. Phase 1 cannot be simultaneously prerequisite-free and label-grade; either it is gated on P1 or its deliverable must be explicitly labelled transient-sensitivity.

MEMORY IS NEVER COSTED, ON A 16 GB SINGLE-GPU PLAN. The plan is otherwise executable on one A5000 — nothing in it needs a cluster, and the CPU-side NRE training (5-member ensembles, d<=13 blocks) is trivial. But the composed multi-compartment native configuration's peak bytes appear nowhere in the arithmetic. The only committed peak-bytes claim is for the fine 75 nm cortex alone ('peak bytes logged < 16 GB', FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:294). CLAUDE.md's rule is that memory pressure is answered with more hardware, never lower density — so peak bytes for the adjudication configuration is a prerequisite the plan omits.

The Phase-3 harness choice is sound and I confirm it. ac/engine/ensemble.py provides EnsembleRunner with np.random.SeedSequence(base_seed).spawn reproducibility (:412-422), RealizationResult (:240), ObservableDistribution.within_band (:335), and mix_ensembles; it imports no warp and is CPU-importable as claimed. That part of the feasibility case holds.
hard_rule_problems: THE AUDIT VIOLATES ITS OWN FORBIDDEN-LIST ITEM (iv) IN ITS OWN ADMITTED SUMMARIES. It forbids 'any observable whose evaluation needs a PI-GAP magnitude', then admits Family-5 'gamma_measured / (dP*R/2)' and Family-6 'per-node virial von-Mises stress ... turgor hydrostatic'. Both carry Pi_0, which GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md §6.4 classifies 'CONVENIENCE — Fischer-Friedrich 2014 HeLa interphase, wrong cell line' with three live values in the tree (40 Pa at ac/cell/assemble.py:147 via common/turgor_pi0.py:60; 133 Pa band-implied and circular; ~72 Pa MCF7-geometry) = a 3.3x spread. And gamma at the motor-loaded baseline is 99.5% passive network (gate_b_dynamic_v2). Since the PI has stated magnitudes are explicitly NOT the current gate, both families are inadmissible right now on the PI's own priority, not merely risky.

THE BLOCK-FACTORIZED LOG-RATIO SUM IS ITSELF A LUMPED SUBSTITUTE. The audit's hard_rule_interaction argues admissibility on three grounds — cannot be a mechanism, cannot be a measurement, cannot be credited — and never asks whether the FACTORIZATION is a lumped proxy. Applying CLAUDE.md's own test ('does this replace a mechanistic process with a lumped one?'): the true likelihood is globally coupled through one displacement solve and load-dependent Bell/catch-slip hazards (see feasibility item 1); the sum of per-block log-ratios is the mean-field approximation of that joint. This is the same class as the aggregate two-anchor NMII kernel the I0-A contract permits only as a diagnostic. It needs either an explicit non-factorized design or an explicit PI ratification that a mean-field INFERENCE (as distinct from a mean-field runtime) is admissible.

ADDING `INFERRED` TO PROVENANCE IS A GATE-CONTRACT CHANGE SHIPPED AS PHASE-0 HYGIENE, AND ITS RANKING MECHANISM DOES NOT EXIST. PROVENANCE currently has four labels (ac/engine/forces_manifest.py:90) and PI_GAP is the honest label for an unsourced quantity. INFERRED gives an unsourced number a legitimizing tier. The audit ranks it below DERIVED, but verify_params.py has no provenance ranking at all (its ladder is citation-verdict based, :93), and the only ranking machinery — verify_forces.py provenance_allow/PROVENANCE_REGRESSION (:286-291, :84) — is wired into no gate. As proposed, the demotion is stated, not mechanical: the vocabulary change lands and the enforcement does not.

IMPORTING THE UNDRIVED 1% residual/tension LITERAL AS A BLOCKING TRAINING-LABEL GATE IS A MAGIC NUMBER. The contract itself records derivation: NONE_ON_DISK and 'FLAGGED' for that value (gate_contracts/GATE_B_sf_motor.yaml). Using it as a hard admission criterion for every label in verify_surrogate.py propagates it into a new gate without derivation.

NO GATE-LOOSENING FOUND, but three schema changes need signed contract rows the audit does not request. G1-G7 all tighten or add; nothing loosens an existing threshold, and the audit correctly routes gate changes through contract_changes.yaml. However: (a) making evidence_origin a REQUIRED field on every results_manifest.yaml row changes the results contract and will fail every existing row on first run; (b) adding INFERRED changes the PROVENANCE vocabulary; (c) adding required grid_invariance_evidence and magnitude_free fields changes every gate contract's hash. The audit asks for a signed row only for the third. All three are contract changes and should be surfaced as such.

The audit's typed-hash and negative-control proposals are the right shape and the precedent it cites is real (ffn_sim/outputs/tag_kb/verify_gate_contracts_negcontrol.py exists). The import-firewall mechanism it cites is also real and correctly located: the hoomd meta_path blocker is at repo-root conftest.py:231-256 installed at :279, and the AST scan is at ffn_sim/tests/ac/test_warp_only_contract.py:5-60. Those parts of the enforcement design need no revision — the problem is the two unwired gates and the misnamed provenance site above.

result.summary:
The audit's DIAGNOSTIC half is unusually solid: I independently reproduced every number in the threshold derivation (kmax = 2,828,099.2886817832 pN/µm, F_pred = 0.2106697371 pN, float32 ×23,170, steric-off 0.06109, bending crossover 2.9521 nm, seg 0.2 → 0.0842839, seg 0.075 → 0.0316065), and I reproduced the negative-control counts EXACTLY by running the script (5/9 with --assume-kmax 1.0, 6/9 with --assume-seg 1e-4), with the four permanently-passing checks being precisely the four it names. Every ABSENT verdict checks out: no definition site for 0.21 and no 0.21 anywhere in driver.py / inner_mechanics.py / ac/engine (reporting-only, confirmed); no production supplier for tol_sq_d; no moment or centroid channel in GlobalCellLedger against four moment promises in ecm_world.py; no A/B comparison code; no rms nodal force. The PCG zero-RHS latch, the abscissa detach reset, and all four residual_over_tension defects are real as described.

But the audit's PRIMARY DELIVERABLE — the canonical replacement resting gate (1a) — is inverted, and it is inverted on the single number the whole safety argument rests on. It claims max|PF_i|/K_ii ≤ min(2.7 nm, sqrt(kBT/K_ii)) is "TIGHTER than 0.21 pN ... at essentially all 494,802 pure-actin bending nodes (K ~ 0.58), by x134". Two independent code facts refute that. First, the assembled diagonal for cytosim bending is 6α, not α (add_bending_preconditioner_kernel adds α to each outer node and 4α to the centre; an interior node sums 6α = 3.4925 pN/µm) so even the idealised tightening is ×22, not ×134. Second and decisively, the production cortex is not crosslink-free: the project's own committed geometry check records n_xl = 1,413,720 and 5.71 ± 2.40 crosslinks per node with only 0.34% carrying none, at ALPHA_ACTININ link_k = 4.6e5 pN/µm. A typical actin node's per-axis Hessian diagonal is therefore ~8.76e5 pN/µm (trace 2.63e6), sqrt(kBT/K_ii) = 0.070 nm collapses onto the thermal branch, and the per-node bound becomes sqrt(kBT·K_ii) = 61-106 pN — a 290-500× LOOSENING at ~99.7% of the actin population, not a tightening. This also puts the proposal in direct contradiction with the audit's own WORDING RULE, which forbids sqrt(kBT·K_ii) as a pass criterion because it is looser than 0.21 by ×9.8-×210. That is the exact class of error the audit exists to stop, and its own meta-gate (5) would have caught it.

Three other things need fixing before this is actionable. (i) A missed defect that breaks the audit's own proposed balance tolerance: GlobalCellLedger.reset() has zero non-test callers, and CellTransaction.step accumulates without resetting, so reaction/traction/force/work/mass are CUMULATIVE across accepted steps — a relative tolerance eps_bal·max(|R|,|T|) then loosens roughly linearly in step count. (ii) The audit's flagship membrane refutation is right but under-evidenced: it proposed "refine a shell with the solver disabled" as a control to run, when ac_membrane_mesh_floor.py already IS that control (build_cell → _accumulate_all → readback, no relax, no ERM preload), and driver.py already documents the mechanism verbatim ("every tether is force-free and the membrane carries the full turgor pressure (~ΔP·A_node per node) unbalanced"). Independent check: Π₀·4πR² = 28,274 pN vs measured Σ|PF| 26,380/26,215 = 93% at both meshes. The refutation is mechanical, not inferential. (iii) The single control the audit recommends building FIRST as "the cheapest test" is not runnable: I executed ac_composed_world_dump.py and it raises TypeError: connector 'membrane_erm_cortex' has an incomplete runtime API; missing ('propose_events',). There is no 32-connector composed slice to disconnect.

Keep the diagnosis, keep the cut-plane identity and GATE C (both well-posed and magnitude-free), re-derive (1a) against the measured K_ii distribution before it goes to PI, and route it as an explicit gate-loosening contract change.
false_alarms: missing_instruments, 't0 (pre-step) telemetry row for the motor slices ... telemetry prints only after slc.step, so no run record contains the zero-state baseline' — FALSE for the SF motor slice, which is the slice whose 'emerges from zero' claim is at issue. ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:481-493 computes `rest` (n_bound, sf_maxF_pN, nmii_maxF_pN, T_max/T_mean/T_abs_max) BEFORE the step loop, prints it as '(1) REST', hard-exits at :493-494 if any head is bound at t0, and persists it into the report JSON at :621. The claim holds only for ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py (whose only `t0` is a wall-clock timer at :464). Mis-scoped from one slice to 'the motor slices'.

abscissa, verdict MISLEADING_NAME — the code never uses the audited name. Every definition site calls it a walked displacement in µm: ffn_sim/ac/motor/resting_setpoint.py:97 'walked power-stroke displacement [µm]'; ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:887 'a positive abscissa (the power stroke) then yields |f| = k_xb·abscissa'; ffn_sim/ac/motor/powerstroke_analytic.py:74 'x_att = anchor + abscissa * walk_dir [µm]'. 'Accumulated power-stroke' is the inventory label the reviewer was told not to trust. The substantive caution (Σabscissa is not cumulative; segment_motor.py:182 / hand.py:207,248 reset on detach) is correct and worth keeping as a forward guard, but it is not a defect in the code as written. Its stated urgency ('abscissa is the leading candidate for the converged-vs-transient discriminator') has no on-disk basis either — the only use of abscissa in the gate script is the rollback bit-equality check at ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:535,544.

Oracle (6)'s stated mechanism is wrong, though its recommendation is right. 'With one connector contributing zero force, the PCG zero-RHS branch latches converged = 1' — `rr` is the GLOBAL dot(r,r) over all n nodes (ffn_sim/ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:2062 reduces self.r over dim=self.n; _cg_begin_kernel:1343 branches on that single scalar). Zeroing one connector in a composed cell leaves rr > 0, so the latch does NOT fire. The false-PASS mechanism the audit describes exists only for a degenerate single-connector slice. Fix the justification; keep the control.

Verdict TAUTOLOGICAL on GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION is too coarse for the evidence. I ran it: 5 of 9 checks are input-sensitive and the two most load-bearing (reproduce_native_predicate_force_exact, frozen_literal_is_route_c) DO fail under both negative controls. The script's own Sanity Gate (ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py:27-30) scopes the negative control to 'the reproduction check' and honours that scope. The defect is the headline aggregation '9/9 checks pass -> DERIVATION VERIFIED' and the four unlabelled identities — not the instrument. Downgrade to MISLEADING_AGGREGATION or report per-check.

Novelty overclaim (not an error, but it inflates the audit's contribution and should be corrected before this reaches PI): the ell^+1 scaling of route (c), the 'FAIL 2.5x' verdict at seg 0.2, the signed-radial oracle gamma_spur = S/(8*pi*R), the mean|PF|-falls-as-ell diagnostic, and the L1/traction admissible-norm point are ALL already computed and printed by ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py (route_d_radial_bias_budget_pn at :380; the grid-scaling table at :467-469 prints 'FAIL 2.5x' and 'FAIL 108.2x'; route (d3) states 'mean|PF| must fall as O(ell^1) ... because a nodal force is a force DENSITY times ell'). The nucleus-dominance point is already ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:106, and the GATE-A withdrawal is already stamped at ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/GATE_A_RESTING_CONVERGENCE_2026-07-23.md:329-340 ('this item is a PROPOSAL, status PROVISIONAL — PI ratification pending').
missed_defects: CRITICAL, and it breaks the audit's own proposal (2): GlobalCellLedger is NEVER RESET between accepted steps. ffn_sim/ac/engine/ledger.py:225-237 defines reset(), and it has ZERO non-test call sites — the only caller in the tree is ffn_sim/tests/ac/engine/test_ledger.py:166. ffn_sim/ac/engine/transaction.py:131-135 calls self.world.accumulate_ledgers(ledger) with no reset, then optionally assemble_balance. So reaction_resultant, traction_resultant, force_resultant, work and mass accumulate MONOTONICALLY over the whole run. Consequences: (a) assemble_balance checks |Sum_steps R + Sum_steps T|, a cumulative not per-step identity; (b) the audit's recommended relative tolerance |R+T| <= eps_bal*max(|R|,|T|,F_floor) has a denominator that grows ~linearly in step count, so the gate LOOSENS without bound over a run — the precise failure mode the audit was written to prevent. Any tolerance recommendation must first fix or declare the accumulation semantics.

Stale acceptance predicate. ffn_sim/ac/engine/transaction.py:137-144: when accepted_d is None and tol_sq_d is None, the predicate silently becomes ledger.balance_ok_d, which assemble_balance did NOT write this step (the guard at :116 only rejects tol_sq_d without a ledger, not a ledger without tol_sq_d). Combined with the no-reset defect above, a balance_ok value set on an earlier step is reused as this step's acceptance predicate. First step is fail-closed (wp.zeros), which is why nobody has seen it.

The audit's flagship membrane refutation is correct but under-evidenced, and the stronger proof was already on disk. It proposes as a negative control 'refine ANY smooth pressurised shell with the solver disabled (zero solver iterations) ... This is a 5-minute CPU test'. ffn_sim/scripts/ac_membrane_mesh_floor.py:24-40 IS that test as executed: build_cell -> _accumulate_all(cell, cell.pos_d, f) -> host readback, with no relax, no inner solve, and no call to _preload_erm_resting_balance. So the '6->8 grid convergence' was measured with the solver doing literally zero work. And ffn_sim/ac/cell/driver.py:182-187 states the mechanism verbatim: 'At build each ERM rest length equals its formation length, so every tether is force-free and the membrane carries the full turgor pressure (~DeltaP*A_node per node, ~40 pN here) unbalanced ... a relaxed cortex plus a positive turgor is not a valid resting baseline (PI physiological-baseline rule) — there is no force-balanced equilibrium there'. Independent numeric confirmation: Pi_0*4*pi*R^2 = 40*706.86 = 28,274 pN vs the measured Sum|PF| of 26,380 (subdiv 6) and 26,215 (subdiv 8) = 93% of the full unbalanced turgor traction at BOTH meshes. The refutation is therefore MECHANICAL, not an inference from two table rows, and the audit's own 'HONEST LIMIT' caveat about sign cancellation is unnecessary here: at t0 on a symmetric icosphere the residual is radial and single-signed by construction, so S is essentially Sum|PF|.

The membrane subdiv 6->8 pair is NOT strictly one-parameter, contrary to 'the membrane subdiv 6->8 pair IS clean'. ac_membrane_mesh_floor.py:47-49 builds with erm_radial_pairing=True, and ffn_sim/ac/cell/compartments.py:655-663 then creates one ERM tether per membrane vertex, so n_erm goes 40,962 -> 655,362 with the mesh — the same class of co-varying confound the audit correctly rejects for the cortex series (density_per_fil 20->40). It happens to be inert because compartments.py:678-681 sets erm_rest = |mem - cortex| at build, making every tether force-free at t0. That inertness must be established, not assumed.

The physiological rung was already measured FAILING, which settles the audit's open question (a) without a new run. ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/NATIVE_QUEUE_RESULTS_2026-07-24.md:98-100: with the production preload (_preload_cortex_pretension + _preload_erm_resting_balance) at subdiv 8, 'the inner solve CONVERGES (max|PF| ~= 0.28, vs the un-preloaded rolled-back ~1.6)'. 0.28 > 0.21. So the correctly-preloaded subdiv-8 baseline fails the incumbent gate, and the closure the audit asks PI to rule on is already withdrawn twice on disk (GATE_A_RESTING_CONVERGENCE_2026-07-23.md:329-340 status stamp; AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:106 'The physiological-mesh rung is 0.28 > 0.21').

The derivation's single positive-control artifact is off-config, and the audit propagates it without noticing. ffn_sim/outputs/ac/resting_native/resting_native_probe2_capture0.6_2026-07-23.json reports N_crosslinks = 70,686 for N_nodes = 494,802 — i.e. cortex_density_per_fil = 1.0, the RETIRED fragmented build. The production coarse cortex is n_xl = 1,413,720 (ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/FINE_CORTEX_GEOMETRY_CHECK_2026-07-24.md:35). Inert for kmax (steric dominates at 2.83e6 either way), but the ONE artifact anchoring reproduce_native_kmax and reproduce_native_predicate_force_exact is a config the project has replaced, and neither the script nor the audit says so. It is also the artifact whose crosslink count would have shown the audit that its K ~ 0.58 assumption is wrong.

Partly circular positive control. reproduce_native_predicate_force_exact (ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py:322-327) back-derives seg_mean_disk = tol_disk / sqrt(eps64) FROM the committed tolerance, then checks route_c(seg_mean_disk, kmax) == tol_disk/dtmu_disk. Since route_c multiplies sqrt(eps64)*seg back in, the seg factor cancels identically and the check reduces to 0.1/kmax == dtmu_disk. That is a real check on kmax (and it passes to rel 0.0e+00), but it is NOT an independent verification of the ell dependence, and the audit reports it as reproducing the identity 'to rel=0.0e+00' without noting the cancellation. Using the CONFIG seg instead (the from_config variant) gives rel 1.902e-04, and my own end-to-end recomputation gives rel 4.7e-11 against the artifact — not 0.

The PCG stopping criterion is arguably mis-specified, not merely under-budgeted, and the audit's SOUND rating lets it off. ||r||/||r_0|| <= sqrt(eps64) = 1.49e-8 is an 8-decade reduction; at the Gershgorin condition number the audit itself cites (~5e6, alpha-actinin 4.6e5 over bending 0.582), CG needs ~0.5*sqrt(kappa)*ln(2/tol) ~ 2.1e4 iterations against max_iterations = 32 (implicit_mechanics.py:1463, confirmed in the artifact as implicit_cg_max_iterations 32) — short by ~650x. Because decide_better_line_search_trial_kernel (:431-435) takes NO trial unless linear_converged != 0, the criterion is the direct mechanism of the recorded '0.0% position change over 3,000 iterations'. A stopping target that is unreachable by three orders of magnitude at the shipped budget, and that gates all progress on being met, is a specification defect.
arithmetic_corrections: INVERTED, and this is the audit's headline claim. 'the local channel is TIGHTER than 0.21 pN by x134 at the ~494,802 actin bending nodes ... looser only at the stiff minority, so it is not gate-loosening in the region that carries the tension measurement'. Two code facts refute it. (i) The assembled per-node diagonal for cytosim bending is 6*alpha, not alpha: ffn_sim/ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:507-517 adds alpha to triples[t,0] and triples[t,2] and 4*alpha to triples[t,1], so an interior filament node accumulates 4a+a+a = 6a = 6*0.58208 = 3.4925 pN/um at seg 0.5 (verified: this is the exact Hessian diagonal of E=(alpha/2)|x_{i-1}-2x_i+x_{i+1}|^2, whose 1-D biharmonic diagonal is 1+4+1). Implied bound = 3.4925*0.0027 = 9.43e-3 pN, so the tightening is x22, not x134. (ii) Decisively: the production cortex is NOT pure-bending. ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/FINE_CORTEX_GEOMETRY_CHECK_2026-07-24.md:35,44 records n_xl = 1,413,720 and crosslinks per node = 5.71 +/- 2.40, with only 1,683 nodes (0.34%) carrying zero. ffn_sim/ac/weave/regions.py:210 sets xl_k = CORTEX.crosslinker.hand.link_k, which I resolved to ALPHA_ACTININ link_k = 460,000 pN/um. add_pair_preconditioner_kernel (implicit_mechanics.py:574-586) with _central_diagonal (:96-108) deposits k*u_a^2 per axis on each endpoint (transverse_k = 0 at rest), so a typical actin node's per-axis diagonal is 5.71*4.6e5/3 = 8.76e5 pN/um (trace 2.63e6). At K_ii = 8.76e5, sqrt(kBT/K_ii) = 0.0699 nm << 2.7 nm, so min() selects the THERMAL branch and the per-node bound is sqrt(kBT*K_ii) = 61.2 pN (trace variant 106 pN). That is 291x (to 505x) LOOSER than 0.21 pN at ~99.7% of the 494,802 actin nodes — the opposite of the claimed direction, and it inverts the recommendation to PI.

Self-contradiction created by the same arithmetic. Because K_ii > kBT/(2.7 nm)^2 = 587.1 pN/um at essentially every crosslinked actin node, delta*_i = min(2.7 nm, sqrt(kBT/K_ii)) collapses to sqrt(kBT/K_ii) and the gate reduces EXACTLY to |PF_i| <= sqrt(kBT*K_ii). The audit's own WORDING RULE states 'this ceiling must NEVER be swapped in as a pass criterion, since it is looser than 0.21 by x9.8 to x210'. Oracle (1a) is that ceiling for the bulk of the population.

Dimensional slip: 'The existing test value 1.0e-18 pN^2 (= 1e-9 pN absolute) is ~6400x above the round-off floor'. 6400 = 1e-9 / 1.56e-13, which treats eps_bal = 10*sqrt(N)*eps64 as if it were a FORCE. It is dimensionless (ffn_sim/ac/engine/ledger.py:130-143 compares n2 [pN^2] against tol_sq [pN^2]). Comparing an absolute pN tolerance to a relative epsilon requires a force scale; without one the '6400x' is unanchored. In an audit whose subject is dimensional hygiene this needs fixing before it is quoted.

eps_bal is quoted inconsistently and reintroduces the N-dependence the relative form was chosen to remove. The 'measured floors' listed (1.56e-13, 1.80e-13, 3.78e-13) are sqrt(N)*eps64, i.e. eps_bal/10 — I reproduce them exactly (sqrt(494802)*2.2204e-16 = 1.562e-13; sqrt(655362)* = 1.797e-13; sqrt(2898126)* = 3.780e-13). The recommended 'eps_bal ~ 1e-12' therefore matches only the smallest N; across the stated range eps_bal spans 1.56e-12 to 3.78e-12, a factor 2.4. Also worth stating: sqrt(N)*eps is the STATISTICAL (random-walk) round-off estimate, not a bound; a worst-case atomic-order bound is O(N*eps).

Over-precision on the membrane pair. 'Sum|PF| = 26,379.5 -> 26,214.5 pN, a 0.63% difference' and 'mean ratio = 16.1 vs N ratio = 16.00' both rest on a 2-significant-figure input (mean 0.040 at subdiv 8, from GATE_A_RESTING_CONVERGENCE_2026-07-23.md:136). +/-0.0005 on 0.040 is +/-1.25% on the L1 total, so the honest statement is 'invariant to within the ~1.3% precision of the reported mean', not 0.63%. The direction and the conclusion are robust; the quoted precision is not earned. (N ratio itself: 655362/40962 = 15.99927, so '16.00' is right.)

CONFIRMED EXACT, recomputed independently end-to-end (no reliance on the audited script): sqrt(eps64) = 1.4901161193847656e-08; epsilon_from_contact_stiffness(1e3, 0.007) = 8.574462700673442e-04; max_core_stiffness(1000, 0.007, eps) = 2,828,099.2886817832 pN/um (matches the committed ledger kmax_pN_per_um bit-for-bit); F_pred at the realized ell = 0.4999048934 is 0.21066973707572859 pN vs artifact inner_tolerance_um/inner_dt_mu = 7.449163398500275e-09/3.535943748517097e-08 = 0.21066973708573 (rel 4.7e-11, not 0); float32 ratio 23,170.47; steric-off kmax = filamin 8.2e5 -> 0.06109 pN (ratio to 0.2107 = 3.45x); seg 0.2 -> 0.0842839267 (frozen literal 2.49x looser); seg 0.075 -> 0.0316064725 (6.64x); KAPPA_ACTIN = 0.0727602023 pN*um^2, alpha(0.5) = 0.5820816184, bending/steric crossover h = (kappa/kmax)^(1/3) = 2.9521137 nm; kBT = 4.280011900e-03 pN*um; sqrt(kBT*1000) = 2.0688 (9.85x above 0.21); sqrt(kBT*4.6e5) = 44.37 (211x); f_head 1.5/2.0688 = 0.725; kBT/(0.0027)^2 = 587.06 pN/um; 0.21/0.0027 = 77.8 pN/um; sqrt(kBT/1e5) = 0.2069 nm; membrane traction 26,379.5/706.86 = 37.32 and 26,214.5/706.86 = 37.08 pN/um^2; gamma_spur = 26,214.5/(8*pi*7.5) = 139.1 = 92.7% of 150. Negative-control fail-counts reproduced by execution: baseline 9/9, --assume-kmax 1.0 -> 5/9, --assume-seg 1e-4 -> 6/9, and the four checks that survive both are exactly {dimensions, dt_mu_units, limiting_case_sigma_radial, route_c_scales_linearly_in_seg}. route_c_scales_linearly_in_seg is algebraically an identity: route_c(c,s,kmax)/s = sqrt(eps64)*kmax/0.1 with no s dependence (ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py:369-375), so spread is float64 noise for any input — the audit's read is exactly right.

One scaling claim I checked that the audit asserts without verifying, and that HOLDS: 'kmax is set by the WCA near-core term, a function of f_cap, sigma_EV, epsilon only'. assemble.py:979-1001 also folds in membrane and nucleus kappa_tilde/ell^3 terms, which ARE mesh-dependent, and calibrate_kappa_tilde (lamina_analytic.py:107-116) makes kappa_tilde grid-invariant (8*pi*kappa/Sigma_ref, Sigma_ref a topological constant ~7.5-22). So membrane refinement drives kappa_tilde/ell^3 as h^-3: with kappa_m = 0.0828 pN*um, kappa_tilde ~ 0.28 pN*um, giving ~128 pN/um at subdiv 6 (131 nm) and ~7.99e3 pN/um at subdiv 8 (33 nm) — both still far below 2.83e6, so kmax is indeed steric-set through subdiv 8 and the ell^+1 scaling survives. Worth recording because it would BREAK around subdiv 12-13, and because refining only the membrane TIGHTENS the executing predicate (tolerance_um tracks the ACTIN seg_mean via assemble.py:1119 / driver.py:506, while dt_mu tracks the global kmax).
feasibility_corrections: NOT RUNNABLE as the recommended first step. Oracle (6), the DISCONNECTION NEGATIVE CONTROL — 'For every one of the 32 connectors, run the composed slice with that connector contributing NO force' — 'I recommend this as the first instrument built, ahead of any magnitude work, because it is the cheapest test'. I executed the only builder of the 32-connector world: PYTHONPATH=/Users/sw1/ffn_cellsim python ffn_sim/scripts/ac_composed_world_dump.py raises TypeError: connector 'membrane_erm_cortex' has an incomplete runtime API; missing ('propose_events',) from ffn_sim/ac/engine/actor.py:150 via assert_fully_bound at actor.py:125. ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:106 independently records '1 of 32 connectors is registered'. So the control is available today for the ~1-4 connectors carried by the working slices (sf_motor_slice, cortex_motor_slice, erm_cortex_slice, interior_column_slice), and standing it up for 32 is a composition project, not a control. The recommendation should be scoped to 'every connector in every runnable slice, plus a standing requirement that each new connector lands with its disconnection control'.

GATE C is the expensive item and the audit prices nothing. From committed timings across ffn_sim/outputs/ac/**: build_wall_s ~7.2-8.7 s at 70,686; inner_solve_wall_s_per_reported_iteration ranges 0.0181 s (explicit) to 1.327 s (rigid-cluster tournament), with the working tournament at ~0.818 s/it. C7's {n,2n,4n,8n} x C5's two structurally different solvers x C6's two step-scales is ~12 distinct full-native runs; at 400 inner iterations x 40 outer steps and 0.82 s/it that is ~3.6 GPU-hours per run, ~44 GPU-hours, i.e. ~2 days wall on the single A5000 (plus C1's kinetics-freeze harness, which does not exist). Feasible on one A5000 but not free, and it should be surfaced as a multi-day GPU budget rather than an unscoped 'implement it as GATE C'.

Feasible and cheap, confirmed: every proposed REDUCTION. S = Sum (PF_i . r_hat_i), Sum|PF_i|, nodal-force/nodal-area, the Jacobi implied-displacement field, the moment M, the centroid, and the traction dipole D are all O(N) device reductions over arrays that already exist, each writing a handful of (1,) scalars. At the largest declared N = 2,898,126 that is sub-millisecond per reduction and kilobytes of memory. The committed native ledger reports gpu_bytes_used = 519,110,656 and gpu_bytes_observed_after_step = 1,127,284,736 against gpu_bytes_total = 16,760,569,856 — ~7% of the A5000. No cluster assumption anywhere.

The Jacobi mechanism oracle (1a) depends on exists exactly as described, and I verified the caveat is mandatory rather than optional. ProjectedAnalyticCG.preconditioner is a per-node vec3d (implicit_mechanics.py:1525); _build_preconditioner (:1780-1800+) sums per-family EXACT diagonals (bending 6*alpha, pair springs k*u_a^2 at rest, plus angle/membrane/WCA/NMII families); apply_preconditioner_kernel (:798-806) forms preconditioned[i] = (r0/d0, r1/d1, r2/d2), i.e. the per-axis implied displacement. But set_preconditioner_kernel (:497-503) writes regularization[0] into EVERY entry first, and omitted_regularization_base (:1430-1455) takes max over {sqrt(eps64)*mechanical_kmax = 0.0421, nucleus k_vol = 1e3, k_ac = 150, kappa_tilde/edge^3, membrane kappa_tilde/edge^3} — so the floor is >= 1e3 pN/um at every node, which alone would put the 2.7 nm bound at 2.7 pN everywhere. The audit's 'MUST be launched with regularization = 0' is therefore load-bearing, not a nicety, and must be a code-enforced argument rather than a documented instruction.

The tensor-network track named in the attack brief has no counterpart in this family's findings, so there is nothing to verify there. The underlying question is however decisive for the audit's cut-plane oracle, so I answered it from the code: mechanical load DOES couple all binding states globally. Per-head loads_hill/loads_bell are read from the crossbridge force, which depends on pos after the global inner solve, and ffn_sim/ac/motor/segment_motor.py:173 advances abscissa[h] by tau*hill_velocity(loads_hill[h], ...) capped by da_max = max(0, (f_stall - loads_hill[h])/k_xb) once per ACCEPTED step. Every head's kinetics is thus coupled to every other head through the whole-cell mechanical solve. This makes the audit's C1 ('FREEZE THE PHYSICS ... disable ALL kinetics') genuinely mandatory rather than a precaution, and it confirms its diagnosis that the recorded 3.4x is an unseparated mixture of non-convergence and kinetic feedback which 'identical bound population' (a count) cannot pin.
hard_rule_problems: GATE-LOOSENING, presented as safe. Oracle (1a) / the first PI question recommend adopting max_i,axis |PF_i|/K_ii <= min(2.7 nm, sqrt(kBT/K_ii)) as the LOCAL resting gate on the stated ground that it 'is not gate-loosening in the region that carries the tension measurement'. Per the arithmetic corrections, at the production cortex's measured K_ii (5.71 crosslinks/node at 4.6e5 pN/um; 99.66% of nodes crosslinked) the criterion admits 61-106 pN per node versus the incumbent 0.21 pN — a 291-505x LOOSENING at essentially the entire actin population, which is precisely 'the region that carries the tension measurement'. Under the no-gate-loosening rule this cannot be recommended with a safety argument attached; it must go to PI as an explicit gate-contract change with the MEASURED per-node K_ii distribution (not an assumed K ~ 0.58) attached, and with the loosening factor stated. The audit does ask for ratification and does concede 'it IS a mixed-direction change' — but the direction it reports is inverted, so PI would be ratifying on a false premise.

Undeclared magnitude in a proposal that forbids them elsewhere. Oracle (2) writes |R + T| <= eps_bal * max(|R|, |T|, F_floor) and never derives F_floor, while oracle (3) explicitly defines its own F_floor as 'the round-off floor of the sum'. As written, for the case the criterion most needs to cover — a force-free symmetric sitter where |R| = |T| = 0 — the entire tolerance is set by an undefined constant. That is structurally the same defect the audit charges against residual_over_tension (a pass criterion proportional to an unsourced k_axial), and under PI priority 2 (magnitudes are explicitly not the current gate) a metric that cannot be evaluated without an undeclared constant is a bad metric.

Also a hard-rule issue in the same oracle: because the ledger never resets (see missed defects), the relative form's denominator max(|R|,|T|) is a run-cumulative quantity, so the proposed tolerance loosens monotonically with step count. A tolerance that loosens as the run proceeds is a gate-loosening mechanism even if its coefficient is derived from round-off.

CLEAN, for the record, so PI is not over-warned. Oracle (1a)'s two lengths are both sourced and magnitude-free: ACTIN_MONOMER_DELTA_UM = 0.0027 (ffn_sim/ac/weave/membrane_ratchet.py:65, Pollard axial rise) and kBT = 4.280011900e-03 pN*um (ffn_sim/ff/units.py). Oracle (1b) correctly defers the coherent fraction f ('ratify the FORM now and the fraction only after S has been measured natively once') and correctly insists on the relative form so it survives the live 3.3x Pi_0 spread. Oracle (3), the cut-plane transmission identity, is genuinely parameter-free (both sides scale with k_axial, k_xb, f_head) and is the strongest thing in the submission. Oracle (4) C4's 10^-p threshold is correctly framed as a declaration about the claim, not a physical constant. Retiring max|PF| as the CLOSING criterion is itself a gate-contract change and is correctly routed to PI.

result.summary: Structurally the audit holds: I independently confirmed in code the outer rectification in method_of_planes_gamma (ff/gamma_estimator.py:111 returns mean(|per-plane sum|); I measured all-T=+1 and all-T=-1 both giving 0.7265), R as a caller constant (ff/gamma_estimator.py:71; scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:306), the one-ended Lagrange reconstruction (ac/cell/assembled_cortical_stress.py:66-71), the bond-vs-turgor sign inconsistency in ff/ff_virial_stress.py (I ran it: a +5 pN tensile bond returns pressure = +0.8333 Pa, turgor dP=40 returns +40, and combining them SUMS to +40.8333), raw max|F| named "residual" (ac/cell/driver.py:170-176, :834; scripts/ac_residual_by_block.py:31 counts "#nodes>0.21 gate" on raw |F|), the vacuous `else True` guard against a committed trace of [113,184,238,266,287,301] (scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:571-573), gamma_apparent = 0.5*dP*R_eq (ff/network_warp.py:1289/1793) frozen at 0.1502 while F_plate moved 37x (FF_STAGE6W:63-65), the ECM-side-only balance gate (ac/engine/ledger.py:265-281 documents add_cell_traction as the force scattered ONTO the ECM; zero non-test callers), no moment channel (grep "moment" in ledger.py = 0 hits against FOUR promising docstrings at ecm_world.py:205/272/293/346), tol_sq_d = None in every slice, and no pinned-vs-clutch disjointness guard anywhere. The GATE_A threshold arithmetic reproduces exactly (0.21067 pN; x23170 in float32; linear in ell; 2.07 pN thermal floor) and gamma_spur = N|PF|/(8*pi*R) is right (367/551/1654/8978). BUT the two most consequential quantitative claims are wrong in OPPOSITE directions, one headline number the audit rated SOUND and propagated as fact is the worst artifact in the family, and the already-written canonical replacement was missed. Usable only after the corrections below; three of the eleven PI questions rest on numbers that do not survive measurement.
false_alarms: RECTIFICATION FLOOR OVERSTATED ~12x, AND THE 'SCATTER IS RECORDED NOWHERE' CLAIM IS FALSE. The audit says the rectified zero-tension floor 'is of the SAME ORDER as the reported observable' and that 'the per-element scatter needed to evaluate it is recorded nowhere'. Both fail. The scatter IS on disk in the very artifact cited for 3.7043: outputs/ac/cell_assembled/gate_b_dynamic_v2.npz carries cmp_cortex_axial_tension (written at scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:352-355). I extracted the 141,372 EXACT end-segment values: mean|T| = 0.0310 pN, sd = 0.2205, median 0.0043, max 6.69. Feeding those actual magnitudes with randomised signs through the real estimator on the real 424,116-segment geometry (crossing fraction 0.0218 = 9,246 per plane; my analytic estimate 0.0212 agrees) gives a null floor of 0.3005 +- 0.0287 pN/um = 8.1% of 3.7043, signal/floor = 12.3. The audit's 1.32 pN/um is correct only as a per-1-pN normalisation (rescaling my measurement gives 1.35); the error is asserting an unknown or 1 pN scatter when the measured RMS is 0.223 pN and is committed. Sign-blindness and the non-zero floor are REAL defects; 'same order as the observable' must be withdrawn.

OBLATE '32% SWING' NOT REPRODUCIBLE - THE SIGN FLIPS WITH THE CONSTRUCTION. The audit offers gamma = 1.4552/1.2699/0.9953 at aspect 1.0/1.5/2.0 (-31.6%) as measured evidence. I ran three defensible oblate remaps at fixed per-element tension with R held at 7.5 on the same estimator: (A) pure z-flatten, element length preserved: 1.7469 -> 1.8997 -> 1.9173, gamma INCREASES 9.7%; (B) volume-preserving (x,y * sqrt(a), z / a): 1.7469 -> 1.5757 -> 1.3346, -23.6%; (C) linear map on endpoints: 1.7469 -> 1.7201 -> 1.6728, -4.2%. Magnitude ranges 5x and the SIGN reverses on an unstated modelling choice, so 'in the direction that UNDERSTATES tension as the cell spreads' holds for only one of three. The structural point (R is an argument, the true cut length is not 2*pi*R on a spread cell) is real and important; the 32% number must go, and the proposed 'require gamma invariant under flattening' acceptance test is ILL-POSED because the answer is set by the remap definition, not by the instrument.

INTERIOR CONTAMINATION IS PROSPECTIVE, NOT LIVE, AND ITS PREMISE IS BACKWARDS. The '1,473% inflation' reproduces (I get 1,459%) but is presented as current evidence for a PROTOCOL_MISMATCH verdict. Today cell.foff_d is cortex-only: the committed manifest records n_actors = 70,686 for a component labelled 'cortex' with 494,802 nodes = 70,686 * 7, and ac/engine/sf_population.py:168 gives sf_arc its OWN flat pos array. Worse, the justification - 'the moment SF / lamellipodium / filopodium filaments enter the same array (which the ac/engine roadmap requires)' - inverts the ratified architecture: PI 2026-07-22 (CLAUDE.md I0-A) requires each component to own a DISJOINT population coupled only through connectors, precisely so they do NOT share an array. The genuine live risk is narrower: assembled_cortical_stress.py:121 is label-blind over whatever is in foff, so it will silently mismeasure IF the frozen incumbent ever adds a non-cortex family. State it as a required guard, not a measured error.

_anchor_dipole MISLEADING_NAME IS OVERSTATED. ac/weave/stress_fiber.py:299 returns max(|r_hi|,|r_lo|) and the field is named dipole_pN with a docstring calling it 'the larger end's contractile pull' - the units in the name are CORRECT and the description is a force, not a moment. The companion residual = |R_lo + R_hi| (:300) is present and correctly described, so the asymmetry information the audit says is lost is in fact reported beside it. This is loose terminology worth renaming, not a metric measuring something other than its name, and it does not belong in the severity class of the gamma_apparent identity.

'THE STABLE VERDICT LETS THE RAW RESIDUAL DOUBLE' IS INCOMPLETE. driver.py:1204 does contain res_end <= max(2*res_start, res_start+1.0), but the `stable` conjunction at :1195-1206 ALSO requires inner_converged, which ac/cell/inner_mechanics.py:290-296 sets only when max_displacement, max_constraint_error AND max_projected_force*dt_mu are all under tolerance. The doubling clause is additional slack on a raw quantity, not the sole criterion. The naming defect stands; the implied 'a diverging run can be stamped STABLE' does not.
missed_defects: gamma_source IS THE WORST INSTRUMENT IN THE FAMILY, AND THE AUDIT RATED ITS PRODUCER SOUND THEN QUOTED ITS OUTPUT AS FACT TO THE PI. From the committed npz I reconstructed the crossbridge family exactly (con_nmii_cortex_motor_xyz/_load, built at scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:388-390): 7,535 elements of MEAN LENGTH 12.7 nm (median 10.4, max 50) against a 14.8 um cut diameter. Only 2.50 crossbridges cross any diametral plane (min 0, max 11). I reproduce gamma_source = 0.0165 with across-plane sd = 0.0188, i.e. |mean|/sd = 0.88 - BELOW the audit's own proposed detection criterion, statistically indistinguishable from zero. gamma_source is a 2.5-element shot-noise readout. So 'gamma_source is 0.0191, i.e. the actual power stroke is 0.5% of the quoted number' - repeated in the SOUND verdict, in the instrument-3 evidence, and as the FIRST PI question - is a length-sampling artifact: method-of-planes weights each bond by crossing probability, which is proportional to length, so a 12.7 nm crossbridge is ~39x less likely to cross than a 0.5 um segment. It is also the wrong accounting: _measure_gamma passes the FULL _accumulate_all force (scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:292-297) into actin_axial_tension, so the crossbridge reaction is ALREADY inside the actin family - the myosin contribution lives in the 3.70, not the 0.019. The correct test of 'is this myosin-driven' is the missing myosin-off t0 control, never the source/network ratio. RETRACT this claim, do not forward it.

THE CANONICAL REPLACEMENT ALREADY EXISTS, IS ALREADY VALIDATED, AND WAS ALREADY ORDERED PROMOTED - the audit cites only the demotion half of the same document. docs/v2_audit/H7_SURFACE_MANIFOLD_EXPLICIT_CORTEX_2026-06-07.md:119 says 'Promote IK whole-shell virial gamma_ik to PRIMARY ... <0.5% vs corrected MOP, ~12x lower sampling variance'; the audit quotes only :121. gamma_ik = sum(T*L*(1-(rhat.u)^2))/(8*pi*R^2) is implemented at archive/hoomd_legacy/cortex/cortical_tension.py:416 (a read-only PORT SPECIFICATION per CLAUDE.md, i.e. the sanctioned source) and appears NOWHERE in ff/, ac/, dcm/, common/, scripts/ or tests/ - I grepped. It is a SIGNED whole-shell sum with no per-plane abs and no plane sampling, so it fixes the rectification AND sampling-variance defects at once, and its manifold variant (realized triangle area instead of 4*pi*R^2, same doc :123) fixes the R-is-an-input defect. I validated it on the real native element set: gamma_IK = 4.9243 vs MOP mean|g| = 5.0213 on the identical all-positive set (1.9% agreement), and on the randomised-sign null gamma_IK = 0.0054 +- 0.058 against MOP's 0.3005 - a 56x reduction of the null floor at 2% agreement on the signal. The audit's two proposals (signed across-plane mean+sd; geometric per-plane cut length from the live triangulation) are strictly more work and strictly weaker than porting 8 lines a PI/Codex review ratified seven weeks ago.

THE END-BIAS OF actin_axial_tension IS FAR WORSE THAN 32.6%, AND IT IS MEASURABLE ON DISK. The audit's 32.6% is a synthetic 7-node filament with a maximally coherent 0.1398 pN/node residual. I measured the real thing from the committed artifact: per filament (7 nodes) sum|f_ext| - the exact upper bound on the end-to-end disagreement, which equals |sum f_ext| - has median 0.0751 pN, mean 0.1267 pN, while the per-filament mean segment |T| has median 0.0054 pN, mean 0.0320 pN. Ratio bias/tension: MEDIAN 13.6, mean 16.5; even the uncorrelated random-walk estimate sqrt(sum f^2) gives a median ratio of 6.0. At the flagship GATE-B state the equilibrium assumption the reconstruction rests on is violated by roughly an order of magnitude relative to the tension reported, not by a third. This COMPOUNDS with the rectifier: the residual-derived component enters T with a random sign per filament, and the outer abs then converts random-sign tension into positive gamma. The two-ended control is the right fix and should be raised in priority accordingly.

THE ff_virial_stress GRID DEFECT IS WORSE THAN 'IT HALVES', AND TWO CALLER SETS WERE MISSED. I ran cortex_node_stress: doubling node count on the same 1 um physical bond at node_vol = V0/n gives max vm 5.0000 -> 2.2222 (worse than halving, because the virial arm shrinks too), so the Pa field carries two superposed non-invariances. The cited callers are right (scripts/ff_resting_full_compartment.py:50, ff_crawl_on_substrate.py:795 AND :803, ff_s1_sphere.py:113) but it missed scripts/ff_cortex_deform_viewer.py:53 and ff_s2_local_load_viewer.py:58, and - more consequentially - missed that the SAME uniform partition is baked into the RUNTIME at ac/cell/assemble.py:931-932 (node_vol[:n_actin] = cell_vol/n_actin, non-actin nodes get ZERO volume) where it feeds the Biot/FSI coupling, not just a viewer.

THE CLUTCH REACTION IS DEAD CODE, WHICH SHARPENS THE 'ABSENT' VERDICT. ac/solid/adhesion_clutch.py:78 allocates _ecm_force_d, :85 zeroes it every accumulate, and it is never read anywhere - the docstring at :66-68 says outright 'with a rigid substrate that reaction is discarded'. So the two-sided Newton reaction the architecture rests on is computed and thrown away each step. There is therefore no adjointness evidence for the ONE force law the PI's adherent-collagen baseline depends on, and the audit's own negative control (sum(clutch force on cell) + sum(clutch force on ECM) = 0) cannot be instrumented until that array is retained.

FOUR docstrings promise a moment channel, not three (ecm_world.py:205, :272, :293, :346). And the audit missed that ac/cell/resting_balance_oracle.py:274 passes np.zeros_like(cor) as node_force, so both Newton-closure diagnostics that measure_cortical_stress retains 'for regression' (net_force_vector_pn, summed_inward_radial_force_pn) are identically ZERO in the one place the audit holds up as the SOUND pattern. The Laplace-as-target structure there is sound; its closure diagnostics are vacuous by construction and must not be cited as evidence that closure is checked.
arithmetic_corrections: gamma_spur = N*|PF|/(8*pi*R) checks out exactly (494802*0.1398/188.50 = 367.0; 0.21 -> 551.2; 0.63 -> 1653.7; 3.42 -> 8977), as do gamma_target = 40 pN/um^2 * 7.5 um / 2 = 150 pN/um and Pi_0*pi*R^2 = 7068.6 pN. But it is a WORST CASE assuming the entire per-node max is coherent AND radial at all 494,802 nodes. The audit labels it worst-case in the evidence field then drops the qualifier in the PI question ('the PASSING gate leaves headroom for ~100x the flagship observable'). At the committed state the per-node composed |F| distribution is mean 0.0181, median 0.0098, p99 0.130, max 6.69 pN (cmp_cortex_fmag), so the coherent fraction is nowhere near 1 and the realistic bound is orders below 367. 'S is the only quantity that bounds the error' survives; the 100x headline does not.

GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION verified independently and correct: 1.4901161193847656e-08 * 0.4999048934 = 7.449163398500275e-09 (bit-matches the committed inner_tolerance_um), / 3.535943748517097e-08 = 0.210670 pN; sqrt(eps32)/sqrt(eps64) = 23,170 and 0.21067*23170 = 4881.5 ~ 4882; linear-in-ell reproduces 0.0843 at 0.2 um and 0.0316 at 0.075 um (ratios 2.49 and 6.64); steric-off 0.21067/0.0611 = 3.45; sqrt(kBT*k_xb) = sqrt(4.280012e-3*1000) = 2.069 pN, 1.5/2.069 = 0.725, 2.069/0.21 = 9.86; 0.63/0.21067 = 2.99 and 0.63/2.069 = 0.304. One inherited nit: the doc says the frozen literal is within 0.34% of 0.21067; the true figure is 0.318%.

MOP null floor: the 1.32 pN/um per 1 pN of scatter is right (rescaling my measured 0.3005 at RMS 0.223 pN gives 1.35). The 2.14 pN/um for 1,413,720 crosslinks I could NOT verify - the count is confirmed (ac/cell/assemble.py:423, n_xl = round(n_filaments*density_per_fil) = 70,686*20 = 1,413,720) but the npz carries no crosslink geometry, so the crossing fraction and hence the floor are unestablished. Naive sqrt(1.41e6/4.24e5) = 1.82 scaling would give ~2.4, so 2.14 implies a slightly shorter mean element; plausible, not established. Do not quote it.

The gamma split is exactly additive in the committed artifact (3.7043 + 0.0191 = 3.7234 = gamma_total), which the audit does not note. Because each family is separately RECTIFIED before summing, that additivity is a coincidence of all families being sign-coherent per plane at this state, not a property of the estimator - under a partially compressive cortex gamma_total would NOT equal the sum, and any future consistency check written on that identity would be silently wrong.

Cost of every proposed magnitude-free instrument, measured on this Mac (the audit gives no cost numbers at all): the full 64-plane MOP over all 424,116 native segments runs in 0.27 s of host NumPy, so the sign-reversal null control and the signed-mean/sd variant are effectively free; actin_axial_tension's pure-Python double loop over 70,686 fibers x 6 segments takes 1.15 s, so the two-ended reconstruction costs ~1.2 s per measurement. Both are out-of-hot-loop post-processing (I0-A compliant). S = sum(PF.rhat) and the moment/adjointness reductions are single device reductions over <=551,434 nodes - microseconds.
feasibility_corrections: ATTACK AXIS 5 IS NOT APPLICABLE AS WRITTEN: the audit under review contains NO 'two design tracks' and NO tensor-network proposal - it is a 17-instrument inventory plus 12 oracles and 12 missing instruments, so there is nothing whose verdict turns on whether mechanical load couples binding states globally. For the record the coupling IS global on the cortex lane: scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:292 calls the whole-cell _accumulate_all and every bound head's load is read from the converged GLOBAL geometry via compute_head_loads_segment_split_r0bind_kernel (ac/engine/cortex_motor_slice.py:520-525), so any future factorised-state scheme would face an all-to-all load coupling. Nothing in this audit rests on it.

EVERYTHING PROPOSED FITS ONE A5000 16GB, with two restatements. (1) 'GRID REFINEMENT OF THE STRESS FIELD: double node count at fixed physical state' is feasible (2.9M nodes at 75 nm already ran on the A5000) but it moves the CONVERGENCE GATE at the same time, because 0.21 is proportional to ell (GATE_A_THRESHOLD consequence 3) - so the refinement oracle cannot be run against the frozen literal without either tightening the gate or invalidating the comparison. The audit does not mention this coupling.

(2) 'RIGID-ROD LIMIT CROSS-CALIBRATION: sweep k_axial upward' is feasible only on the implicit path. The committed run records lambda_sf = 3.684e6 pN/um at k_axial = 1000 (outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/sf_motor_native_gate.json, cfl block) and the explicit step is C_target/lambda_max, so three decades of k_axial means ~1000x more inner iterations. At 360 SF nodes that is nothing; at native SF population it requires ac/engine/sf_implicit.py, which exists but has no native evidence in the engine audit. Feasible, with a dependency the audit omits.

THE OBLATE-INVARIANCE ORACLE IS NOT EXECUTABLE AS AN ACCEPTANCE TEST. Its answer (+9.7% / -23.6% / -4.2% across three defensible remaps) is set by an unstated choice of how to deform the shell, so 'require gamma invariant' has no well-defined pass criterion. Replace it with the shape-agnostic manifold-area normalisation (H7 doc :123), which needs no synthetic deformation at all - the realized triangulation area is already on device.

THE MOP-VERSUS-LAPLACE CALIBRATION IS CIRCULAR IN PRACTICE EVEN THOUGH THE RATIO IS FORMALLY MAGNITUDE-FREE. The audit is right that gamma_MOP/(Pi_0*R/2) is Pi_0-independent to leading order (the hoop tension of a pressurised shell at equilibrium is Pi_0*R/2 regardless of stiffness), but it requires the shell to BE at equilibrium - and non-convergence of exactly that state is the open blocker. The oracle cannot run until the thing it is meant to certify is already solved. Rank it after S, not beside it.
hard_rule_problems: THE PROPOSED REPLACEMENT GATE REQUIRES AN UNSOURCED MAGNITUDE, WHICH THE PI HAS EXPLICITLY RULED OUT AS A GATE RIGHT NOW. 'gamma_spur/gamma_target <= f' with gamma_target = Pi_0*R/2 depends on Pi_0 = 40 Pa, which ac/engine/forces_manifest.py:377-384 classifies verbatim as CONVENIENCE - 'the MAGNITUDE is NOT sourced for MCF7' - quoting AC_DECISION_CARDS section 77, '40 Pa stays a HeLa diagnostic proxy only'. The audit's defence, 'Pi_0-invariant in relative form', is unsupported: gamma_spur = S/(8*pi*R) is a property of the SOLVER residual and no argument is offered that S scales with Pi_0. Unless that proportionality is demonstrated the proposal is a magnitude gate wearing a ratio's clothing, and the unsourced tolerance f is a second unsourced constant on top.

'CANONICAL REPLACEMENT' FOR max|PF| < 0.21 IS AMBIGUOUS BETWEEN ADDITIVE AND SUBSTITUTIVE, AND THE SUBSTITUTIVE READING IS GATE-LOOSENING. If S/gamma_target replaces the max|PF| predicate, a state with a large but incoherent residual passes - S can be near zero while max|PF| is 3.42 pN. That is a contract change requiring PI sign-off under CLAUDE.md 'no gate-loosening'. The source derivation document is scrupulous about exactly this distinction (it refuses the thermal floor as a pass criterion because it is looser than 0.21 and 'adopting it as a pass would be gate-loosening'); the audit writes 'canonical_replacement' and relegates 'record max|PF| alongside' to a trailing clause. Restate as ADDITIVE or route as an explicit contract-change proposal.

'REQUIRE |mean|/sd >> 1' IS NOT A RATIFIABLE THRESHOLD AND CONFOUNDS NOISE WITH PHYSICS. '>> 1' names no number. Worse, the 64 Fibonacci planes are deterministic and share one centre, so the across-plane sd is not a sampling error of the mean - on an anisotropic cortex it is largely PHYSICAL anisotropy. On the PI's own baseline (adherent, spread on 2D collagen) anisotropy is expected, so an |mean|/sd criterion would reject genuinely tensed spread cells. The defensible null is the sign-randomisation control the audit also proposes (I measured null 0.124 vs signal 10.52 on real data) or, better, signed gamma_IK whose null I measured at 0.0054 +- 0.058. Drop |mean|/sd as a gate; keep it as a reported diagnostic.

EVERY PROPOSED ENFORCEMENT IS INTENTION-BASED EXCEPT TWO, IN A PROJECT WITH SIX RECORDED DISCIPLINE FAILURES AND SEVEN GUARDS THAT RETURNED CONFIRMED 0/7 TODAY. Mechanical: the build-time 'pinned_mask AND clutch_mask = empty' assertion, and replacing `else True` with a raise. Everything else is a naming convention or a reporting habit - 'rename to residual_raw_*', 'report both numbers in every record', 'mark provenance = IDENTITY_NOT_MEASUREMENT so a downstream summary cannot silently promote it', 'assert any artifact carrying gamma_passive also carries the turgor'. Note the precedent that kills this class: ac/engine/surface_body.py:349-353 ALREADY raises on membrane/cortex aliasing and the native lane bypasses it simply by never constructing the facade. A raise no production path reaches is not enforcement. Each item needs a named executing call site on a production path or a collected test that fails the build.

'A tension/traction reading protocol keyed to convergence: no magnitude may be emitted unless the state passed its own residual gate' is the single most valuable proposal in the audit and carries NO enforcement mechanism at all ('it should be a shared harness rule, not one script's discipline') - exactly the class of rule this project has failed six times. It must be a function that raises (e.g. measure_cortical_stress refusing to return a gamma without a convergence certificate), not a rule. Likewise the proposed vacuous-guard sweep ('for every boolean in every verdict dict, assert the predicate was exercised') is only enforceable as a collected test over the verdict constructors; proposed as a one-time audit pass it decays the moment someone adds a verdict key.

result.summary: Substantially correct and unusually well-evidenced: I independently reproduced ~15 of its findings byte-for-byte, including both of ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py's negative controls to the exact spread values it quoted (1.136e-16 / 1.317e-16), all four kb_coverage fingerprint escapes empirically, the exact kb-check census (30/1/29/7), the ast.get_source_segment comment bypass, the RED suite, and the full route-(c) arithmetic by differentiation. The 13 TAUTOLOGICAL verdicts on assemble_balance, accepted_d=ones, the 11 zero-exit drivers, rest_force_free/r0, test_wiring substrings, the docstring-matching projector assertion, the pi0 alias "dimensional gate", assert_disjoint_populations, the hard-coded True verdict fields, tension_zero_while_no_head_is_bound, the sf_arc CFL clamp, route_c_scales_linearly_in_seg, and the results fingerprint all hold. But it fails in five ways that matter for a re-founding deliverable. (1) It found the r0=build-geometry identity and then did not follow it into the gate it actually breaks: the headline emergence criterion in BOTH the "FIRST composed native cell" gate and the ECM gate is `post > 10*max(rest,1e-12)`, which because rest is identically ~0 degenerates to `post > 1e-11 pN` — float noise passes, and that predicate is what gates the exit code. (2) It missed that GlobalCellLedger.reset() exists and is never called by the transaction, so every ledger channel is cumulative across steps and its own proposed fix would accumulate too. (3) The single instrument it rated SOUND and held up as "the template" escapes on a one-line lowercase-variable edit and does not cover ffn_sim/ac/ at all, where 42 device="cpu" sites live including a Warp CPU launch in the production package. (4) One false alarm (monomer_flux mass_d is a correct disjoint partition of A_total, not a meaningless sum) plus a flagship recommendation whose stated rationale is wrong in both directions (reciprocity is satisfied by any +/-f pair regardless of allocation, the native GATE-B endpoints alias ONE global array, and reciprocity already runs green on the Mac in 8 places). (5) Two proposals have hard-rule problems — an unflagged gate-loosening on the mesh-sensitivity threshold, and a "sourced resting strain" requirement listed under magnitude-free oracles — and NOTHING it proposes is mechanically enforced, in an audit whose own premise is that intention-based discipline has failed six times.
false_alarms: FALSE ALARM — monomer_flux mass_d 'meaningless sum'. The audit claims monomer_flux.py:290-293 and :425-427 'push a_total_d, field_pool_d AND consumer_bound_d into the SAME ledger.mass_d scalar, so the mass channel is a meaningless sum'. Read the code: monomer_flux.py:243 documents a_total_d as the scratch the FIELD-CONTENT reduce writes (monomer_field_content_reduce_kernel over the masked grid, :283-289), field_pool_d as the separate free-monomer reservoir (:241), and consumer_bound_d as each consumer's bound pool (:313). These are three DISJOINT partitions of total actin; summing them is exactly A_total, as the inline comment at :292-293 ('field content ... + free-monomer pool (bound pools added by the connectors)') and the docstring at :274-277 ('together the mass channel accumulates A_total for the global conservation gate') both state. The sum is correct. The real defects are different: nothing reads mass_d, and it is never zeroed between steps (see missed defects).

WRONG RATIONALE on the flagship recommendation — 'Connector reciprocity ... cannot be satisfied by construction when the two endpoint arrays are separate allocations.' This is wrong twice.
